guidance.chaining: set with dryRun:true previews the would-reap count; config:list-overrides shows the active override.

tools.name: coord:thread
tools.description: Reconstruct a coord thread rooted at `root_msg_id` — every entry connected via the `related_msg_id` chain, sorted by ts ascending.

guidance.when: You want the full conversation around a coord message (replies, acks, resolutions).
guidance.notWhen: For a fresh inbox sweep — use coord:inbox.

tools.name: coord:thread-post
tools.description: Post a message to a coordination thread by conversation_id (e.g. a spawned voter casting its structured ```vote``` block, or the advocate posting its ```advocate``` objection).

guidance.when: You were spawned into a vote/deliberation with a CONVERSATION_ID and need to cast your structured vote or objection into that thread.
guidance.notWhen: Replying in an open conversation you joined — use conversations:post. A direct message to an agent — coord:send.

tools.name: coord:vote
tools.description: Run a diverse-lens, confidence-weighted vote on a decision and get back a resolution (decisive) or a curated escalation (split). One voter per lens + an advocate arguing against the lead.

guidance.when: You face a genuinely uncertain, consequential choice between named options and want a diverse, anti-correlated read before committing — instead of deciding alone or escalating raw.
guidance.notWhen: A trivial or reversible choice — just decide. A pure factual lookup — use search/docs. To ask the human directly, use coord:ask-owner / coord:escalate.

tools.name: coord:wake-mode
tools.description: Read or set an agent's wake mode — auto (wakes fire immediately) or manual (wakes are staged for the owner to release/edit/skip). Omit `mode` to read; omit `agent` to read/set the global default. The pause/edit gate (hive-agent-tabs D-005).

guidance.when: Switching an agent (or the default) between auto and manual wake delivery — e.g. pausing a bee's auto-injected turns to review them first, or switching back.
guidance.notWhen: Reading who's online or what an agent is doing — that's coord:presence / fleet:assignments. Reviewing the staged wakes themselves — that's coord:wake-queue.

tools.name: coord:wake-queue
tools.description: Review a manual-mode agent's STAGED wakes: list them, release one (deliver as-is or edited as the agent's next turn), skip one (discard), or drain the whole queue — release_all delivers ONE coalesced wake for everything staged; skip_all discards everything. The pause/edit gate's review surface (hive-agent-tabs D-005 / P-009).

guidance.when: Reviewing a manual-mode agent's staged wakes from its pane — releasing the ones to deliver (optionally edited) and skipping the rest. Draining a backlog → release_all (one consolidated turn) or skip_all, never N individual releases.
guidance.notWhen: An auto-mode agent — its wakes fire immediately, nothing is staged. Changing the mode itself — that's coord:wake-mode.

tools.name: coord:watermark
tools.description: Read a coordination watermark — last-read ISO timestamps for messages / escalations / plan-events + the notify msg_ids surfaced. DEFAULT: your own. Pass `agent` to read a PEER's: their `read_through_ts` (messages_shown_ts) is a READ-RECEIPT — ≥ your message's ts ⇒ they've SEEN it (ping them, don't re-route); behind ⇒ not yet seen (wait, or wake if idle). With `agent`+`sent_ts` you get a direct `seen` boolean.

guidance.when: Turn start — the OMP coordination extension calls this to scope the inbox to new entries. To check if a PEER has seen a message you sent (READ-RECEIPT, EI-2042): coord:watermark { agent: <their ownerId from coord:presence>, sent_ts: <your message ts> } → seen:true means it was injected into their context.
guidance.notWhen: Routine reads — coord:inbox without a watermark returns the full inbox.

tools.name: coord:watermark-set
tools.description: Advance your coordination watermark. Call at TURN END with the newest ISO timestamp you have seen on each surface. Partial update — omitted fields keep their current value. `subscriptions_fired` is replaced wholesale when supplied.

guidance.when: Turn end — the OMP coordination extension records how far you read this turn.
guidance.notWhen: Mid-turn — advancing early would hide notifications that arrive before the turn finishes.

tools.name: coord:whoami
tools.description: Return the coordination identity the server resolved for you: ownerId (the stable per-agent id), ownerLabel, source, workspaceId, userId, and your inbox_wake_key (the key a coord:send {wake:true} fires + the one coord:await-inbox watches). A debug aid for confirming how the coordination layer sees this agent.

guidance.when: Debugging identity — "what ownerId am I?" before relying on lock or message behaviour.
guidance.notWhen: Routine work — identity is resolved automatically by every coord:* and locks:* call.

tools.name: cross_harness:docs_get
tools.description: Fetch documentation pages from any registered harness by explicit slug. Batch up to 10; pass `heading` (single-slug only) for a section slice. Per-slug error envelope.

guidance.when: You have slugs from cross_harness:docs_outline and need the page contents from a specific harness (named by harnessSlug arg).
guidance.notWhen: You are inside a harness — use docs:get, which auto-targets your harness.
guidance.chaining: cross_harness:docs_outline { harnessSlug } → cross_harness:docs_get { harnessSlug, slugs } → optionally re-fetch with { harnessSlug, slugs: [picked], heading } for surgical reads.

tools.name: cross_harness:docs_outline
tools.description: Outline of any registered harness's documentation by explicit slug. For engineers operating outside a harness context who need to query a specific harness's docs. Per-run cached.

guidance.when: You are not inside a harness context (no spawn URL harness slug) but need a specific harness's documentation. Pass harnessSlug explicitly.
guidance.notWhen: You are already inside a harness (ctx.harnessSlug is set) — use docs:outline instead, which auto-targets your harness.
guidance.chaining: cross_harness:docs_outline { harnessSlug } → cross_harness:docs_get { harnessSlug, slugs }.

tools.name: cross_harness:docs_search
tools.description: Keyword search across any registered harness's documentation by explicit slug. Returns ranked hits (slug, title, description, excerpt). For out-of-harness engineers who need to find content in a specific harness without scanning its outline by hand.

guidance.when: You have specific terminology in mind and want to find which page in a specific harness covers it. Faster than scanning cross_harness:docs_outline by hand when the section name is non-obvious.
guidance.notWhen: You are inside a harness — use docs:search, which auto-targets your harness. You do not know which harness to query — list with `harness:list` or `cross_harness:docs_outline` per slug first.
guidance.chaining: cross_harness:docs_search { harnessSlug, query } → cross_harness:docs_get { harnessSlug, slugs: [top-hit] }.

tools.name: cross_harness:inbox
tools.description: Read messages addressed to a harness (status pending|all|other; optional role filter).

guidance.when: You need to see messages addressed TO a specific harness across senders. The cross-harness analog of `messages:inbox`.
guidance.notWhen: For YOUR (the calling principal's) inbox, use `messages:inbox`. For sent items, use `cross_harness:outbox`.

tools.name: cross_harness:outbox
tools.description: Read messages a harness sent (cross-schema scan by from_slug).

guidance.when: You need to see what a specific harness sent — across recipients. Cross-harness analog of `messages:outbox`.
guidance.notWhen: For YOUR outbox, use `messages:outbox`. For incoming, use `cross_harness:inbox`.

tools.name: cross_harness:plans_get
tools.description: Fetch the full parsed structure of one plan in any harness by explicit slug: frontmatter, ## Now, items with effectiveStatus, decisions. Read-only.

guidance.when: You have a slug + harness from cross_harness:plans_list (or know both directly) and need the plan contents.
guidance.notWhen: You are inside the target harness (ctx.harnessSlug is set) — use plans:get, which auto-targets your harness.
guidance.chaining: cross_harness:plans_list → cross_harness:plans_get { harnessSlug, slug }.

tools.name: cross_harness:plans_list
tools.description: List plans of any registered harness by explicit slug. For agents operating outside a single harness context who need to query another harness's plans. Read-only — writes go through ambient plans:*.

guidance.when: You are not inside a harness context (or want to inspect a different harness from outside) and need a directory of that harness's plans. Pass harnessSlug explicitly.
guidance.notWhen: You are already in the target harness (ctx.harnessSlug is set) — use plans:list, which auto-targets your harness.
guidance.chaining: cross_harness:plans_list { harnessSlug } → cross_harness:plans_get { harnessSlug, slug }.

tools.name: cross_harness:plans_search
tools.description: Keyword search across plans of any registered harness by explicit slug. Scopes: slug, title, now, items, decisions, prose (a slug fragment finds the plan it names). Read-only.

guidance.when: You're looking for prior work in another harness and don't have a slug. Pass harnessSlug + query.
guidance.notWhen: You are inside the target harness — use plans:search, which auto-targets your harness.
guidance.chaining: cross_harness:plans_search { harnessSlug, query } → cross_harness:plans_get { harnessSlug, slug } on the top hit.

tools.name: cross_harness:recent_activity
tools.description: Workspace-wide recent activity feed (ts, harness_slug, action, subject, actor) from harness_shared.audit_log.

guidance.when: User asks "what's been happening across all my harnesses?", "any cross-harness activity?". The workspace-level activity feed.
guidance.notWhen: For ONE harness's activity, use `harness:status`. For your own audit trail, use `audit:list`.

tools.name: cross_harness:supervisor_notes
tools.description: Read supervisor notes for a harness (id, body, source, created_at).

guidance.when: You need the supervisor's annotations on a harness — context the supervisor logged that's not in audit_log.
guidance.notWhen: For escalation flags + raw notes from the on-disk files, use `harness:escalation`. supervisor_notes is the PG-backed view.

tools.name: curation:change-feed
tools.description: The Change Feed — a derived projection over completion records (work-item completions, gym proposals, plan runs). Summaries reference the originals (rationale:feed pattern). One calm rollup per tick, drill-down on demand. Filter by harness or user-requested work.

guidance.when: You want to see recent changes across the fleet (what work finished, what proposals landed) without a replicated log. Pass userRequestedOnly to see only user-facing changes; harness to scope to one project.
guidance.notWhen: For the raw fleet signals use curation:feed. For historical audit of all changes use the underlying work-items / coord-event-log directly.

tools.name: curation:feed
tools.description: Pull the curator-operator's salience-ranked fleet signals (escalations / blockers / decisions-needed / completions / progress) — the READ projection of the salience policy for a dashboard. A pure read of the CURRENT salient state (no loop, no chat-surface, no flag); the pui Fleet 'curated' view consumes this.

guidance.when: You want the curator's view of what matters across the fleet right now — the salience-ranked signals (escalations, blockers, decisions owed, recent completions) for a dashboard or status read. Pass surfaceOnly to get just the always-surface signals; harness to scope to one project.
guidance.notWhen: For the raw tool-call firehose use activity:recent / the activity stream. To make the operator SURFACE a message into the chat, that's the curation loop (flag-gated), not this read.

tools.name: curation:state-of-hive
tools.description: The "state of the Hive" corpus digest — a deterministic rollup of cross-corpus meta-patterns (recurring friction, time/token sinks, chronic deferrals, capability gaps) over the change feed + completions + reverts. The Scout loop's grounded ideation substrate; each pattern references the originals (drill in via work_items:get / plans:get / curation:change-feed).

guidance.when: You want the introspective "what are the Hive's standing meta-patterns" rollup — the recurring friction, where time/tokens go, what keeps being deferred, and the absent capabilities — as the grounded substrate for generative ideation (the Scout loop) or a state-of-the-Hive review. Each pattern carries refs back to the originals.
guidance.notWhen: For the raw stream of recent completions use curation:change-feed. For salience-ranked live fleet signals (escalations/blockers) use curation:feed. For the captured-improvement triage queue (auto vs human lanes) use improvements:digest.
guidance.chaining: curation:state-of-hive → drill into a pattern via its refs (work_items:get on wi:<id>, plans:get on plan:<slug>, curation:change-feed) → feed the digest to the Scout ideators.

tools.name: db:check_drift
tools.description: Report DB migration drift — sql/*.sql files not yet applied (per harness_shared.schema_migrations). Detection only. `missing` = added since the last operator boot; restart the operator (boot auto-applies) or use db:migrate. `extra` = applied but file gone (investigate).

guidance.when: After adding a migration, or when a runtime "missing column/relation" error suggests the live DB lags the sql/ dir.
guidance.notWhen: Applying a migration — that is the boot auto-apply (restart) or db:migrate for a one-off.
guidance.chaining: missing non-empty → restart the operator (or db:migrate the file under exclusive(db-schema)).

tools.name: db:migrate
tools.description: Apply a SQL migration file, coordinated. DRY RUN unless confirm:true. With confirm, acquires exclusive(db-schema) and drains schema-dependent work (wait:{max_drain_sec}) before running psql -f <file>, then releases. The real apply also requires PAPERCUSP_ALLOW_DB_MIGRATE=1. Prefer this over a raw psql -f.

guidance.when: Applying a migration / destructive DDL that could disrupt in-flight queries. Dry-run to see holders; confirm to drain + apply.
guidance.notWhen: Read-only SQL needs no lock. Never apply migrations casually on a shared box.
guidance.chaining: db:migrate { file } (dry) → review → db:migrate { file, confirm: true }.

tools.name: db:migrate-policy
tools.description: Read or set the deploy-migration connection policy: lockTimeoutMs (the DDL lock_timeout the deploy migrator uses — default 15000, the value behind two deploy outages) and statementTimeoutMs (optional; null to unset). set is audited + one-call-revertible via the control harness; migrate.ts reads it fail-safe (defaults on any read error).

guidance.when: Before a deploy whose migration legitimately needs longer to acquire its lock — raise lockTimeoutMs for that window — or to add a statement_timeout, without editing migrate.ts and redeploying through the path you are tuning.
guidance.notWhen: For the BOOT-time migration lock_timeout (it runs before PG config is readable — stays an env/code default per the plan keep-hardcoded list). To see all live overrides, config:list-overrides.
guidance.chaining: config:list-overrides shows the active override; config:reset-overrides reverts it to the 15000 default.

tools.name: db:next-migration
tools.description: Atomically reserve the next migration number for a libs/papercusp/libs/db/sql/<NNN>-*.sql file. Hands out GREATEST(max-on-disk across the serving + canonical staging trees, max-reserved, max-applied)+1 under a pg advisory lock so two agents racing `ls | tail` never collide. Returns the number + a suggested filename/path; write the file there and it auto-applies on the next operator restart (A1 boot-apply).

guidance.when: BEFORE creating a new SQL migration file — reserve the number first instead of `ls | tail`, so a concurrent agent cannot pick the same NNN.
guidance.notWhen: Applying a migration (that is the boot auto-apply / db:migrate) or checking drift (db:check_drift).
guidance.chaining: db:next-migration { name } → write the returned path → restart the operator (boot auto-applies) or db:migrate.

tools.name: db:txn-timeouts
tools.description: Read/set/reset the per-workspace transaction timeouts (lockTimeoutMs / statementTimeoutMs) applied by inWorkspaceTxn, merged over the baked 5s/5s defaults. Mid-incident, raise lockTimeoutMs to ride out same-workspace contention or statementTimeoutMs to let a slow mutation finish — no deploy. Empty override / kill-switch off (papercusp-txn-timeouts-config) = byte-identical 5s/5s. set/reset audited + one-call-revertible.

guidance.when: State-mutating tools are failing with workspace_contended (PG lock_timeout 55P03 / statement_timeout 57014) under same-workspace contention, and you need to widen the window for the incident — raise lockTimeoutMs and/or statementTimeoutMs. get to inspect the effective timeouts + override.
guidance.notWhen: Not for the DEPLOY-migration lock_timeout (db:migrate-policy), nor for the BOOT migration timeout (env/code). This only sizes the per-workspace inWorkspaceTxn lock_timeout/statement_timeout.
guidance.chaining: config:list-overrides shows the active txn-timeouts override; config:reset-overrides reverts it. The kill-switch papercusp-txn-timeouts-config (default ON) forces the baked 5s/5s defaults when OFF.

tools.name: decision_ledger:list
tools.description: The Queen's decision ledger newest-first: governed actions (layer=action — what ran, with posture auto/gated/rejected) and the Queen's per-item dispositions (layer=disposition — act/defer/reject/route-to-research/no-op + why). Filter by layer/category/posture/disposition/time. Each row carries the autonomy axes (category, risk_tier, reversibility, authority) + provenance links. Read-only.

guidance.when: Auditing what the Queen has decided / what the fleet has done: 'what auto-decisions happened?', 'show the gated actions in spend-budget', 'what did she defer?'. Pair with autonomy:policy_get to see why a category gates.
guidance.notWhen: A roll-up of counts by posture/category — decision_ledger:summary. Prompt/rule mutations specifically — change_ledger:list. The live policy ceilings — autonomy:policy_get.
guidance.chaining: decision_ledger:summary (the shape) → decision_ledger:list { layer, category, posture } for the rows → a row.links (runId/spawnId/itemRef) to drill to the transcript / item.

tools.name: decision_ledger:summary
tools.description: Roll-up of the Queen decision ledger: total + counts by layer (action/disposition), posture (auto/proposed/gated/rejected), category, and disposition verb, over a time window. The cheap shape-read before decision_ledger:list. Read-only.

guidance.when: Getting oriented: 'how much is the Queen auto-deciding vs gating?', 'which categories see the most gated actions?', 'what's the disposition mix this week?'. Then decision_ledger:list for the rows.
guidance.notWhen: You want the actual rows — decision_ledger:list. Live ceilings — autonomy:policy_get.
guidance.chaining: decision_ledger:summary → decision_ledger:list { the posture/category that stands out }.

tools.name: deploy:harness
tools.description: Deploy a harness's execution plane to its configured cloud frame: provision the machine, bootstrap the runtime (own loop + own embedded-pg), join it as a federated peer. The harness must have been created with a non-local `deployment` (e.g. {target:'latitude'}). Set `deployment.desktop` (true | {displays,geometry}) for a GUI-capable frame: one Xvfb display per agent slot, agents get a leased DISPLAY. Returns {ok, frame}.

guidance.when: Moving a cloud-configured harness onto a real frame so its agents run remotely (distinct IP, own Claude sub) while state federates to the local view.
guidance.notWhen: A local harness (no cloud deployment). Tearing one down — deploy:teardown. Checking status — deploy:status.
guidance.chaining: harness:create { …, deployment:{target:"latitude", desktop:true, …} } → deploy:harness { slug } → deploy:status / deploy:teardown.

tools.name: deploy:hive
tools.description: Deploy a Hive (grouping of harnesses) to a Swarm (cloud fleet): place the Queen (local|dedicated|colocated) and deploy each member harness's execution to a frame. Per-member failures are reported, not fatal. Returns {ok, result}.

guidance.when: Running a whole group of harnesses in the cloud — full-auto laptop-optional, or just to scale out execution across frames.
guidance.notWhen: A single harness — deploy:harness. Tearing one down — deploy:teardown_hive.
guidance.chaining: deploy:hive { hiveId, members, swarm } → deploy:teardown_hive when done.

tools.name: deploy:status
tools.description: Report a harness's deployment: its `deployment` config + the live frame handle (id/host/region) if deployed. Returns {ok, deployment, frame|null}.

guidance.when: Checking where a harness runs (local vs which cloud frame) and the frame's reachable host.

tools.name: deploy:teardown
tools.description: Tear down a harness's cloud frame — DESTROY (not stop) to end billing. No-op if nothing is deployed. Returns {ok, destroyed}.

guidance.when: Done with a cloud harness (or to stop its billing). Teardown destroys the machine so it stops costing money.
guidance.notWhen: Pausing temporarily — there is no stop; destroy + redeploy is the model (frames are cattle).

tools.name: deploy:teardown_hive
tools.description: Tear down a Hive — DESTROY every member execution frame + the Queen control frame (ends all billing). Pass the same hiveId + members + queen placement used to deploy. Returns {ok, destroyed, failed}.

guidance.when: Done with a deployed Hive (or to stop all its billing). Frames are cattle — destroy + redeploy is the model.

tools.name: dev:activity
tools.description: Most-recent tool invocations across selected workspaces (live activity feed).

guidance.when: Diagnostic feed of recent workspace activity — for dashboards and debugging. Lower-detail than `audit:list`.
guidance.notWhen: For agent action audit, use `audit:list`. dev:activity is for the /dev panel, not for analysis.

tools.name: dev:audit
tools.description: Cross-workspace audit_log feed (last N hours).

guidance.when: Dev-panel audit view — filtered + paginated for UI display.
guidance.notWhen: For analysis or LLM consumption, use `audit:list` directly. dev:audit is a UI-shaped projection.

tools.name: dev:build_status
tools.description: Local-host build mtime + bin/prod log tail + dev/prod server reachability.

guidance.when: Read recent build status from the dev panel — pass/fail per harness.
guidance.notWhen: For ONE harness's smoke tests, use harness-specific tools. dev:build_status is the cross-harness dev panel feed.

tools.name: dev:coord_categorize
tools.description: Categorize the coord_event_log `messages` corpus into lifecycle buckets (completion/claim/intent/restart/ack/finding) vs the irreducible contextual residual. The instrument for coord-lifecycle-automation D-006: re-run after each phase; contextualPct + automatedPct are the headline metrics.

guidance.when: Measure coord-lifecycle automation progress — how much free-text coord is predictable lifecycle vs genuinely contextual.
guidance.notWhen: To read your inbox use coord:inbox; this is an aggregate measurement over the whole corpus, not a feed.

tools.name: dev:dogfood_substrate_status
tools.description: Hyperbee substrate diagnostic: booted harnesses, per-row health verdict, workspace summary. The substrate is always active (no flag gate). Mirrors /api/admin/dogfood-substrate-health.

guidance.when: Investigating substrate boot state, claim error rates, or workspace-level dogfood health. The substrate always boots, so run this any time after the operator has started.
guidance.notWhen: For per-harness Insights or feature-level data, use the harness:* tools. This is the dogfood substrate layer specifically.
guidance.chaining: Pair with reading the agent-insights/substrate-flag-flip-runbook page for what to do if verdicts come back degraded/unhealthy.

tools.name: dev:event_emitter
tools.description: Replay-buffer probe — emits N tick events with serial ids. Dev-only.

tools.name: dev:harnesses
tools.description: List harnesses across selected workspaces with health verdict for each.

guidance.when: Dev-panel harness enumeration with diagnostic columns (active connections, recent errors).
guidance.notWhen: For ordinary list, use `harness:list`. dev:harnesses is the diagnostic projection.

tools.name: dev:ipc_echo
tools.description: IPC transport verification — echoes the message back as a small typed event stream.

tools.name: dev:omp_session
tools.description: Find and read the omp session JSONL file for a spawn_id, by cwd + start-time match against ~/.omp/agent/sessions/.

guidance.when: Inspect an OMP CLI session's state — useful when debugging long-running CLI flows.
guidance.notWhen: For PRODUCTION agent runs, the orchestrator owns sessions. dev:omp_session is the CLI-tool inspector.

tools.name: dev:pg_active_queries
tools.description: List current pg_stat_activity rows (pid, state, query, duration) for the operator database.

guidance.when: Diagnostic: list currently-running PG queries (pg_stat_activity). Use when investigating slow / hung queries.
guidance.notWhen: For routine diagnostics, the /dev/pg panel is enough. Use this tool when scripting an investigation.

tools.name: dev:pg_health
tools.description: PostgreSQL version + connection counts (total/active/idle) for the operator database.

guidance.when: Diagnostic snapshot of PG health — connections, longest query, lock count. For the /dev/pg dashboard.
guidance.notWhen: For application-level health, use `harness:health`. pg_health is the database layer.

tools.name: dev:pg_query
tools.description: Run a read-only SELECT / WITH…SELECT against the operator Postgres (the canonical store behind plans, work-items, issues, observations, tool_invocations, scorecards, recipes, …). Read-only enforced; statement_timeout 5s; rows capped.

guidance.when: A filtered / aggregate / recency read of PG-CANONICAL state. Plans, work-items, issues, observations (engineer_issues), tool_invocations, scorecards are PG tables — the `*:list` tools and `docs/plans/*.md` files are PROJECTIONS. Query PG directly instead of fetching a whole `*:list` and post-filtering (which returns a huge result that spills to a file → don't then jq the projection). Example — recent plans this workspace: `SELECT plan_slug,status,created FROM harness_shared.harness_plans WHERE created >= '2026-06-17' AND workspace_id = '<ws>' ORDER BY created DESC LIMIT 50`. Aggregates (counts/group-by) are first-class here and awkward to jq.
guidance.notWhen: To CHANGE state — use the documented write verbs (plans:*, work_items:*, issues:* — they emit audit + sync invalidation). Writes are rejected here anyway (read-only transaction). For code-graph queries use `gitnexus:query`; for prose full-text use `search:fulltext` / `search:semantic`.
guidance.chaining: Alias any duplicate output column names (the result is wrapped in a subquery for the row cap, and PG rejects duplicate subquery columns). Pass `maxRows` to widen the cap up to 2000; if `truncated` is true, add a tighter WHERE / LIMIT rather than raising the cap blindly.

tools.name: dev:pg_table_sizes
tools.description: List tables in a pg schema with total size, index size, and estimated row count. Defaults to harness_shared.

guidance.when: Diagnostic: per-table sizes + row counts. Use when investigating storage growth.
guidance.notWhen: For application data analysis, query the relevant tools directly. pg_table_sizes is an ops view.

tools.name: dev:pipeline_position
tools.description: Read-only: where a change sits along the git-sync → green-checkpoint → release pipeline. Pass a repo-relative `path` (its latest commit) OR a `sha`; returns committed/on-staging/in-main/deployed + the green-gate stall context + a one-line summary. Answers "did my edit land + is it live on :3070?" without forensic git/PG/curl.

guidance.when: After leaving an edit in the tree (git-sync owns commit/push), to confirm it reached origin/staging, passed the green gate into main, and deployed to the live :3070 operator — or to see WHY it is stuck (gate red/stalled).
guidance.notWhen: To PAUSE sync (use locks:acquire_resource on git-sync:<slug>). For the whole-pipeline dashboard use the /admin Git tab; this is the targeted per-path/sha probe.
guidance.chaining: Edit a file → (git-sync commits within minutes) → dev:pipeline_position{path} to confirm it reached staging/main/:3070.

tools.name: dev:processes
tools.description: Inventory of agent-related processes on this host (run.sh, omp, claude, paperclip, pty, next) with cmdline, cwd, and inferred harness/workspace.

guidance.when: List tracked processes (delegates, plugin subprocesses, orchestrator children) for the /dev panel.
guidance.notWhen: For ACTIVE spawns, use `orchestrator.list_active`. For delegates, use `delegates:list`. dev:processes is the unified diagnostic view.

tools.name: dev:rate_governor_status
tools.description: Snapshot the fleet rate-limit layer now: live config (maxSimultaneousAgents + AIMD floor), fleet cap vs in-flight vs AIMD-effective concurrency, per (provider, model-class) governor buckets (paused/until, in-flight vs maxConcurrent, RPM/ITPM/OTPM headroom), recent usage telemetry (token throughput, $spend, usage% where a provider ceiling is known), and the opusBudget pacing state (aggregate 5h opus utilization + zone + which criticality classes are shedding opus→sonnet to stay under the ceiling, B-GW-4). Buckets are empty until a governed agent turn has run. Use to see whether the fleet/gym is currently rate-limit-paced, paused, AIMD-throttled, or opus-budget-shedding.

guidance.when: Diagnose whether agent spawns / stateless LLM calls are being paced or paused by the rate-limit governor (e.g. "why are runs slow / stalled?"), or read the fleet cap / effective concurrency / usage% the top-bar shows.
guidance.notWhen: Service up/down — dev:service_health. Migration drift — db:check_drift. EDITING the cap — operator:rate_limit_config.

tools.name: dev:restart
tools.description: Restart the operator dev server, coordinated. DRY RUN unless confirm:true. With confirm, acquires exclusive(dev-server) and drains current users (wait:{max_drain_sec}) before restarting, then releases (broadcasts "back up"). The real restart also requires PAPERCUSP_ALLOW_DEV_RESTART=1 on the host. Prefer this over a raw systemctl restart.

guidance.when: You need to restart the dev server (e.g. to pick up a lib/** edit). Run dry first to see who is using it; then confirm to drain + restart.
guidance.notWhen: Just probing the server — that needs no restart. Never restart casually on a shared box; it disrupts every agent using the app.
guidance.chaining: dev:restart (dry) → review holders → dev:restart { confirm: true, max_drain_sec } → connection drops as it restarts.

tools.name: dev:service_health
tools.description: Probe the dev services now (:3070 operator, :3055 vite, :3350 scout, :8082 code-server, the Tauri desktop via its dev-bridge eval + IPC socket + recent error toasts, AND the papercup-bg-host DBOS ticker via routine fire-freshness) — up/down + status + latency. The "bg-host-ticker" entry is a SEPARATE service from :3070: when it reads down, git-sync + every scheduled routine are FROZEN even though :3070 is up — do NOT dev:restart the operator for that, the bg-host needs reviving. The desktop entry reports present:false when no desktop is running. Use before relying on a service or after a "connection refused".

guidance.when: Confirm which dev services are up before testing against one; diagnose a "connection refused" / stale-server symptom; OR diagnose a git-sync / routine-engine stall — the "bg-host-ticker" entry tells you whether the SEPARATE bg-host routine engine is frozen (so you do not misattribute it to :3070).
guidance.notWhen: File/lock contention — that is locks:queue. Migration drift — db:check_drift.

tools.name: dev:session_detail
tools.description: Drilldown for one spawn_id: agent metadata, tool invocations timeline, child spawns, related chats.

guidance.when: Read full detail of one /dev session — request history, env, traces.
guidance.notWhen: For the SESSION LIST, use `dev:sessions` first.

tools.name: dev:sessions
tools.description: Cross-workspace agent sessions, one row per spawn_id with started/ended/tool_count/error_count/duration totals.

guidance.when: List recent /dev panel sessions — used by the dev UI to populate session pickers.
guidance.notWhen: For application AGENT chat sessions, use `agent_chats:list`. dev:sessions is the panel's own concept.

tools.name: dev:state_counter
tools.description: Demo state-shaped tool: ticks a counter and publishes each tick via ctx.publishState. Reconnect-resilient by construction.

tools.name: dev:telemetry
tools.description: Per-tool invocation rollup (count, error rate, p50/p95) across selected workspaces over the last N hours.

guidance.when: Read recent telemetry datapoints (errors, slow requests). For the /dev/telemetry dashboard.
guidance.notWhen: For per-agent audit, use `audit:list`. telemetry is observability-shaped, not action-shaped.

tools.name: dev:tool_cooccurrence
tools.description: Pairwise tool co-occurrence (support / confidence / lift) grouped by spawn_id over MCP tool_invocations — which tools get invoked together in one agent turn. The deterministic candidate-generator for wrapper/bundle tools.

guidance.when: Find which agent tools are invoked TOGETHER in the same turn (spawn), ranked by support / confidence / lift — to spot bundle/wrapper candidates and feed code-recipes candidate generation. Analytical / offline; MCP-transport calls only.
guidance.notWhen: For per-tool counts or latency use `dev:telemetry`; for a forensic per-agent timeline use `audit:list`. A high lift on tiny support is spurious — keep a support floor (minSupport), and remember lift != determinism: this NOMINATES pairs, a human/gate judges whether the steps are mechanical before wrapping.
guidance.chaining: dev:tool_cooccurrence (find bonded pairs) → judge determinism → wrap as a composite (e.g. extend coord:orient) or feed code-recipes promotion.

tools.name: discovery:hives
tools.description: Browse the P2P hive directory — the verified hives this peer has seen announced on the well-known directory topic (title · description · owner · member harnesses). Best-effort gossip: joining a listed hive still runs the full admission/attestation flow. Feeds the pui Hives/Network board + the desktop HiveDirectoryPanel.

guidance.when: You want to see hives available to join across the P2P network (the browse list behind the pui Hives/Network board + the desktop HiveDirectoryPanel).
guidance.notWhen: To list the workspace-local deployed hive frames (hiveControlFrames) use the harness/hive surfaces. To actually join a listed hive, run the join-shared-harness flow per member topic.

tools.name: discovery:set_hive
tools.description: Create or edit a hive's P2P directory listing — title, description, and visibility (public = announce to the global directory; invite = invite-scoped topic only; private = never announced). Saves the metadata to the workspace registry and announces it per visibility so peers can browse + join it.

guidance.when: You want to publish a hive to the P2P directory so other peers can discover + join it, or edit an existing listing (title/description/visibility).
guidance.notWhen: To deploy a hive’s execution frames use deploy:hive. To browse OTHERS’ hives use discovery:hives. Setting visibility:private withdraws a hive from the directory (it stops being re-announced; peers age it out via TTL).

tools.name: docs:get
tools.description: Fetch documentation pages by slug — your harness's docs (in a harness), your project's docs (PAPERCUSP_PROJECT_DOCS_ROOT env var), or the Papercusp framework reference (papercusp-su callers only). Batch up to 10; pass `heading` (single-slug only) for a section slice. Per-slug error envelope.

guidance.when: You have slugs from docs:outline and need page contents. Use `heading` (single-slug) when only one section of a long page is relevant.
guidance.notWhen: You do not yet know the slug — call docs:outline first. To fetch another harness's docs from outside, use cross_harness:docs_get.
guidance.chaining: docs:outline → docs:get { slugs } (batch up to 10) → optionally re-fetch with { slugs: [picked], heading } for surgical reads.

tools.name: docs:outline
tools.description: Return the documentation table-of-contents for your context — your harness's docs (in a harness), your project's docs (PAPERCUSP_PROJECT_DOCS_ROOT env var), or the Papercusp framework engineering reference (papercusp-su callers only). Cached per run. Call this FIRST when you need design context; drill in via docs:get.

guidance.when: You need design context, architectural rationale, or "how does X work" answers and have not yet called docs:outline this run.
guidance.notWhen: You already called docs:outline this run — cached. For prose recall (chats, escalations, brainstorms) use search:fulltext. To explore another harness from outside, use cross_harness:docs_outline.
guidance.chaining: docs:outline → docs:get { slugs: [...] }. Use { slug, heading } when only one section of a long page is relevant.

tools.name: docs:search
tools.description: Keyword search across your context's documentation — your harness's docs (in a harness), your project's docs (PAPERCUSP_PROJECT_DOCS_ROOT env var), or the Papercusp framework reference (papercusp-su callers only). Returns ranked hits (slug, title, description, excerpt).

guidance.when: You have specific terminology in mind (a function name, concept, or component) and want to find which doc page covers it. Faster than scanning the outline when the section name is non-obvious.
guidance.notWhen: You do not know what to search for — call docs:outline first. For PG-stored prose (chats, escalations) use search:fulltext. To search another harness from outside, use cross_harness:docs_search.
guidance.chaining: docs:search → docs:get { slugs: [top-hit] } (or { slug, heading } if the hit excerpt names a specific heading).

tools.name: events:await
tools.description: Register a one-shot WAKE subscription on an exact event key (e.g. lock:grant:<ticket>, plan-run:finished:<id>, or any key a source/peer will events:emit) — the named sugar for watch(key,{wake:true,once:true}). When it fires you are re-invoked — a live managed-pty session gets the wake injected as a turn; an exited session is resumed with the wake reason as the prompt; an open terminal we cannot inject gets an inbox nudge and is resumed when it exits. Then END YOUR TURN — do not poll or hold the connection.

guidance.when: You need X-to-happen-before-you-proceed and X is announced as an event: a lock grant, a plan-run finishing, a peer answering, CI/deploy landing, a custom key a collaborator will emit. Register, optionally tell the emitter the key, then end your turn and sleep.
guidance.notWhen: Ambient interest in an area — that is topics:subscribe (notify; never wakes). Sub-minute waits inside one turn — just do the bounded blocking call. Recurring schedules — the pot/routines own time-based wakes; an await is ONE-shot.
guidance.chaining: events:await { event } → end your turn. On wake, the turn text carries the event + payload — continue the blocked work. events:cancel to retract; events:status to inspect your active awaits + recent wakes.

tools.name: events:cancel
tools.description: Cancel one of your active events:await registrations (await_id — you will not be woken), or ACK a pending/parked wake delivery you already saw via the inbox nudge (delivery_id — you will not be resumed for it). Pass at least one.

guidance.when: The thing you were waiting on no longer matters (cancel the await), or a parked wake reached you in-turn via the inbox and you handled it (ack the delivery so the system does not also resume you).
guidance.notWhen: A fired await needs no cancel (one-shot — it already cleared). You cannot cancel or ack a peer’s.
guidance.chaining: events:status to find the await_id / delivery_id → events:cancel.

tools.name: events:emit
tools.description: Fire an event key through the await-event primitive: every agent with an events:await on the key is woken (durable delivery — pty-inject / session-resume / inbox ladder); an optional `to` list additionally receives a coord inbox notification (notify policy — never wakes). Use the key your waiter registered (events:await tells them what to wait on).

guidance.when: Announcing that the thing a peer is blocked on has happened: their requested work is done, an artifact landed, a decision resolved. Pair with events:await — the waiter registers the key, you emit it.
guidance.notWhen: General status narration — lifecycle auto-emits + work_items:complete already cover it. Conversation — coord:send. If nobody could plausibly be awaiting the key and you have no `to`, the emit reaches no one (it is not a log).
guidance.chaining: Peer: events:await { event: K } → you: do the work → events:emit { event: K, summary } → peer wakes.

tools.name: events:graph
tools.description: Inspect the event-reaction reactive graph: every registered rule as an `on → fire` edge (the Events file + emits desugar + plugin/blueprint rules), with its condition kind, mode, and source. With recent:true, also returns the reactions that actually fired (from tool_invocations) with their cause-chain — the answer to "why did this fire?".

guidance.when: You want to see the declarative "when X, fire Y" wiring — what reactions exist, what triggers them, and (recent:true) what has actually fired lately with its cause-chain. Pass `on` to see only the rules that fire on a given tool.
guidance.notWhen: To register a rule, use the events registry API in code (registerReactionRule) or a tool's `emits` field — there is no runtime "add a rule" tool by design (rules are curated code). For the live worker activity stream use `activity:recent`.

tools.name: events:status
tools.description: Inspect the await-event surface: your active awaits, your recent wake deliveries (with channel + status), and optionally the workspace wake meter (per-agent wake counts, last 24h — the wake-storm detector).

guidance.when: Checking what you are (still) waiting on, whether a wake fired and via which channel, or whether the fleet is wake-storming (meter: true).
guidance.notWhen: Reading your message stream — that is coord:inbox. Following an area — topics:feed.

tools.name: experiment:catalog
tools.description: Discover the registered experiment tests (eval-battery Subjects) the self-learning loop can run. Each entry: id, kind (replay|component|whole-instance|whole-hive|drill), fidelityTier (offline=~$0 deterministic replay, the default screen; shadow; live=real agent spend), knobSlice (the knob-space addresses it can vary), metrics (deterministic signals + judge rubric dimensions), costClass. Read-only. Filter by kind/tier. Pair with experiment:run to invoke one.

guidance.when: Choosing which test to run against a knob change — list the catalog to see what kinds exist, which tier each runs at (offline replay is the cheap default screen), and which knobs each can vary. Filter by kind/tier.
guidance.notWhen: Running an experiment (experiment:run). Scoring one gym run’s deterministic guardrails (gym:signals). Subjective quality scoring (gym:judge).
guidance.chaining: experiment:catalog → pick a testId + read its knobSlice → experiment:run with arms addressing only that slice.

tools.name: experiment:results
tools.description: List recent experiment runs (the experiment_runs ledger) for this workspace — battery, test, tier, winner, per-arm scores, total cost, and decision (proposed|applied|rejected). Read-only; newest-first; filter by testId. Closes the loop with experiment:run (which records here).

guidance.when: Reviewing how past experiments performed — which arms won, at what cost, and whether they were applied. Filter by testId to a single test kind.
guidance.notWhen: Running a new experiment (experiment:run). Discovering test kinds (experiment:catalog).
guidance.chaining: experiment:run → experiment:results (read back the recorded outcomes).

tools.name: experiment:run
tools.description: Run an experiment: A/B a knob change against a battery via the eval-battery engine and get per-arm judge scores + the compareArms verdict. OFFLINE replay is the default front door (tier defaults to "offline", ~$0 deterministic) — re-run each synthetic case under each arm’s policy/model overlay and score outcome/process/divergence; rides frontier:replay-harness (flag + governor budget; origin-tagged spend), refusing with NO spend if dark/exhausted. Escalating to a spending tier (set tier:"live") requires escalation justification (a positive offline signal or a written couldn’t-isolate trigger; +costException for whole-instance/whole-Hive) and an armed governor budget — it fails closed. The gym live tier is reachable when its AbDeps are armed; instance/hive stay staged (their own loops drive them). Arms must address only the test’s knobSlice (experiment:catalog). A winner is a PROPOSAL — applying it rides commit→reproject + graduation, never this tool.

guidance.when: Testing how a knob change performs before adopting it — screen a policy/prompt overlay against a battery on the cheap offline replay tier; the result ranks arms vs the baseline.
guidance.notWhen: Discovery (experiment:catalog). Scoring one gym run (gym:judge/gym:signals). Applying a winner to live prompts — that rides commit→reproject + graduation (D-006), never here.
guidance.chaining: experiment:catalog → pick testId + read knobSlice → experiment:run → (winner is a proposal).

tools.name: features:get
tools.description:
When to use: User names a specific feature ("the auth one", "F-AUTH-001") and you need its body / acceptance criteria.

When NOT to use: For a list of features in a harness, use `harness:list_features`. For changes over time, use `features:history`.

Chaining: Follow `harness:list_features` or `features:search` to find the id.

guidance.when: User names a specific feature ("the auth one", "F-AUTH-001") and you need its body / acceptance criteria.
guidance.notWhen: For a list of features in a harness, use `harness:list_features`. For changes over time, use `features:history`.
guidance.chaining: Follow `harness:list_features` or `features:search` to find the id.

tools.name: features:history
tools.description:
When to use: User asks "what changed on feature X?", "who edited the spec?", or you need a timeline of edits.

When NOT to use: For the CURRENT body, use `features:get`. For cross-feature audit, use `audit:list`.

guidance.when: User asks "what changed on feature X?", "who edited the spec?", or you need a timeline of edits.
guidance.notWhen: For the CURRENT body, use `features:get`. For cross-feature audit, use `audit:list`.

tools.name: features:list_related
tools.description:
When to use: You have a feature and need to find related ones — tag overlap, shared chunks, dependency neighbors.

When NOT to use: For free-text "find features about X", use `features:search`. For ALL features in a harness, use `harness:list_features`.

Chaining: After `features:get`, use this to discover the neighborhood.

guidance.when: You have a feature and need to find related ones — tag overlap, shared chunks, dependency neighbors.
guidance.notWhen: For free-text "find features about X", use `features:search`. For ALL features in a harness, use `harness:list_features`.
guidance.chaining: After `features:get`, use this to discover the neighborhood.

tools.name: features:search
tools.description:
When to use: Free-text query for features matching a topic ("auth", "error handling") — use when the user names a concept, not a specific feature id.

When NOT to use: For specific feature id, use `features:get`. For ALL features in a harness, use `harness:list_features`. For cross-resource search, use `search:query`.

guidance.when: Free-text query for features matching a topic ("auth", "error handling") — use when the user names a concept, not a specific feature id.
guidance.notWhen: For specific feature id, use `features:get`. For ALL features in a harness, use `harness:list_features`. For cross-resource search, use `search:query`.

tools.name: features:tag_vocabulary
tools.description:
When to use: You need the set of known feature tags before tagging a new one — keeps tags consistent across the harness.

When NOT to use: For finding features BY a tag, use `features:search` (free-text) or `features:list_related`.

guidance.when: You need the set of known feature tags before tagging a new one — keeps tags consistent across the harness.
guidance.notWhen: For finding features BY a tag, use `features:search` (free-text) or `features:list_related`.

tools.name: flags:get
tools.description: Resolve one Papercusp feature flag to a boolean for this host.

tools.name: flags:list
tools.description: List every Papercusp feature flag with its resolved boolean state for this host. Use to discover what features are gated, audit V1 ship state, or check whether a flag is on before suggesting work that depends on it.

guidance.when: Before recommending or executing work that lives behind a feature flag (snapshots, templates, marketplace, oracle, harness phases, cloudflare publish).
guidance.notWhen: For runtime user-facing flag reads, use the /api/flags/bootstrap endpoint from the client.

tools.name: flags:set
tools.description: Flip a Papercusp feature flag on or off in PostHog. High-risk: changes app-wide behavior. Provide a clear reason; it is recorded for audit.

guidance.when: User explicitly asks to enable / disable a feature, OR Papercusp is being prepared for a release and the V1 ship state needs to be set.
guidance.notWhen: For ad-hoc testing of UI behavior, prefer the PostHog dashboard so changes are visible to other agents and humans.

tools.name: fleet:admit
tools.description: Ask the backpressure governor whether a spawn is affordable (global spend ceiling + per-harness/user bulkhead + circuit breaker + role credits). Debits the buckets/credit on admit; consumes nothing on refusal.

guidance.when: Before spawning an agent, to bound runaway fleet spend. Unconfigured scopes are unconstrained, so this is a no-op until the curator seeds governor cells via fleet:governor.
guidance.chaining: fleet:governor (seed buckets/circuits/credits) → fleet:admit (per spawn) → spawn if admitted.

tools.name: fleet:assignments
tools.description: The canonical "who's on what" query: per-agent presence + plan-item + work-item claims unified (claim-primary, holder liveness AND progress joined). Each live agent carries its ordered work-list — `doing` (head-of-line), `queued`, `load` — the externalized per-bee TodoWrite the Queen reads for placement (load → warm-inject vs fresh slot; head-of-line → evict; ordered plan → affinity). The single LIVE source for "is X really being worked": surfaces `orphaned` (live lease, DEAD holder) AND `stalled` (live holder, NO progress in window) claims — both reclaimable, neither "covered" — plus per-claim `activity` (free|reserved|alive|progressing|stalled|dead) and declared-but-unclaimed intents. Read this, not a stale coord broadcast (agent-activity-liveness-truth).

guidance.when: Answering "who's running / what is agent X doing / X's ordered work-list / how loaded is X / is anyone on plan P". The state query AND the placement-decision read — use it instead of scanning coord:inbox or replaying lifecycle messages.
guidance.notWhen: You want to be notified of future changes (subscribe the fleet_assignment change-feed) or you need full message history (coord:inbox).
guidance.chaining: fleet:assignments { plan } → an orphaned/stalled claim (dead/not-progressing holder = NOT covered) → work_items:release / plan_items:release, or pick it up yourself; never assume "someone's on it" from a coord message. fleet:assignments { agent } before messaging an agent about its work.

tools.name: fleet:bee_mail
tools.description: Read one bee's coordination mail by ownerId: its INBOX (messages addressed to it, or broadcast) and its OUTBOX (messages it sent). The observer view behind the bee-dossier dock pane — distinct from coord:inbox, which reads YOUR own inbox. Read-only; no heartbeat.

guidance.when: Rendering the bee-dossier pane, or inspecting what a specific bee has received/sent without being that bee.
guidance.notWhen: Reading YOUR own inbox (use coord:inbox — it also heartbeats your presence). Deriving fleet state / who is on what (use fleet:assignments).
guidance.chaining: fleet:selected_bee {} (poll the selection) → fleet:bee_mail { owner_id } + fleet:assignments { agent: owner_id } for the full dossier.

tools.name: fleet:cancel
tools.description: Cancel a spawn subtree: mark every active descendant cancelled and release its claims + locks NOW. The structured-concurrency abort — use it instead of waiting for leases to expire.

guidance.when: A human/operator aborts a unit of work, or a supervisor tears down a doomed subtree. Cancels the named spawn AND all its descendants transitively, freeing their locks + work-item/plan-item claims immediately.
guidance.notWhen: To cancel a single leaf with no children — that is the same call with a leaf spawn_id, but prefer it when you specifically mean the whole subtree.
guidance.chaining: fleet:tree (inspect the subtree) → fleet:cancel { spawn_id }.

tools.name: fleet:drain
tools.description: Signal a running bee to gracefully wind down (checkpoint, release locks/claims, return work-list, exit). Distinct from fleet:cancel (hard kill). The bee can cooperate or request deferral (propose/dispose). The Queen waits bounded time before reclaiming the slot. Returns immediately; the drain is async.

guidance.when: You (the Queen) want to reclaim a bee slot: the occupant has low-priority work, is blocked, or the priorities have shifted. Send a drain cue to give the bee a chance to hand off cleanly.
guidance.notWhen: The bee is actively running a high-priority task (let it finish naturally). Or if immediate slot reclaim is critical (use fleet:cancel). Or if the bee is unresponsive (use fleet:cancel after a timeout).
guidance.chaining: fleet:drain { bee_id } → (later, bounded) fleet:assignments { agent: bee_id } (check if the bee has released its slot) → fleet:spawn { role: "bee", brief: ... } (spawn fresh).

tools.name: fleet:governor
tools.description: Configure the backpressure governor: set a token bucket (spend ceiling/bulkhead), a circuit breaker, or a credit pool; grant credits; or record a spawn success/failure against a circuit.

guidance.when: Seeding or tuning fleet backpressure (the curator owns this). scope_key examples: "global", "harness:papercup", "user:alice", "role:worker".
guidance.chaining: fleet:governor { op:"set_bucket", scope_key:"global", capacity, refill_per_sec } → fleet:admit per spawn.

tools.name: fleet:opus_budget
tools.description: Read or set the fleet opus-budget shed bands: reserveStart (shed background opus→sonnet), reserveHard (also shed normal), nearCap (pace critical), staleMs. Default 0.75/0.88/0.95. The only incident lever for opus shedding; set is audited + one-call-revertible, with monotonicity (reserveStart < reserveHard < nearCap < 1) enforced.

guidance.when: During an opus capacity crunch, shed earlier (lower reserveStart) to reserve more 5h headroom, or relax the bands when budget is fine — live, no redeploy.
guidance.notWhen: To change WHICH roles count as critical/background (those role lists are still code consts — a tracked follow-up). To READ live pacing/zone state, use dev:rate_governor_status.
guidance.chaining: dev:rate_governor_status shows the live opusBudget zone take effect; config:list-overrides shows the active override.

tools.name: fleet:place_batch
tools.description: Place a whole batch of ready work onto the fleet in ONE wake: ranks each task↔bee by affinity (explicit-intent > file-overlap > recent-activity > queue-similarity), then warm-injects onto warm bees / fresh-spawns into free slots / queues the overflow — up to the fleet ceiling. The Queen's serial placement loop, collapsed to one call. Pass `tasks` (your importance-ranked frontier) or a `harness` to pull its open backlog; `dry_run` returns the plan without acting.

guidance.when: You (the Queen) have surveyed + ranked the ready frontier and want to place several tasks at once instead of looping fleet:spawn/coord:send per task. Pass the ranked work-item ids as `tasks` (importance order) — the tool fans them across free slots + warm bees by affinity in one turn.
guidance.notWhen: Placing a SINGLE task (just fleet:spawn or coord:send), or you have not yet surveyed the frontier (work_items:list + fleet:assignments first). Not a survey tool — it acts. Use dry_run:true to preview the plan.
guidance.chaining: work_items:list (the frontier) + fleet:assignments (bee load) → fleet:place_batch { tasks } → fleet:tree to watch the fresh spawns; an await_event in the result means re-run for the deferred tail on a freed slot.

tools.name: fleet:sandbox_deps
tools.description: Check the host dependencies of the fleet spawn sandbox (bubblewrap/socat/srt, the Ubuntu 24.04+ AppArmor userns profile, container nesting, platform support). Read-only; returns per-check verdicts with remedies.

guidance.when: Fleet spawns fail at sandbox startup, before enabling the sandbox on a new host/deployment, or when auditing a frame/VM before placing work on it.
guidance.notWhen: Diagnosing a running service being down (use dev:service_health) or a spawn failing for non-sandbox reasons (read its run log first).
guidance.chaining: fleet:sandbox_deps {} → fix the failed checks via their remedy lines (or opt the host out with PAPERCUSP_FLEET_SANDBOX=0) → retry the spawn.

tools.name: fleet:selected_bee
tools.description: Get or set the ephemeral "selected bee" for the bee-dossier dock pane. With no args, RETURNS the currently selected bee (the bee pane polls this). With `select`, PUBLISHES the selection (the swarm/Fleet pane calls this when its cursor moves). In-memory, per-workspace, non-durable — a transport between the two pui dock processes, never persisted.

guidance.when: Driving the desktop chat dock's bee-dossier pane: the swarm pane sets the selection on cursor move; the bee pane reads it to know which bee to render.
guidance.notWhen: You want durable assignment state or "who is on what" — use fleet:assignments. This holds only the transient UI selection.
guidance.chaining: Fleet pane: fleet:selected_bee { select: { owner_id } } on cursor move. Bee pane: fleet:selected_bee {} (poll) → fleet:assignments { agent } + fleet:bee_mail { owner_id } for the dossier.

tools.name: fleet:spawn
tools.description: Spawn one agent of a role into a registered harness (project). Returns a spawn_id immediately; the run is tracked durably in the nursery — watch it with fleet:tree, stop it with fleet:cancel. role="worker" requires chunk.

guidance.when: The user asks to launch an agent on a piece of work — "spawn a validator in <harness>", "put a worker on <feature>", "have a scoper break down X". The spawn is fire-and-forget: acknowledge the launch and check fleet:tree later. Pick a `tier` per task (quick/standard/deep/max — see the arg rubric); omit it for routine work at the role default.
guidance.notWhen: For answering a question you already know — spawning is for new work, not lookups. For the durable feature pipeline, file a work_item and let the harness autoloop dispatch it.
guidance.chaining: fleet:spawn → (later) fleet:tree { spawn_id } to watch → fleet:cancel { spawn_id } to abort.

tools.name: fleet:supervise
tools.description: Report a crashed spawn. The supervisor restarts the strategy's set (one_for_one/one_for_all/rest_for_one) within the restart-intensity budget, or tears the subtree down + escalates to a human when it is crash-looping.

guidance.when: A supervised child exited abnormally and you (the control supervisor / curator) must decide restart-vs-escalate. Returns the restart set, or the escalation id when the crash-loop bound is breached.
guidance.notWhen: For a clean human abort — that is fleet:cancel, not a crash.
guidance.chaining: detect crash → fleet:supervise { spawn_id } → (restart the returned set) | (handle the escalation).

tools.name: fleet:tree
tools.description: Read a spawn subtree (the nursery): every descendant with its status, owner, role, and the work it serves, plus whether the root can complete (no live child).

guidance.when: Before fleet:cancel (see what would be torn down) or before completing a nursery (the completion gate refuses while a child lives).
guidance.chaining: fleet:tree → fleet:cancel { spawn_id }.

tools.name: gateway:reload
tools.description: HOT-RELOAD the inference gateway account pool from the DB source-of-truth NOW (POST :8788/admin/reload) — applies a just-made accounts:register / accounts:remove / egress change to the RUNNING gateway immediately, NO restart (vs waiting for the gateway’s ~60s poll). Returns {ok, changed, version, accounts}; changed:false means the live pool already matched the DB.

guidance.when: Right after accounts:register / accounts:remove / an egress change, to apply it live without a gateway restart.
guidance.notWhen: You can wait ~60s — the gateway polls + hot-reloads the DB pool on its own.
guidance.chaining: accounts:register → gateway:reload → gateway:status.

tools.name: gateway:status
tools.description: Read the inference gateway LIVE config (GET :8788/admin/config): the account-pool config version, the live account ids, and the admission/AIMD concurrency state. Use to see what pool + concurrency the RUNNING gateway is actually using, or to confirm a gateway:reload landed (the version bumped). Returns {ok, version, accounts, admission, aimd, ...}.

guidance.when: Confirming what the running gateway is using right now, or verifying a hot-reload took effect (version bump).
guidance.notWhen: Editing the pool itself — accounts:register / accounts:remove (then gateway:reload to apply live).
guidance.chaining: accounts:register/remove → gateway:reload → gateway:status (confirm version + accounts).

tools.name: generators:publish
tools.description: Publish the item-set your feature discovered (a scan/enumerate/audit result) so a completion-time generative wave (`for_each: { from_feature: <your feature> }`) can mint one child feature per item — each blocked_by your feature, so they run only after you finish. Idempotent (re-publishing replaces the set).

guidance.when: Your feature is the discovery half of a discover-then-act generative wave (the plan declares a `for_each: { from_feature: <you> }` wave) and you have produced the concrete list of items the downstream wave should fan out over.
guidance.notWhen: Your work has no downstream generative wave, or the item-set is already known at promote time (use a promote-time `items`/`glob`/`sql` resolver instead).
guidance.chaining: Call once near the end of your run, after the scan/enumeration is complete and verified.

tools.name: goals:get
tools.description:
When to use: User names a specific goal and wants the rationale / acceptance criteria.

When NOT to use: For a list of goals, use `goals:list` first.

Chaining: Follow `goals:list` to find the id.

guidance.when: User names a specific goal and wants the rationale / acceptance criteria.
guidance.notWhen: For a list of goals, use `goals:list` first.
guidance.chaining: Follow `goals:list` to find the id.

tools.name: goals:list
tools.description:
When to use: User asks "what are we trying to do?", "what are my goals?", or you need a goal id before calling `goals:get`.

When NOT to use: For TASKS (concrete TODOs), use `tasks:list`. Goals are the higher-level intent; tasks are how you get there.

Chaining: Pair with `goals:get` for the full body.

guidance.when: User asks "what are we trying to do?", "what are my goals?", or you need a goal id before calling `goals:get`.
guidance.notWhen: For TASKS (concrete TODOs), use `tasks:list`. Goals are the higher-level intent; tasks are how you get there.
guidance.chaining: Pair with `goals:get` for the full body.

tools.name: gym:judge
tools.description: Score a gym run's distilled trace with the frozen Opus judge (the only grader of record), using the target blueprint's rubric. Pass {intent, projectContext, distilledTrace, rubric?} where rubric mirrors the target's blueprint.gym.rubric (omit → GYM_JUDGE_RUBRIC_V1). Returns {d1,d2,d3,composite,rationale,judgeModel,rubricHash,costUsd,...}. Reasons ABOVE the harness's own validator (intent/spec-gaps, quality, process).

guidance.when: Scoring a completed gym run for the optimizer — the subjective reward the proposer optimizes. Use the TARGET blueprint's gym.rubric so a coding vs research target is judged on its own dimensions.
guidance.notWhen: Deterministic guardrails (regressions, planted-bug) — that is gym:signals, which the optimizer cannot game. Literal spec conformance — that is the target harness's own validator.
guidance.chaining: gym runner → collect+distill trace → gym:judge (rubric from target) → proposer reflects on the rationale.

tools.name: gym:set-gates
tools.description: Read or set a harness's gym promotion gates: epsilon / delta (accept margins) + costCeiling (max cost multiple of baseline a champion may promote at). Default 0.1 / 0.5 / 3. The gym loop is human-gated, so these only steer its ADVISORY verdict. set is audited + one-call-revertible.

guidance.when: Tune a harness's gym accept strictness — raise epsilon/delta to demand a bigger measured win before a champion is flagged promotable, or raise costCeiling to tolerate a costlier champion.
guidance.notWhen: To accept/reject a specific proposal use gym:accept (human gate). Judge WEIGHTS live in the blueprint gym rubric, not here. To arm the gym loop itself, see the gym autoloop config.
guidance.chaining: config:list-overrides shows active per-harness gate overrides; config:reset-overrides reverts them.

tools.name: gym:signals
tools.description: Evaluate a target blueprint's deterministic gym signals (un-gameable guardrails) over one run's inputs. Pass `signals` (from the target's blueprint.gym.signals) + any of {preTests, postTests, plantedBug, harnessOutputText, drillOutcomes}. Returns {results:[{name,value,applicable,metric?}], unknown, known, drillSource}. Built-ins: regressionsFromTests (pre+post tests), plantedBugCaught (plantedBug+harnessOutputText), drillResolveRate/drillTriageAccuracy/drillMttsh (drill rows w/ planted known answers; value=SLO verdict, metric=raw rate/ms). Drill rows: pass drillOutcomes, or set loadDrillOutcomes to read the live sandbox corpus from PG.

guidance.when: Scoring a gym run's deterministic guardrails — the optimizer can't game these, so they gate/monitor a variant independently of the judge. Resolve the TARGET blueprint's gym.signals by name; set loadDrillOutcomes to pull the live red-queen sandbox corpus for the drill signals.
guidance.notWhen: Subjective quality scoring — that is the frozen judge (gym:judge). Running the pipeline — the gym runner.
guidance.chaining: gym runner → collect run inputs (tests/output) → gym:signals (loadDrillOutcomes for drill targets) → proposer + trace summary.

tools.name: harness:create
tools.description: Create a harness and instantiate a Blueprint into it. Provide an existing repo `path` OR `parentDir`+`folderName` to make a new dir; choose the blueprint via `blueprintId` (resolved local → installed → built-in, e.g. "coding"/"research" or a Cupboard-installed id) OR an inline `blueprint` object. The blueprint's knobs.requiresRepo decides git-init: coding → a git repo, research → a repo-less state dir. Registers the harness, provisions its PG schema, writes the git-canonical .papercusp/blueprint.yaml. Returns {ok, slug, path, blueprint}.

guidance.when: Spinning up a new managed harness (coding from a repo, or a repo-less research harness) configured by a blueprint. The agent-authorable path to a new harness.
guidance.notWhen: Running an existing harness (orchestrator). Authoring a blueprint without creating a harness — blueprint:create/extend.
guidance.chaining: blueprint:extend/validate → harness:create { slug, path|parentDir+folderName, blueprintId|blueprint }.

tools.name: harness:escalation
tools.description: Read escalation + supervisor-notes for a harness (PG-canonical; falls back to disk).

guidance.when: User asks "what's flagged?", "what got escalated to the supervisor?", or you need to see the supervisor's notes on a harness.
guidance.notWhen: For general "what's wrong with X" (open issues), use `issues:list`. Escalation files are a specific, narrower view than the issue list.

tools.name: harness:generate-from-repo
tools.description: Generate a coding harness from an EXISTING git repo (kind #1 creation). Deterministically detects the test command (and VERIFIES it by running it once), the toolchain, monorepo/frontend flags, and harvests AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/TESTING.md into an `extends: coding-factory` blueprint override; validates it; then creates the harness via harness:create. Skips if the repo already has .papercusp/blueprint.yaml. Use `dryRun` to preview the generated override without creating. Returns {ok, slug?, skipped?, override?, detection, validation}.

guidance.when: Onboarding an existing code repository as a managed coding harness — you want the blueprint inferred from the repo (test command, stack, monorepo/frontend) rather than authored by hand.
guidance.notWhen: The repo already has a .papercusp/blueprint.yaml (it is skipped — edit the file instead). Creating a repo-less / research harness, or one whose blueprint you author explicitly — harness:create with blueprintId/blueprint. Generate-from-plan (kinds #2/#3) is out of scope.
guidance.chaining: harness:generate-from-repo { slug, path, dryRun:true } → (inspect override) → harness:generate-from-repo { slug, path } (creates). Or blueprint:validate the returned override.

tools.name: harness:get
tools.description:
When to use: User asks about a specific harness by name ("tell me about sheets", "what's the status of forms") and you need its row + feature counts.

When NOT to use: For a list of all harnesses, use `harness:list`. For LIVE health (escalated/blocked), prefer `harness:status` or `escalations:get` — `harness:get` is the static record.

Chaining: Follow `harness:list` if you don't have the slug. Follow with `harness:status` if you also need live counts.

guidance.when: User asks about a specific harness by name ("tell me about sheets", "what's the status of forms") and you need its row + feature counts.
guidance.notWhen: For a list of all harnesses, use `harness:list`. For LIVE health (escalated/blocked), prefer `harness:status` or `escalations:get` — `harness:get` is the static record.
guidance.chaining: Follow `harness:list` if you don't have the slug. Follow with `harness:status` if you also need live counts.

tools.name: harness:health
tools.description: Read consolidated health verdict for a harness (alive, escalated, feature counts, ghost rate, checks).

guidance.when: User asks "is sheets healthy?", "is the harness running?". Single fast snapshot — alive, escalated flag, feature-status counts.
guidance.notWhen: For LIVE phase + activity (recent audit events), use `harness:status`. For open issues, use `issues:list`.

tools.name: harness:list
tools.description:
When to use: User asks "what harnesses do I have?", "show me my projects", or you need a slug to feed into harness:get / harness:status.

When NOT to use: For ONE specific harness, use `harness:get`. For a single harness's live health (active/done counts), use `harness:status`.

Chaining: Pair with `harness:get` (detail) or `harness:status` (live counts) once you have the slug.

guidance.when: User asks "what harnesses do I have?", "show me my projects", or you need a slug to feed into harness:get / harness:status.
guidance.notWhen: For ONE specific harness, use `harness:get`. For a single harness's live health (active/done counts), use `harness:status`.
guidance.chaining: Pair with `harness:get` (detail) or `harness:status` (live counts) once you have the slug.

tools.name: harness:list_features
tools.description: List features for a harness slug (optionally for a specific phase: staging, testing, production).

guidance.when: User asks "what features does sheets have?" or you need a feature id before calling `features:get`. Pass a phase to scope (staging = upcoming, testing = in-flight, production = done).
guidance.notWhen: For ONE feature's detail, use `features:get`. For the harness as a whole, use `harness:list`/`harness:get`.
guidance.chaining: Pair with `features:get` for body, `features:history` for change log.

tools.name: harness:markdown_index
tools.description: Load the per-harness markdown index (filename + headings + anchor ids) across the workspace.

guidance.when: User asks "what docs exist?", "where's the spec for X?", or you need to navigate to a specific section of the harness's markdown.
guidance.notWhen: For the CONTENT of an indexed file (state files in any one harness), use `docs:get` — context-aware: when called inside a harness it serves that harness's content. For wiki-style backlinks (`[[name]]` references), use `wiki:backlinks`. This tool's unique value is the cross-harness sweep in one call.

tools.name: harness:membership
tools.description: List / add / remove / move which workspaces a harness belongs to. Registry edits only — never touches the harness folder or its run data.

guidance.when: User asks to move a harness to another workspace, share/link a harness into a second workspace, see which workspaces a harness is in, or remove a harness from a workspace. op=list reads; op=add/remove/move mutate.
guidance.notWhen: To CREATE a brand-new harness from a folder/repo, use the harness create flow (POST /api/harness/projects), not this — membership only links/moves harnesses that already exist somewhere.

tools.name: harness:migrate-config-json
tools.description: One-time backfill (deprecate-harness-config-json-2026-06-06): lift every harness's legacy `.papercusp/config.json` INSTANCE content (phase/phases/dept + per-instance knob overrides) into the workspace-PG registry, so the file is no longer read as a config source. Idempotent — already-migrated / file-less harnesses are skipped; scaffold contract artifacts (harness_token/parent_slug/slug) are left in the file. Returns {ok, scanned, migratedCount, results:[{slug,fields}]}.

guidance.when: Once per workspace after the config.json→PG cutover, to lift any pre-existing harness config.json instance content into the registry. Safe to re-run (idempotent).
guidance.notWhen: Routine operation — this is a one-time backfill. New harnesses persist instance config to PG directly; nothing reads config.json on the live path.

tools.name: harness:overview
tools.description: One 'state of X' read: a harness's status + escalations (with `harness`) or the harness index (without), PLUS the cross-cutting open-issues snapshot — harness:list / harness:status / issues:list / harness:escalation in ONE round-trip instead of four.

guidance.when: Answering "what's the state of X" / "what's going on" — pass `harness` for one harness's status + escalations + open issues, or omit it for the harness index + open issues, in one round-trip instead of harness:list + harness:status + issues:list + harness:escalation.
guidance.notWhen: You need one harness in full detail (harness:status / harness:get), one issue (issues:get), or a topic-filtered issue sweep (issues:list { topic }). Do NOT call it in a loop over every harness — pass the one slug you care about.
guidance.chaining: Bundles: harness:status + harness:escalation [+ harness:list] + issues:list — prefer this over calling them separately. → issues:get / issues:claim a problem it surfaces.

tools.name: harness:pending_reviews
tools.description: List unresolved pending-review entries for a harness slug (optionally per phase).

guidance.when: User asks "anything pending review?", "what needs my approval?". The dedicated tool for plan-review state.
guidance.notWhen: For open ISSUES (problems, bugs), use `issues:list`. For all pending hook events, use `pending_events:list`.

tools.name: harness:phase_path
tools.description: Resolve the on-disk path for a (harness_slug, phase) pair. Phase = staging|testing|production.

guidance.when: You need the absolute filesystem path for a harness phase before reading files inside it.
guidance.notWhen: For listing files INSIDE the phase dir, use `harness:markdown_index` or `harness:list_features`. This tool only resolves the dir path.

tools.name: harness:status
tools.description:
When to use: User asks "what is harness X doing right now?", "is sheets active?", or you need recent-activity counts + phase.

When NOT to use: For "what's WRONG with X", use `issues:list` (problems-side view). For static facts about the harness, use `harness:get`.

guidance.when: User asks "what is harness X doing right now?", "is sheets active?", or you need recent-activity counts + phase.
guidance.notWhen: For "what's WRONG with X", use `issues:list` (problems-side view). For static facts about the harness, use `harness:get`.

tools.name: harness_docs:anchor
tools.description: Anchor one OR many manual docs to the code they document (their subject_ref) so drift is tracked; optionally verify against HEAD. Single: { docId, documents? }. Many: items:[{ docId, documents?, verify?, title?, harness? }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, docId, source?, status?, anchored?, subjectRef? | error }], counts } — correlate by docId not position; one failure never fails the rest. Unanchored manual docs remain allowed but flagged "not drift-tracked".

guidance.when: A human-authored doc should be drift-tracked: declare what code it covers. Run after writing/editing the doc, or to fix a wrong anchor. Anchor several at once via items:[…].
guidance.notWhen: For a generated doc use harness_docs:record (it sets a generated baseline). To only re-confirm currency use harness_docs:verify.
guidance.chaining: harness_docs:anchor { documents } → (later, on a drift nudge) harness_docs:verify.

tools.name: harness_docs:ingest
tools.description: Backfill a harness's existing FS docs into the typed drift-tracked model: anchor docs that declare/imply a subject as manual records (baselined to HEAD). One-time per harness; idempotent.

guidance.when: After this harness has existing docs/*.md that predate the typed model, to make the ones with a declared/inferable subject drift-tracked.
guidance.notWhen: Record-less docs already show as "not drift-tracked" via the merged read — ingest is only needed to anchor docs that declare a subject. No need to run repeatedly.
guidance.chaining: harness_docs:ingest → harness_docs:list (review which anchored) → harness_docs:anchor (fix any wrong/missing anchors).

tools.name: harness_docs:list
tools.description: List a harness's merged docs (generated · manual · augmented) with source badges + drift status (fresh/stale/review/untracked), and the active doc's body + augmented overlay. Supersedes the FS-only project-docs read.

guidance.when: You want a harness's project docs WITH provenance + freshness — which are generated vs human, which are stale, which are not drift-tracked.
