guidance.notWhen: For Papercusp framework docs use docs:get/outline. For raw markdown without metadata the old project-docs endpoint still exists but is superseded.
guidance.chaining: harness_docs:list → harness_docs:regenerate (stale generated) / harness_docs:verify (stale manual) / harness_docs:set_overlay (add human nuance).

tools.name: harness_docs:record
tools.description: Record one OR many generated docs' provenance + drift anchor (subject_ref) and stamp each generated-from the harness repo's current HEAD. Single: { docId, documents? }. Many: items:[{ docId, documents?, title?, harness? }]. Call immediately after writing the file(s), passing what you read. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, docId, source?, status?, generatedFromSha?, subjectRef?, anchorPaths? | error }], counts } — correlate by docId not position; one failure never fails the rest.

guidance.when: You (the documenter) just wrote or refreshed generated doc file(s) (docs/features/F-<id>.md, a guide). Call once per doc with the feature + the exact files/symbols you read; record several at once via items:[…].
guidance.notWhen: For a human-authored manual doc, use harness_docs:anchor instead (it sets a verify baseline, not a generated baseline). Do not call for docs you only read.
guidance.chaining: Write the .md file(s) → harness_docs:record { docId, documents } (or items:[…]). The freshness sweep then tracks them against future commits.

tools.name: harness_docs:regenerate
tools.description: Request a documenter regeneration of one OR many stale generated/augmented docs (preserving any human overlay). Single: { docId }. Many same harness: { docIds:[…] }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ docId, harness? }]. Each enqueues; the doc refreshes when the documenter re-records it. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, docId, enqueued? | error }], counts } — correlate by docId not position; one failure never fails the rest.

guidance.when: A generated doc is stale (its subject code changed) and you want it refreshed. Regenerate several at once via docIds:[…] or items:[…].
guidance.notWhen: For a manual doc use harness_docs:verify. To preserve human nuance across the regen, add it via harness_docs:set_overlay first.
guidance.chaining: harness_docs:list (find stale generated) → harness_docs:regenerate { docIds:[…] }.

tools.name: harness_docs:set_overlay
tools.description: Attach a human "augmented" overlay to one OR many docs — nuance that rides on top of the generated body and survives regeneration; empty string clears it. Single: { docId, overlay }. Many: items:[{ docId, overlay, harness? }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, docId, source?, hasOverlay? | error }], counts } — correlate by docId not position; one failure never fails the rest.

guidance.when: A generated doc is accurate but missing the human "why"/caveats you want preserved across regenerations. Add it as an overlay rather than hand-editing the generated body (which a regen would lose). Set several at once via items:[…].
guidance.notWhen: To change the generated body itself, fix the code/feature and regenerate. For a fully human doc, author it as a manual doc.
guidance.chaining: harness_docs:list → harness_docs:set_overlay { overlay } (or items:[…]).

tools.name: harness_docs:verify
tools.description: Re-verify one OR many manual docs: stamp the drift baseline to the current HEAD and mark fresh. Single: { docId }. Many same harness: { docIds:[…] }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ docId, harness? }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, docId, verifiedSha? | error }], counts } — correlate by docId not position; one failure never fails the rest. Use after reviewing a doc the freshness sweep flagged for re-verify.

guidance.when: A manual doc was flagged for re-verify (its subject code changed) and you confirmed it's still accurate — or you just edited it to match. Verify several at once via docIds:[…] or items:[…].
guidance.notWhen: For a generated doc use harness_docs:regenerate. To set the anchor in the first place use harness_docs:anchor.
guidance.chaining: harness_docs:list (find review docs) → read → harness_docs:verify { docIds:[…] }.

tools.name: hive:add-member
tools.description: Wire an existing harness in as a MEMBER of a local Hive (sets its hive_slug so its work federates within the Hive and surfaces in the Queen's member-scoped hive:survey). Registry edit only — never moves the harness folder or run data; best-effort seeds the member's git-sync routine. Idempotent (re-adding is a no-op success). Use this to remediate a member-less Hive whose Queen surveys workspace-wide and escalates out-of-scope debris.

guidance.when: A Hive has no members so hive:survey falls back to workspace-wide scope (frontier empty / Queen-unresolvable escalations) — wire the real harness in. Also the producer for shared-hive federation membership.
guidance.notWhen: Adding a person/device to a Hive (that is admission, a separate concern). Removing a member (re-point via the registry / hive:leave for a joined remote hive). Nesting a Hive home as a member (rejected — Hives compose as peers).
guidance.chaining: hive:list / hive:get to find the Hive home + the member slug → hive:add-member → hive:start (or hive:wake) so the Queen surveys the now-scoped frontier → hive:survey to confirm members[] is non-empty + scope is hive-local.

tools.name: hive:ask
tools.description: Initiate a cross-Hive ASK to a peer Hive (by pubkey): a question the peer Hive owns the answer to. The envelope is signed, sent store-and-forward, and recorded in this Hive's ask ledger; the peer's answer arrives asynchronously — events:await the returned answeredEvent key. Requires an outbound grant to the peer.

guidance.when: The Queen/owner needs an answer another Hive is the authority on (it owns that domain). Find the peer via discovery:hives, then hive:ask, then events:await the returned answeredEvent.
guidance.notWhen: Handing the peer WORK to do (use hive:request_work). Within-Hive questions (coord:ask / conversations). Granting a peer to send asks INTO this Hive (that is the inbound hive:cross_grant).
guidance.chaining: discovery:hives (find the peer Hive pubkey) → hive:ask { hive, peerHivePubkey, subject, body } → events:await { event: <answeredEvent> }. Review outstanding asks with hive:asks.

tools.name: hive:asks
tools.description: List this Hive's cross-Hive ask ledger: the requests it initiated to peer Hives (and inbound ones with direction:'in'), with each row's peer, kind, subject, correlation id, state (queued|sent|answered|declined|expired) and reply. Filter by state / direction / peer / kind.

guidance.when: Reviewing the status of cross-Hive asks/work-requests — what is still pending, what was answered/declined — or deduping before initiating a new ask to a peer that already owns one.
guidance.notWhen: Inbound admission policy (hive:cross_grant list shows who may send INTO this Hive). Within-Hive work status (work_items:* / harness:status). Blocking on one specific pending ask (events:await its answeredEvent — do not poll this list).
guidance.chaining: hive:ask / hive:request_work create rows here; hive:asks { hive, state: "answered" } reviews the replies.

tools.name: hive:ban_member
tools.description: OWNER bans a member for repeat abuse: records the ban in the owner-signed policy (denies re-join, keyed on the stable github id) AND revokes their devices (write-block now; a READ cut-off at the next C-001 re-key epoch). Pass unban:true to lift. Requires holding the Hive key. revoke:false bans (policy-only) without revoking.

guidance.when: A member is a confirmed repeat abuser (see hive:moderation_queue) and you (the owner) want them removed AND unable to re-join.
guidance.notWhen: Hiding one piece of content — that is hive:takedown. Revoking your OWN device — substrate:revoke_self_device.
guidance.chaining: hive:moderation_queue → hive:ban_member → hive:moderation_resolve (mark actioned). The read cut-off completes when the C-001 re-key op-path lands.

tools.name: hive:beacon_consent
tools.description: Manage whether THIS Hive publishes a live status beacon (active agents, queue depth, focus, last-completed) onto the directory gossip — the owner-consent gate, default-OFF (D-002). Pass `consent` to set it (true = publish, false = stop); omit `consent` to read the current state. The consent federates to every Swarm of the Hive and gates B-06's beacon publisher. The beacon only rides a PUBLISHED (public/invite) hive's re-announce — enabling it on a private hive has no effect until the hive is published.

guidance.when: Enabling, disabling, or checking this Hive's status-beacon publishing — the same consent the desktop publish-flow asks for, managed from the agent surface. Pass consent:true to opt a published hive into the beacon, consent:false to withdraw it, or omit consent to read the current value.
guidance.notWhen: Directory visibility (public/invite/private) — that's discovery:set_hive. Cross-Hive ask/work-request grants — hive:cross_grant. Within-Hive coordination — coord:* / topics.
guidance.chaining: discovery:set_hive { visibility:'public' } (make the hive discoverable) → hive:beacon_consent { hive, consent:true } (opt the now-public hive into the live beacon).

tools.name: hive:control_policy
tools.description: Read or set the hive placement-watchdog thresholds: breakerThreshold (failed placements → cursed-item breaker), recoveryDebounceMs (min gap between recovery wakes for one stalled unit), dormancyGraceMs (post-dormancy recovery-sweep grace), infraBreakerThreshold (bounded infra-loss breaker). Replaces the PAPERCUSP_HIVE_PLACEMENT_* env gates; set is audited + one-call-revertible.

guidance.when: Tune the placement watchdog live — e.g. raise breakerThreshold to give a flapping unit more recovery attempts before cursing it, or shorten recoveryDebounceMs to re-place stalled work faster during an incident.
guidance.notWhen: For placement AFFINITY weights use hive:set-steering (D-005). For stale-claim reclaim use work_items:reclaim_config; for session reaping use coord:session_reaper_config.
guidance.chaining: config:list-overrides shows the active override; config:reset-overrides reverts it.

tools.name: hive:create
tools.description: Stand up a NEW local hive (root-only): provision a home harness running the hive (kind:'hive') blueprint, stamp it harness_kind:'hive', and optionally wake the Queen. Composes the harness-provision primitives + hive:wake, transactional with rollback. NOT callable from a bee/parented agent — hives are peers, never nested. Cloud placement is a separate step (deploy:hive).

guidance.when: Standing up a NEW local hive (its home harness + Queen) in one call. Operator/user only.
guidance.notWhen: Deploying an EXISTING hive to a cloud frame — deploy:hive. A plain non-hive harness — harness:create. From a bee — not allowed (spin a kind:harness subharness instead).
guidance.chaining: hive:get { slug } to inspect; hive:declare-wake to set the cadence; deploy:hive to place it on a Swarm; hive:dissolve to tear it down.

tools.name: hive:create_from_repo
tools.description: Create a Hive FROM a GitHub URL: repo→Hive lookup first (an existing Hive returns a JOIN OFFER, zero side effects), then clone, blueprint detect + test-verify, Hive home + first member harness, upstream coords stamped, auto-publish. Visibility is derived from the repo: public repo → discoverable directory listing; private repo → Private (invite-only, hidden, secret-gated). Returns {ok, existing?} or {ok, created:{hiveSlug, memberSlug, memberPath}, publish}.

guidance.when: Onboarding a GitHub repository as a NEW Hive in one call — the paste-a-URL creation flow. Also the backend the CreateHarnessPicker GitHub-URL entry drives.
guidance.notWhen: The repo may already have a Hive and you only want the answer — lookup happens inside, but a read-only check is the picker flow. An existing LOCAL repo — harness:generate-from-repo. A repo-less hive — hive:create. Adding a repo into an EXISTING hive — harness:create { hive } after cloning (the into-hive picker mode).
guidance.chaining: hive:create_from_repo { githubUrl } → on {existing} drive the join (POST /api/harness/join-link per member link) → on {created} hive:get / discovery:set_hive to edit the listing.

tools.name: hive:cross_grant
tools.description: Owner-managed cross-Hive grants: grant/revoke/list which peer-Hive pubkeys may exchange which kinds (ask | work-request) with this Hive. DIRECTED: 'in' admits a peer's traffic INTO this Hive; 'out' lets THIS Hive send to a peer (required before the Queen can ask another Hive). Default-deny both ways; grants are quota-capped (maxPerHour/maxBodyBytes, defaults 60/hr + 64KiB), optionally expiring (expiresInHours), and federate to all of this Hive's Swarms.

guidance.when: Setting this Hive's cross-Hive policy — grant 'in' (admission) or 'out' (egress; owner-gated before the Queen's first hive:ask to a new peer), list, or revoke. maxPerHour/maxBodyBytes/expiresInHours tune quota/expiry.
guidance.notWhen: Within-Hive coordination (coord:*/topics) or Swarm work placement (work_items:co_locate) — this is only the sovereignty boundary between Hives.
guidance.chaining: discovery:hives (peer pubkey) → hive:cross_grant {action:"grant", direction, peerHivePubkey, kinds}; "out" before hive:ask / hive:request_work.

tools.name: hive:declare-wake
tools.description: Declare the Hive operator's next wake (REPLACE semantics — omitted parts are cleared): a time (`at` ISO / `inSeconds`), event subscriptions (`events: [{on, when?, note?}]`), both, or nothing (`mode:'none'`). The time is clamped to a wake floor; event wakes fire hive:wake when the subscribed tool-event matches.

guidance.when: You are the hive/operator ending a turn — ALWAYS declare your next wake (a time, events, or explicitly none). Also when the user asks to schedule or re-schedule the operator.
guidance.notWhen: To fire the hive right now — that is hive:wake.
guidance.chaining: hive:status to inspect the current declaration; hive:wake for an immediate manual fire.

tools.name: hive:dissolve
tools.description: Tear down a local hive (root-only, destructive — pass confirm:true): clear the Queen's wake so she won't re-wake, cancel every live bee + its subtree, and deregister the home harness. Optionally drop the harness PG schema (default keep). Idempotent. Does NOT destroy a deployed cloud frame — that is deploy:teardown_hive.

guidance.when: Permanently tearing down a local hive — stop the Queen, cancel its bees, deregister it. Operator/user only.
guidance.notWhen: Destroying a deployed cloud frame (the Queen/member execution planes) — deploy:teardown_hive. Pausing a hive without tearing down — hive:declare-wake { mode:none }. From a bee — not allowed.
guidance.chaining: hive:get { slug } to inspect before; deploy:teardown_hive first if the hive is deployed to a Swarm.

tools.name: hive:get
tools.description: The full state of one hive: its home harness + deployment + wake schedule (scheduled?, next/last fire, event subscriptions), its live bees with {doing, queued, load}, and its todo-work frontier depth. Composes resolveHive + fleet:assignments + work_items — the one call for "how is hive X doing".

guidance.when: You want one hive in depth: is the Queen scheduled to wake, who are the bees and how loaded, how much work is queued.
guidance.notWhen: A list of all hives — hive:list. The raw per-agent fleet view across the workspace — fleet:assignments.
guidance.chaining: hive:list to find the slug; hive:wake to fire the Queen now; hive:declare-wake to change the cadence; hive:dissolve to tear it down.

tools.name: hive:get-steering
tools.description: Read the current owner steering for the Hive — the focus `directive`, `eligiblePlans` (plans the Queen may pick up now), and pause state (`pauseNewWork` / `pausedUntil`) the Queen reads on every wake. An un-steered Hive returns the default (no directive, no plan restriction, not paused). The READ twin of hive:set-steering.

guidance.when: Checking what the Queen is currently steered toward — before changing it, or to confirm a hive:set-steering write landed.
guidance.notWhen: Changing steering — hive:set-steering. Reading the whole hive status — hive:status.

tools.name: hive:leave
tools.description: Leave a shared hive you JOINED (root-only, pass confirm:true): stop federating (leave the swarm topic), delete the member git-sync routines, drop local presence rows, and deregister the remote_hive view + its member clones. Idempotent + best-effort. Clone dirs are kept by default — deleteClones:true also removes them. NOT for a local hive you own — that is hive:dissolve.

guidance.when: A joiner cleanly leaving a shared hive they joined — stop federating, deregister the joined view + members, kill their git-sync routines. Operator/user only.
guidance.notWhen: Tearing down a LOCAL hive you OWN (stop its Queen, cancel its bees) — hive:dissolve. Pausing federation without leaving — there is no pause; leave + re-join. From a bee — not allowed.
guidance.chaining: hive:list / hive:get to find the joined hive (remote_hive) view slug before; re-join via the hive directory join flow if you change your mind.

tools.name: hive:list
tools.description: The workspace-local hives (kind:'hive' harnesses — the Hives): each with its home slug, deployment target, wake (scheduled? next/last fire), and a live-agent count. The local-lifecycle view; for joinable network hives use discovery:hives, for per-bee placement detail use fleet:assignments, for one hive in depth use hive:get.

guidance.when: You want the workspace-local hives (the Hives) and their wake/load at a glance.
guidance.notWhen: Browsing joinable hives across the P2P network — that is discovery:hives. The raw per-agent fleet view — fleet:assignments. One hive in depth — hive:get.
guidance.chaining: hive:get { slug } to drill into one; hive:create to add one; hive:dissolve to tear one down.

tools.name: hive:membership_decide
tools.description: OWNER decision on a pending-join request: approve (trust-admit the joiner + their captured devices) or deny (never admitted). Requires this Swarm to hold the Hive key (the owning Swarm). The approval flips a pending joiner into the trust set and federates; a denial is final until the owner approves later.

guidance.when: A joiner is pending under approval-mode membership (see hive:membership_pending) and you (the owner) want to admit or reject them.
guidance.notWhen: Banning an already-admitted member for abuse — use hive:ban_member (revoke + re-key teeth). Setting the membership mode itself — that is hive policy.
guidance.chaining: hive:membership_pending (review the queue) → hive:membership_decide (per joiner).

tools.name: hive:membership_pending
tools.description: List a Hive's pending-join requests (the approval-mode admission queue). Under membership:'approval' a joiner stays pending until the owner approves; this is the owner's review queue. Read-only — decide with hive:membership_decide.

guidance.when: The Hive's membership policy is 'approval' and you (the owner) want to see who's waiting to join. Pair with hive:membership_decide to approve/deny.
guidance.notWhen: For the trust roster (already-admitted members) use hive:get / harness:membership. Setting the membership MODE is hive policy (the policy authoring surface), not this.
guidance.chaining: hive:membership_pending (review) → hive:membership_decide (approve/deny each).

tools.name: hive:moderation_queue
tools.description: The owner's moderation queue — list member-filed reports for a Hive (default the open ones). Read-only. Act on a report with hive:moderation_resolve (action/dismiss), hive:takedown (hide content), or hive:ban_member.

guidance.when: You (the owner) want to review reports members filed via hive:report.
guidance.notWhen: Filing a report (that is hive:report, member-side).
guidance.chaining: hive:moderation_queue → hive:takedown / hive:ban_member / hive:moderation_resolve.

tools.name: hive:moderation_resolve
tools.description: OWNER resolves a moderation report: 'actioned' (you took action — e.g. a takedown/ban) or 'dismissed' (no action). Federates the resolution back. Requires holding the Hive key. Does NOT itself hide content or ban — use hive:takedown / hive:ban_member for that.

guidance.when: You reviewed a report (hive:moderation_queue) and want to mark it resolved.
guidance.notWhen: You want to actually hide content (hive:takedown) or ban a member (hive:ban_member) — do that first, then resolve.
guidance.chaining: hive:moderation_queue → (hive:takedown / hive:ban_member) → hive:moderation_resolve.

tools.name: hive:pause
tools.description: PAUSE the hive: persist hive_started=false (disarms the liveness watchdog), set the global wake-mode to manual (autonomous wakes are STAGED for review instead of firing — the one freeze seam, D-005), and clear the Queen's pending time wake. Optionally drain live bees gracefully. Resume with hive:start.

guidance.when: The user clicks Pause Hive / asks to freeze autonomous operation, or you need the colony quiet (incident, review, cost control).
guidance.notWhen: To stop ONE bee — fleet:drain / fleet:cancel. To pause one plan — plans:pause. Pausing does not kill running turns; they finish and their follow-on wakes stage.
guidance.chaining: hive:pause { drainBees:true } for the harder stop → coord:wake-queue to review staged wakes → hive:start to resume.

tools.name: hive:queen_efficiency
tools.description: The Queen's per-wake prompt efficiency: cache-hit ratio (Win-1 frozen-prefix cache), avg turns/wake (Win-2 round-trip elimination), token + cost totals, and cachedWakes (the 'cache is real' signal, P-003). Scoped to a hive home, or workspace-wide when no harness is given. Read-only.

guidance.when: To inspect the LIVE Queen's per-wake efficiency — is the frozen-prefix cache paying off (cacheHitRatio / cachedWakes) and is the precomputed brief cutting round-trips (avgTurns)? The B-06 measurement read.
guidance.notWhen: For a SCENARIO run’s efficiency score — that is the hive-eval efficiency class (it scores these per run). This tool is the ad-hoc live-Queen read.
guidance.chaining: hive:status for wake/placement state; hive:survey for the frontier.

tools.name: hive:report
tools.description: File a moderation report against content or a member in a Hive. The report federates to the owner's moderation queue. Requires the owner to have enabled reporting (moderation.reportable in the Hive policy); otherwise reporting is off and this no-ops.

guidance.when: You are a member of a Hive with reporting enabled and want to flag abusive content or a member to the owner.
guidance.notWhen: You ARE the owner taking action — use hive:takedown (hide content) / hive:ban_member (ban a member). Reporting is the member→owner signal, not the owner action.
guidance.chaining: hive:report (member flags) → owner reviews hive:moderation_queue → hive:moderation_resolve / hive:takedown / hive:ban_member.

tools.name: hive:request_work
tools.description: Initiate a cross-Hive WORK-REQUEST to a peer Hive (by pubkey): ask the peer to do something in its domain. The envelope is signed, sent store-and-forward, and recorded in this Hive's ask ledger; it becomes a work_item in the peer's backlog that THEIR Queen prioritizes. The peer's response arrives asynchronously — events:await the returned answeredEvent key. Requires an outbound grant to the peer.

guidance.when: The Queen/owner wants a peer Hive to take on a piece of work in its domain. Find the peer via discovery:hives, then hive:request_work, then events:await the returned answeredEvent.
guidance.notWhen: Asking a QUESTION (use hive:ask). Placing work on your OWN Swarm (work_items:* / fleet:*). Granting a peer to send work-requests INTO this Hive (that is the inbound hive:cross_grant).
guidance.chaining: discovery:hives (find the peer Hive pubkey) → hive:request_work { hive, peerHivePubkey, subject, body } → events:await { event: <answeredEvent> }. Review outstanding requests with hive:asks.

tools.name: hive:set-steering
tools.description: Set the owner steering the Queen reads on every wake (the 👑 Queen tab writes through this): a focus `directive`, `eligiblePlans` / `eligibleHives` (what she may pick up + the placement scope NOW — eligibility ≠ lifecycle status), `pauseNewWork`/`pausedUntil`, and the P-006 THROTTLE knobs (`cadenceFloorSec`, `maxBees`, `idleActivities`, `autoScaleOut`, `modelTiers`/`tierCeilings`, `decomposition`) — each a SESSION override of a live operator seam. Writes the owner-steering:* hive_settings, refreshes the panel, AND wakes the Queen so the change takes effect immediately. `clear:true` wipes all steering; omitted fields are unchanged (null/[] clears one field). See each arg description for detail.

guidance.when: Steering the Queen from the owner surface — focus her on specific plans, give a directive, or pause new work (incident / cost / review). The 👑 Queen tab is the UI for this.
guidance.notWhen: Freezing the WHOLE hive (all autonomous wakes) — hive:pause. Per-plan lifecycle (draft/ready/shipped) — plans:*. Stopping ONE bee — fleet:drain / fleet:cancel.
guidance.chaining: hive:set-steering { eligiblePlans:[...], directive:"only these plans" } → the Queen wakes + honours it next placement. hive:set-steering { pauseNewWork:true } → she drives existing work to terminal then idles. hive:get-steering reads the current state; clear:true resets.

tools.name: hive:start
tools.description: START the hive (the global control, distinct from a per-plan Start): persist hive_started=true, re-affirm the Queen's default event-wake subscriptions (plan-started / work-item-created / escalation), set the global wake-mode to auto, and wake the Queen now (floor-debounced). The liveness watchdog holds "a wake is always armed" from here until hive:pause.

guidance.when: The user clicks Start Hive / asks to boot the colony, or you are bringing a paused hive back to autonomous operation.
guidance.notWhen: To wake the Queen once without changing the started state — hive:wake. To start one plan — plans:start. To create a hive — hive:create.
guidance.chaining: hive:status to verify (started, subscriptions, next wake); hive:pause to suspend.

tools.name: hive:status
tools.description: The Hive operator's current state: started/paused (the Start-Hive bit), the pending time wake (one-shot routine), event subscriptions + live rule ids, last wake, the floor, and the watchdog health signal (fallback fires in 24h). Read-only.

guidance.when: To see when/whether the operator will wake next, or to verify a hive:declare-wake landed.
guidance.chaining: hive:declare-wake to change the declaration; hive:wake to fire now.

tools.name: hive:survey
tools.description: The Queen's plan-aware placement survey: started plans ranked (which plan to pour bees into) AND the unplaced work-item frontier ranked (which ready item to place), across EVERY member harness — one ranker, two views. Read-only; call it at the top of a placement wake.

guidance.when: You are the Queen starting a placement wake — survey what to work on next (which plan matters, which ready items to place) across all member harnesses.
guidance.notWhen: You already hold a specific work-item id and just need to place it — go straight to fleet:spawn / the batch placement.
guidance.chaining: hive:survey → place the top frontier items (fleet:spawn / batch placement) and steer plan order (work_items:set_priority / plans:set-priority); hive:status to inspect the wake declaration.

tools.name: hive:takedown
tools.description: OWNER takedown: hide a piece of content across the Hive by adding its ref to the owner-signed moderation.takedownList (re-signed + federated; honest peers honor it as a tombstone, no resurrection). Pass restore:true to un-hide. Requires holding the Hive key.

guidance.when: A member reported content (hive:moderation_queue) that you (the owner) want hidden on every honest peer.
guidance.notWhen: Banning the AUTHOR for repeat abuse — that is hive:ban_member (revoke + re-key teeth). Takedown hides content; ban removes a member.
guidance.chaining: hive:moderation_queue → hive:takedown (hide) → hive:moderation_resolve (mark actioned).

tools.name: hive:update
tools.description: Edit a hive's config: its deployment target (execution plane) and per-instance config overrides (maxCostUsd, parallelWorkers, …). A thin registry writer — no agent-lifecycle effects (never wakes/cancels). Cannot change harness_kind (a hive cannot reclassify). Root-only.

guidance.when: Changing a hive's deployment target or its per-instance config overrides (budget/parallelism knobs).
guidance.notWhen: Waking/pausing the Queen — hive:wake / hive:declare-wake. Placing/removing bees — fleet:*. Deploying to a cloud frame — deploy:hive.
guidance.chaining: hive:get { slug } to see the current config; deploy:hive to act on a changed deployment target.

tools.name: hive:wake
tools.description: Fire the Hive operator immediately (launches the hive blueprint via the invoke route). Floor-debounced: a wake within the floor window of the previous one is skipped unless force:true. The target of event-wake reaction rules and the manual user override.

guidance.when: The user asks to wake/kick the operator now, or an event-wake rule fires (it targets this tool automatically).
guidance.notWhen: To schedule a future wake — that is hive:declare-wake.
guidance.chaining: hive:status to see the last/next wake; hive:declare-wake to schedule.

tools.name: hooks:known
tools.description: Static well-known hook-event allowlist (kernel set; plugin-registered hooks extend this).

guidance.when: Static enum of supported hook event names — use to validate an event string before firing or registering for it.
guidance.notWhen: For PENDING events queued up, use `pending_events:list`. For firing an event, use `plugins:fire_event`.

tools.name: improvements:capture
tools.description: Capture a papercusp improvement you discovered (a friction, a missing affordance, a bug in the tooling) as a durable, claimable, `papercusp-improvement`-tagged work-unit. kind=bug → auto-implement-eligible later; change|feature → human-reviewed. Search-first: declines an obvious duplicate (link to it instead) unless force. Pass `paths` when you know the files involved — it feeds the protected-path safety gate. Pass lane:"observation" for a turn-end-reflection PRE-IDEA — it files into a separate lane that NEVER enters the work queue (Scout-digest + the Observations pane only).

guidance.when: You hit a papercusp DX / tooling / code friction worth fixing but out of your current scope. File it here so it lands in the triage backlog instead of being lost. Use kind=bug for something broken, kind=change for a desired improvement, kind=feature for net-new (the last two stay human-gated). Include `paths` (repo-relative files involved) when known — the auto-implement risk gate reads them.
guidance.notWhen: A problem in a MANAGED harness/project (not papercusp itself) — that is issues:create with that harness scope. Something needing real design — write a plan (plans:new) and capture with kind=feature linking it. A passing question — coord:ask.
guidance.chaining: improvements:capture { kind, title, paths? } → (later) improvements:digest triages it → an agent claims + fixes it self/inline, or the auto-implement loop picks up the bugs and improvements:resolve closes them.

tools.name: improvements:digest
tools.description: Triage the captured papercusp-improvement backlog: scores + dedups every improvement work-unit and splits it into the auto-eligible lane (kind=bug, no protected surface) vs the human-review queue. Read-only — surfaces the queue, implements nothing. (P-010) Supports per-Hive scope filtering.

guidance.when: To review the papercusp self-improvement backlog — what is captured, what is auto-eligible vs needs a human, and which items look like duplicates to merge. The human-facing triage view. (P-010) Pass harnessSlug to filter to a specific Hive's ideas.
guidance.notWhen: You want one improvement in full — issues:get { id }. You want to file one — improvements:capture. You want to browse another area — topics:feed { topic }.
guidance.chaining: improvements:digest → issues:get / issues:claim on a queued item → fix it self/inline (or improvements:capture to add more).

tools.name: improvements:keyless-digest
tools.description: Triage surface for KEYLESS improvement items (no payload.watchdogKey — manual / non-watchdog EIs) — the un-managed backlog that never dedups, ages, or auto-closes. Returns the keyed-vs-keyless headline split, age-band rollup (fresh < 7d · aging 7–30d · stale ≥ 30d), and the review queue (keyless EIs ≥ 7d, oldest-first) with a per-item disposition (claim-or-close / follow-up-owner). Read-only — closes nothing; surfaces the pile so a human/Queen can drain it (P-014).

guidance.when: To see and triage the un-managed backlog — the keyless EIs that the watchdog lifecycle (dedup/aging/auto-close) cannot touch because they carry no watchdogKey. Use it as the periodic keyless human-review digest: drain the stale-review queue (claim, close if obsolete, or convert a recurring one to a keyed form).
guidance.notWhen: You want watchdog/auto-implement health — improvements:watchdog-status. You want the full captured (keyed) backlog triage — improvements:digest. You want one item — issues:get.
guidance.chaining: improvements:keyless-digest → for each review item: issues:claim (take it), issues:close (obsolete), or re-file via improvements:capture with a stable key if it is a recurring signal. improvements:watchdog-status surfaces the same keyless headline split.

tools.name: improvements:learning_loops
tools.description: Inspect the self-learning loop routines: per workspace-singleton learning loop (calibration, scout, graduation, iq-battery, …) its routine state — firing / stale (active but not firing) / dark-by-design (frontier, unarmed) / should-be-on-but-dark (an always-on loop gone dark) / absent — plus the @singleton↔legacy double-state. Read-only — the dark-loop visibility surface so a built-but-never-armed loop does not rot unseen.

guidance.when: To answer "which learning loops are dark / wedged / never armed?" — the standing health of the self-learning machinery (calibration sweep, scout, graduation, gym, iq-battery, …). Catches the recurring class: a loop seeded inactive behind a default-OFF flag that nobody armed, an always-on loop that wedged (stopped firing), or a @singleton↔legacy migration collision.
guidance.notWhen: For the watchdog tick health + auto-implement dispatch ledger use improvements:watchdog-status. For the captured backlog use improvements:digest.
guidance.chaining: improvements:learning_loops → (a dark frontier loop) the per-lane arming runbook; (a should-be-on-but-dark / stale loop) investigate the routine then improvements:capture.

tools.name: improvements:resolve
tools.description: Close the loop on a captured papercusp improvement you worked: outcome `fixed` (requires testsRun — the verification evidence) marks it resolved so it leaves the queue; `could-not-fix` releases it for a retry (exhausted retries route to a human); `needs-human` routes it to the human queue permanently.

guidance.when: You finished working a dispatched/claimed improvement (usually as the implement worker). Fixed + tests green → outcome fixed with the evidence. Could not make it work → could-not-fix with what you tried. The fix would touch a protected surface (operator-core safety / deploy machinery / a migration) or needs judgment → needs-human.
guidance.notWhen: You only want to comment progress — issues:comment. You are closing a non-improvement issue — issues:close. The item was never captured (no EI/WI id) — improvements:capture it first if it is worth tracking.
guidance.chaining: improvements:digest → (dispatch/claim) → implement + test → improvements:resolve { id, outcome, summary, testsRun }.

tools.name: improvements:set-auto-policy
tools.description: Read or set the auto-implement risk policy: autoKinds (the bug→change→feature graduation dial), maxPerRun / maxAttempts (dispatch ceilings), and TIGHTEN-ONLY protected-path/keyword additions (the baked TCB floor is unioned + never removable — no remove op by design, D-002). Inert until the IMPROVEMENT_AUTO_IMPLEMENT flag is armed; audited + one-call-revertible.

guidance.when: Graduate the auto-implement lane (widen autoKinds as trust is earned), tune the dispatch rate (maxPerRun/maxAttempts), or ADD a path/keyword to the never-auto protected set — live, no redeploy.
guidance.notWhen: To REMOVE a baked protection (impossible by design — D-002 tighten-only). To arm auto-implement itself, flip FLAGS.IMPROVEMENT_AUTO_IMPLEMENT via /admin/features (this only configures the policy). To triage the queue, use improvements:digest.
guidance.chaining: improvements:digest shows the auto/human partition under the current policy; config:list-overrides shows the active override; config:reset-overrides reverts it.

tools.name: improvements:set-watchdog-tunables
tools.description: Live-tune the improvement-watchdog's collector bars + per-tick caps (its payload_template tunables) without a deploy. `get` reads the current standing tunables; `set` merges a patch through the control harness (dryRun preview, post-apply verify+auto-revert, audit, one-call revert). Keys are the watchdog PAYLOAD_TUNABLE_KEYS (e.g. transientMinCount, maxPerTick, structuralMinRate).

guidance.when: A watchdog collector is too noisy or too quiet on a running fleet (e.g. raise transientMinCount during a flaky-infra window, or lower a min-count to capture more) and you want to retune it live instead of poking the routine payload by hand or editing code.
guidance.notWhen: To turn the watchdog on/off (flip its routine `active` — autoloop/routine control). To READ what it last captured, use improvements:watchdog-status. This tool tunes the payload layer; the maxPerTick env override still wins at tick time.
guidance.chaining: improvements:watchdog-status to see current capture behavior; set with dryRun:true to preview the proposed-vs-current diff before applying.

tools.name: improvements:triage
tools.description: Queen-turn triage: route each scored idea by the D-005 taxonomy (product→place; code-bug→the policy tier's lane; infra-environment→owner-escalation; process-prompt→gate/gym; needs-design→plans:new). The risk-tier policy is the one safety verdict — triage adds only routing (D-003). Persists the decision on the idea lifecycle. (P-010) Per-Hive scope filtering.

guidance.when: To triage captured ideas: read the digest summary, walk the human queue in RANK order (the P-040 ranker — triage-all carries each item's rank breakdown), classify by the D-005 taxonomy, decide (place/gate/gym/reject), and record the Queen's judgment. (P-010) Pass harnessSlug for one Hive. mode=retriage-all re-routes the whole open backlog after a taxonomy/policy change.
guidance.notWhen: You want to READ ideas — use improvements:digest. You want to CAPTURE — use improvements:capture. You want implementation status — use improvements:resolve.
guidance.chaining: improvements:triage → work_items:create/update for placed ideas, or coord:escalate for human-gate ideas. A rank breakdown showing a 'calibration' contribution → calibration:summary { predictor } to weigh the bettor's claim before deciding.

tools.name: improvements:watchdog-status
tools.description: Inspect the improvement watchdog: the last N tick records (collector health, signals, captured ids, known-open/stale-resolved pre-filter drops, deferred keys, self-escalations) plus a rollup summary AND the auto-implement dispatch ledger (counts by state + recent dispatches). Read-only — the diagnostic surface over harness_shared.watchdog_ticks + improvement_dispatches.

guidance.when: To check whether the improvement watchdog is running and healthy — when it last ticked, which collectors failed, what it captured vs declined vs deferred, and which standing signals the key pre-filter is dropping. The first stop for "why did/didn't the watchdog file X?" — and for the auto-implement lane's dispatch ledger ("did the dispatch fire / is a worker on it / did it die?").
guidance.notWhen: You want the captured backlog itself — improvements:digest. You want one improvement — issues:get { id }. You want to file one — improvements:capture.
guidance.chaining: improvements:watchdog-status → issues:get on a captured/self-escalated/dispatched id → improvements:digest for the full backlog triage.

tools.name: inbox:triage
tools.description: Triage one attention item (the operator inbox PASS): downgrade a false positive or resolve it → the auditable "Handled by operator" tier; escalate an under-flagged item or confirm a real one → the Decisions tier. Record WHY in `note` (required on downgrade/resolve). The downgrade is always visible + auditable, never a silent vanish.

guidance.when: Operator inbox PASS — run FIRST each wake over the Decisions tier: re-tier an attention item after reading it (downgrade noise, escalate something a worker under-flagged, confirm/resolve a real decision), always recording the why in `note`. Leave the inbox clean before sleeping.
guidance.notWhen: Acting on the item itself (resolve an escalation → coord:resolve; mark a plan item done → plans:set-status). Messaging the owning agent → coord:message-agent.

tools.name: instance:boot
tools.description: Boot a new harness from an InstanceSpec, reproducing the captured instance. Reuses harness:create.

guidance.when: Instantiate a NEW harness identical to a captured InstanceSpec (same blueprint + SHA + deployment + genome).
guidance.notWhen: To create a fresh harness from scratch, use `harness:create`. To clone-and-vary in one call, use `instance:clone`.
guidance.chaining: instance:capture → instance:boot.

tools.name: instance:capture
tools.description: Capture an InstanceSpec (blueprintRef + repoSha + deploymentConfig + genome) from a live harness, for reproducible boot/vary.

guidance.when: Capture a reproducible descriptor of a live harness/instance — its blueprint + git SHA + deployment + genome — to boot or vary an identical one. The replacement for the retired snapshot clone path.
guidance.notWhen: For a full state backup (code+data), git + PG already cover it. To create a fresh harness from scratch, use `harness:create`.
guidance.chaining: instance:capture → instance:boot (identical) or instance:clone (with a genome delta).

tools.name: instance:clone
tools.description: Capture a harness → optionally apply a genome delta → boot an identical / same-origin clone.

guidance.when: Clone a live harness into a new identical one, or a same-origin variant (pass a genomeDelta). The reproducible-clone replacement for the retired snapshot fork.
guidance.notWhen: For a fresh harness from scratch, use `harness:create`. To capture a spec without booting, use `instance:capture`.
guidance.chaining: instance:clone = instance:capture → (vary) → instance:boot in one call.

tools.name: intel:artifacts
tools.description:
When to use: You need the Intel-panel-shaped view of recent artifacts — grouped + summarized for UI display.

When NOT to use: For loading a specific artifact body, use `artifacts:load`. For listing artifacts a tool produced, use the tool's response. intel:artifacts is the panel feed.

guidance.when: You need the Intel-panel-shaped view of recent artifacts — grouped + summarized for UI display.
guidance.notWhen: For loading a specific artifact body, use `artifacts:load`. For listing artifacts a tool produced, use the tool's response. intel:artifacts is the panel feed.

tools.name: intel:spawn_tree
tools.description:
When to use: User asks "what triggered this?", "show me the lineage of agent X", or you need the parent-child spawn graph for an Intel-panel-style view.

When NOT to use: For LIVE running spawns only, use `orchestrator.list_active`. spawn_tree is historical + structural; list_active is the now-snapshot.

guidance.when: User asks "what triggered this?", "show me the lineage of agent X", or you need the parent-child spawn graph for an Intel-panel-style view.
guidance.notWhen: For LIVE running spawns only, use `orchestrator.list_active`. spawn_tree is historical + structural; list_active is the now-snapshot.

tools.name: issues:claim
tools.description: Claim one OR many issues (assign to yourself, or to `assignee`) before fixing, so others know they are owned. Auto-subscribes you. Single: { id, assignee? }. Many same assignee: { ids:[…], assignee? }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ id, assignee? }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, issue? | error, holder? }], counts } — correlate by id; a claim_conflict on one item never fails the rest.

guidance.when: You are about to start work on issue(s) — claim first so two agents do not duplicate the fix. Claim several at once via ids:[…] or items:[…].
guidance.notWhen: Just reading/triaging (no claim needed). To drop a claim, issues:release. A per-item `claim_conflict` means a LIVE peer already holds it — coordinate with the `holder` (coord:send), do not blind-retry.
guidance.chaining: issues:list → issues:claim → (fix) → issues:close / issues:promote.

tools.name: issues:close
tools.description: Set one OR many issues' lifecycle state: resolved (fixed/answered), closed (won't-fix / no longer relevant), or open (reopen). Single: { id, state? }. Many same state: { ids:[…], state? }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ id, state? }]. Resolving notifies all subscribers, including mention-mode. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, issue? | error }], counts } — correlate by id; a not-found item never fails the rest.

guidance.when: An issue is fixed (resolved) or is being dropped without a fix (closed). Reopen with state=open if it recurs. Close several at once via ids:[…]+state or items:[…].
guidance.notWhen: Promoting it to a tracked fix feature — issues:promote (which keeps it open/fixing until the feature lands).

tools.name: issues:comment
tools.description: Add a note to one OR many issues' comment threads. Subscribers are notified. Single: { id, body }. Many same body: { ids:[…], body }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ id, body }]. Use for investigation findings, repro details, or a status update. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, post? | error }], counts } — correlate by id; a not-found item never fails the rest.

guidance.when: You have something to add to an existing issue — a repro, a root-cause finding, a decision, or progress. Comment on several at once via ids:[…]+body or items:[…].
guidance.notWhen: Editing the issue itself (issues:update) or resolving it (issues:close).

tools.name: issues:create
tools.description: File an engineer/SU issue — a real problem you discovered but are not fixing right now. Tag topics so agents subscribed to that area see it. Returns the issue id (EI-<n>). Dup-check with issues:search first.

guidance.when: You hit a real problem mid-work that is out of your current scope (or that you are deferring) and want it tracked + visible to others in the area. Tag the relevant topics.
guidance.notWhen: A passing question with no clear owner — use coord:ask (knowledge-first). Something you are fixing right now in-scope — just fix it. A validator finding inside a pipeline run — that goes through the validator pipeline, not here.
guidance.chaining: issues:search (dedup) → issues:create { topics } → issues:claim when you start → issues:close on resolution; issues:promote to mint a fix feature.

tools.name: issues:get
tools.description: Read one OR many engineer issues in full — fields, topic tags, the comment thread, and its links — in ONE call. Pass `id` for one or `ids` for several (1–100). Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, issue?, error? }], counts } — correlate each result by its id, not by position; a missing id comes back as that item's { ok:false } without failing the rest.

guidance.when: You have one or more issue ids (from issues:list/search) and want their detail before claiming, commenting, or fixing. Pass every id you need at once via `ids` instead of calling per id.
guidance.notWhen: Scanning many — use issues:list.
guidance.chaining: issues:list → issues:get { ids:[…] } → issues:claim / issues:comment / issues:close.

tools.name: issues:link
tools.description: Link one OR many issues to another object — e.g. this issue blocks a plan item or a feature. rel = blocks | relates | duplicates | fixes. target = a {kind, ref} like {plan_item, '<plan-slug>#P-003'} or {feature, '<harness>#F-012'} (a feature ref MUST be harness-qualified — bare 'F-012' is rejected). Pass unlink:true to remove. Single: { id, targetKind, targetRef, rel?, unlink? }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ id, targetKind, targetRef, rel?, unlink? }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, rel?, target?, linked? | error }], counts } — correlate by id; one bad item never fails the rest.

guidance.when: One or more issues block specific work (a plan item / feature) — link so that work is shown blocked until the issue closes; or relate/dedup issues. A feature ref is harness-qualified: "<harness>#<feature_id>" (e.g. "papercup#F-12"). Link several at once via items:[…].
guidance.notWhen: Tagging it to a topic area — issues:tag.

tools.name: issues:list
tools.description: List engineer/SU issues. Filters: state (open|resolved|closed), scope, assignee, severity, topic (issues tagged it), mine (assigned to you). The agent-facing problem tracker — distinct from the validator pipeline (harness:status shows that).

guidance.when: To see open problems in an area before starting work, find something to pick up, or check what you are assigned. Filter by a topic to see everything filed against that area.
guidance.notWhen: You want validator-pipeline findings for one harness — that is harness:status. You want one issue in full — issues:get.
guidance.chaining: topics:list → issues:list { topic } → issues:get → issues:claim.

tools.name: issues:promote
tools.description: Promote one OR many issues into F-FIX features so the harness pipeline fixes them. A harness-scoped issue mints into its harness; an operator-scope issue needs a target harness. Single: { id, harness? }. Many same harness: { ids:[…], harness? }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ id, harness? }]. Records the linked feature; the issue stays open until the fix lands. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, issue?, feature? | error }], counts } — correlate by id; one failure never fails the rest.

guidance.when: An issue is a real defect that should be FIXED by the pipeline (not just tracked or answered) — promote it to mint + link the fix feature. Promote several at once via ids:[…]+harness or items:[…].
guidance.notWhen: A question/discussion (resolve it), a nit you would not spend a feature on, or an issue already linked to a feature.
guidance.chaining: issues:get → issues:promote { harness } → the F-FIX feature dispatches in that harness; issues:close when it lands.

tools.name: issues:release
tools.description: Release (unassign) an issue so someone else can pick it up — e.g. you are blocked, deprioritizing, or handing off.

guidance.when: You claimed an issue but are not going to finish it — release so it is pickable again.
guidance.notWhen: You finished it — issues:close instead.

tools.name: issues:search
tools.description: Full-text search engineer issues by title/body. Use before issues:create to avoid filing a duplicate, or to find a known problem.

guidance.when: Before filing an issue (dedup), or to locate an existing one by keywords.
guidance.notWhen: You want a filtered list by state/topic/assignee — issues:list.
guidance.chaining: issues:search → issues:get / issues:comment (add to the existing one instead of a dup).

tools.name: issues:subscribe
tools.description: Follow one OR many specific issues so their comments/updates/resolution inject into your inbox. mode = full | digest | mention. Pass unsubscribe:true to stop. Single: { id, mode?, unsubscribe? }. Many: { ids:[…], mode?, unsubscribe? } or items:[{ id, mode?, unsubscribe? }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, subscribed? | error }], counts } — correlate by id; a not-found item never fails the rest. (To follow an area, use topics:subscribe.)

guidance.when: You care about one or more specific issues (you reported them, depend on them, or can contribute) and want their updates pushed to you. Subscribe several at once via ids:[…] or items:[…].
guidance.notWhen: You want everything in an area — topics:subscribe is the scalable unit.

tools.name: issues:tag
tools.description: Add or remove topic tags on one OR many issues. Tagging routes an issue to everyone subscribed to that topic — the main way an issue reaches the right people. Single: { id, add?, remove? }. Many same tags: { ids:[…], add?, remove? }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ id, add?, remove? }]. topics:list to see/create topics. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, topics? | error }], counts } — correlate by id; a not-found item never fails the rest.

guidance.when: One or more issues belong to a relevance area (e.g. zero-cache, federation) so the people following that area should see them. Tag several at once via ids:[…] or items:[…].
guidance.notWhen: The topic does not exist yet — topics:create it first (prefer an existing one).
guidance.chaining: topics:list → issues:tag { add:[topic] }.

tools.name: issues:update
tools.description: Edit one OR many issues' title / body / severity / kind / found-during / linked feature. Notifies subscribers. Single: { id, …fields }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ id, …fields }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, issue? | error }], counts } — correlate by id; a not-found item never fails the rest. (State → issues:close; tags → issues:tag; comments → issues:comment.)

guidance.when: Refine issue(s) you or someone else filed — clarify the title/body, re-rate severity, correct a mislabeled kind (bug↔change — the kind picks the auto-implement lane, so keep it honest), or attach the feature that will fix it. Edit several at once via items:[…].
guidance.notWhen: Resolving it (issues:close), adding a note (issues:comment), or routing it to a topic (issues:tag).

tools.name: learning_packs:candidates
tools.description: List learning-pack item CANDIDATEs — cross-hive recurring lessons the recurrence-escalation loop staged for owner review (default: pending only). Each carries provenance: the friction signature, the scopes it recurred across, the recurrence count, and the source improvement-item ids.

guidance.when: The owner asks what fleet lessons await review, or before learning_packs:decide_candidate (the id comes from here).
guidance.notWhen: To read a hive's installed learnings (learning_packs:list / memory:list) or the pack catalog (learning_packs:list).
guidance.chaining: learning_packs:decide_candidate { id, action } to adopt into the fleet-lessons pack or dismiss; after an adopt, hives pick the item up via learning_packs:install/upgrade.

tools.name: learning_packs:decide_candidate
tools.description: Decide one OR many pending learning-pack candidates: adopt (write it into the fleet-lessons pack — version bumps so hives see updateAvailable; optionally edit title/text first) or dismiss (terminal — the signature never re-stages). This is an OWNER decision; candidates are never auto-published. Single: { id, action, note?, title?, text? }. Many same action: { ids:[…], action }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ id, action, note?, title?, text? }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, action?, … | error }], counts } — correlate by id, not by position; one bad candidate never fails the rest.

guidance.when: The owner has reviewed pending candidate(s) (learning_packs:candidates) and says adopt/dismiss — or asks you to apply their edits while adopting. Decide several at once via ids:[…]+action or items:[…].
guidance.notWhen: To seed a lesson into a hive pool directly (adoption only updates the PACK; hives adopt via learning_packs:install/upgrade). Unprompted bulk adoption — each candidate is an explicit owner call.
guidance.chaining: learning_packs:candidates first (ids + drafts). After adopt: hives with fleet-lessons installed show updateAvailable → learning_packs:upgrade { hive, pack: "fleet-lessons" }; others via learning_packs:install. Bulk: single | items[] (or ids) → { ok, results, counts }; correlate by id not position; one failure never fails the rest.

tools.name: learning_packs:export
tools.description: Export a hive's shared learnings into the standard pack shape (learning-packs/<packId>/ — manifest + one-learning-per-file) inside a member repo's working tree, ready to commit + publish. Defaults to the hive's ORGANIC learnings only; includePackRows re-exports installed-pack content too (explicit opt-in).

guidance.when: The user wants to share their hive's accumulated learnings — first step of the publish flow.
guidance.notWhen: Installing or browsing packs — learning_packs:list/install.
guidance.chaining: After the files are committed + pushed by the project's normal flow, learning_packs:publish lists the pack on the Comb (it publishes PENDING — operator approval gates public visibility, D-007).

tools.name: learning_packs:install
tools.description: Install a learning pack into an existing hive's shared memory, with the install-time conflict review: incoming learnings are classified clean/duplicate/conflict against the hive's current pool; clashes require explicit per-item resolutions (install · skip · replace · keep-both). Defaults skip clashes — existing content outranks the incoming pack.

guidance.when: Adding a pack to an EXISTING hive (a new hive seeds its pack at creation). Call once to get the review; re-call with resolutions (or acceptDefaults: true) to apply.
guidance.notWhen: At hive creation (hive:create seeds automatically). To re-adopt a newer version of an already-installed pack — learning_packs:upgrade.
guidance.chaining: learning_packs:list { hive } first (what's installed); after install, learning.hive invalidates so the Learnings view refreshes.

tools.name: learning_packs:list
tools.description: List resolvable learning packs (builtin + Comb-installed) and, when `hive` is given, that hive's installed state: per-pack rows present/edited, enabled/disabled, and whether a newer pack version is adoptable.

guidance.when: Before learning_packs:install/upgrade (what's available + what's already in the hive), or when the user asks what learnings their hive carries.
guidance.notWhen: To read the actual learning texts — learning.hive backs the Learnings UI, and memory:list { hive_slug } returns the rows.
guidance.chaining: learning_packs:install { hive, pack } to add one; learning_packs:upgrade when updateAvailable; learning_packs:set_enabled to mute a pack without uninstalling.

tools.name: learning_packs:publish
tools.description: List an exported learning pack on the Comb: resolves the member repo's GitHub coords, publishes a kind='learning-pack' listing (listing_ref = packId) with the operator's gh token + attestation. The listing lands PENDING (D-007) — an operator must approve it before anyone else sees it.

guidance.when: After learning_packs:export and the files are pushed to the GitHub repo.
guidance.notWhen: The pack files are not on GitHub yet — publish points at the repo; export first, push, then publish.
guidance.chaining: The response carries review_status pending — the submitter sees it on their own listing; operators approve at /admin/cupboard-moderation.

tools.name: learning_packs:set_enabled
tools.description: Enable or disable one OR many learning packs' injection for a hive WITHOUT uninstalling them — the rows stay stored; agents just stop recalling them. Cheap to flip, fully reversible. Single: { hive, pack, enabled }. Many packs same hive: { hive, packs:[…], enabled }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ hive, pack, enabled }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, hive, pack, enabled? | error }], counts } — correlate by hive+pack, not by position; one failure never fails the rest.

guidance.when: Trying out whether a pack helps, or quarantining one that seems to misdirect agents — before reaching for uninstall. Flip several at once via packs:[…] or items:[…].
guidance.notWhen: Permanently removing a pack — learning_packs:uninstall.
guidance.chaining: learning_packs:list { hive } shows enabled state per installed pack. Bulk: single | items[] (or packs) → { ok, results, counts }; correlate by hive+pack not position; one failure never fails the rest.

tools.name: learning_packs:sweep
tools.description: Re-run the conflict judge across a hive's whole shared memory pool and report contradiction pairs — catches conflicts that emerged AFTER install (pack learnings vs what the hive organically learned later). Read-only; capped at 200 rows per sweep.

guidance.when: Periodic hygiene (a Queen idle-turn task), after installing a pack into a hive with many organic learnings, or when agents seem to be following contradictory guidance.
guidance.notWhen: At install time — learning_packs:install runs its own per-item review.
guidance.chaining: Resolve a reported pair deliberately: memory:forget the wrong side, or memory:update it to reconcile.

tools.name: learning_packs:uninstall
tools.description: Remove a learning pack's rows from a hive's shared memory (provenance-driven). Rows the user edited since seeding are KEPT by default and reported; keepEdited: false removes those too. Organic (hive-learned) rows are never touched.

guidance.when: The user wants a pack gone from a hive, or before re-installing a pack from scratch.
guidance.notWhen: To temporarily mute a pack — learning_packs:set_enabled { enabled: false } keeps the rows and just stops injecting them.
guidance.chaining: learning_packs:list { hive } shows what remains; kept edited rows are listed in the response.

tools.name: learning_packs:upgrade
tools.description: Adopt a newer version of an installed learning pack: NEW items (no row in the hive's pool) are classified like an install and added per your resolutions; rows already present are never auto-modified. Call once for the plan, re-call with resolutions (or acceptDefaults: true) to apply.

guidance.when: learning_packs:list shows updateAvailable for an installed pack.
guidance.notWhen: First-time install — learning_packs:install.
guidance.chaining: The response reports installedVersions vs availableVersion + the adoptable-new-items review.

tools.name: lexicon:active_pack
tools.description: The active brand pack's full term→label map (every term key → singular/plural forms) plus the pack id. Resolved via the server-side lexicon twin so the `papercusp-the-hive` flag is respected. The single source of truth for any non-React/non-server surface (e.g. the Rust pui) that needs the live lexicon without duplicating the packs.

guidance.when: A client outside the React/server lexicon wiring (the pui TUI, a CLI) needs the active term labels; fetch once at startup and re-fetch on a flag change if a push rail exists.
guidance.notWhen: You are in React (use the useLexicon hook) or server code (import term() from the lexicon module) — those resolve in-process.

tools.name: locks:acquire
tools.description: Claim a set of files for exclusive editing. Returns ok+lock_id on success, or busy+contention details on failure. On contention prefer wake_on_grant:true — queue a waiter ticket + a one-shot wake subscription and return immediately; you END YOUR TURN and are re-invoked when the cascade grants you the locks (no polling, no held turn). wait={max_sec:N} (≤300) is the legacy blocking wait for short same-turn needs. Paths MUST be repo-relative POSIX (no leading ./, no //, no trailing /, no .., no backslashes, no absolute paths) — the server canonicalizes equivalent spellings to one lock key but rejects malformed ones; resolve symlinks caller-side before claiming.

guidance.when: For a DELIBERATE multi-file claim you hold across several edits AND the commit — acquire once for the whole set, release after committing. Per-edit locking is already automatic on every client (the PreToolUse/tool_call hook acquires + releases around each individual Edit/Write/apply_patch), so the gap this fills is the edit→commit window the hook cannot cover.
guidance.notWhen: Read-only inspection needs no claim. A single incidental edit needs no manual call — the hook covers it. Do NOT wrap every edit in acquire/release; that duplicates the hook and churns the lock.
guidance.chaining: On ok: make your edits → commit → locks:release { lock_id }. On busy: wake_on_grant:true → end your turn; the wake turn carries your lock_id + TTL (already running) — edit, then release. Only block (wait) when you need the lock within THIS turn and the holder is about to finish; events:cancel + locks:cancel_wait to retract a queued wake.

tools.name: locks:acquire_granular
tools.description: Acquire a multi-granularity intention lock on a path NODE (a file, a directory/subtree, or the harness root ""). mode "X" = own the subtree exclusively (a directory lock for a refactor, or a file write); "S" = read the whole subtree; "SIX" = read the subtree while writing one node; IS/IX are the intention modes (usually derived for you). The lock places the matching intention on every ancestor incl. the harness root, so a harness-exclusive (X on "") now conflicts with any descendant file lock. All-or-nothing — you get the whole lock-set or a conflict list. Release with locks:release_granular.

guidance.when: A directory/subtree refactor (mode X on the dir), reading a whole subtree (S), or coordinating file-vs-harness-level work the per-edit lock is too fine for. Use "" as the path to take/contend the harness root.
guidance.notWhen: A single-file edit — the per-edit hook + locks:acquire already cover that. Cross-resource coordination (dev-server / db-schema) — use locks:acquire_resource.
guidance.chaining: locks:acquire_granular { path, mode:"X" } → on ok do the work → locks:release_granular { lock_id }. On conflict, inspect the returned conflicts and pivot/retry.

tools.name: locks:acquire_resource
tools.description: Acquire a NAMED resource (must be registered; see locks:list). mode:"shared" = "I am using it" (many coexist); mode:"exclusive" = "I need to restart/mutate it" (granted only once shared holders drain to zero). For exclusive, set wait:{max_drain_sec:N} (≤300) to block while existing shared holders finish — new shared acquisitions are refused meanwhile. Release with locks:release_resource.

guidance.when: Before relying on a shared resource (mode shared), or before a destructive action on it like restarting the dev server (mode exclusive). Registered resources only — check locks:list.
guidance.notWhen: File edits — use locks:acquire (the per-edit hook already covers those). An unregistered ad-hoc name — register it first (locks are useless if names diverge).
guidance.chaining: shared: acquire_resource{mode:shared} → use it → release_resource. exclusive restart: acquire_resource{mode:exclusive,wait:{max_drain_sec}} → on ok+held do the restart → release_resource (signals it is back up).

tools.name: locks:cancel_wait
tools.description: Abandon a queued waiter ticket. Returns cancelled=true if the wait was active; cancelled=false means a grant raced (you now hold a lock you didn't want — call locks:release immediately).

guidance.when: Mid-wait, when the user redirects you to other work or you decide a different approach.
guidance.notWhen: After you've already received an ok response from locks:acquire — there's no waiter to cancel.
guidance.chaining: On cancelled=false → locks:release { all_mine: true } to free the lock you got handed.

tools.name: locks:check_command
tools.description: Check a raw shell command against the named-lock registry: does it touch a resource with an exclusive (restart/migration) in flight? Returns decision (allow | warn | block) + the matched resources. The verdict a raw-Bash gate consumes.

guidance.when: A hook (or you) wants to know if a destructive command would collide with an in-flight exclusive hold before running it.
guidance.notWhen: Acquiring a lock — use locks:acquire_resource. File edits — locks:queue.
guidance.chaining: block → wait / coordinate; warn → proceed with care; allow → run.

tools.name: locks:heartbeat
tools.description: Extend a held lock's TTL. Returns extended=true on success; extended=false means the lock had already expired or been stolen.

guidance.when: For edits expected to take >15 min, call once at the halfway mark.
guidance.notWhen: For short edits — the default 20-min TTL covers it. Heartbeating every minute is wasteful.

tools.name: locks:heartbeat_resource
tools.description: Extend a named-resource lease you hold (by lock_id) for another ttl_sec. Owner-checked; no-op if the lease already lapsed.

guidance.when: Holding a named resource longer than its TTL — heartbeat near the halfway mark.
guidance.notWhen: Short holds within one TTL window. Released locks need no heartbeat.
guidance.chaining: locks:acquire_resource → (long work, heartbeat periodically) → locks:release_resource.

tools.name: locks:list
tools.description: List registered named resources (name, rule, enforcement level) and who currently holds each, with a draining flag. The authoritative discovery surface for resource locks — only registered names are acquirable.

guidance.when: Before acquiring a named resource (to learn the exact name + the rule), or to see who holds a resource / whether it is draining.
guidance.notWhen: File-lock contention — that is locks:queue.
guidance.chaining: locks:list → locks:acquire_resource { resource, mode }.

tools.name: locks:queue
tools.description: Read the active locks and pending waiters for a workspace. Optionally filter by paths (overlap) or owner. Pass include_completed=true to also return terminal waiters from the last 24h (diagnostics).

guidance.when: Diagnostics — "what are the other agents doing?" or "why am I blocked?". Cheap, MVCC read.
guidance.notWhen: Before every acquire — locks:acquire already returns busy context. Use queue when the user asks.

tools.name: locks:release
tools.description: Release a held lock set. Pass lock_id (with optional paths filter) for a specific lock, or all_mine=true to release every lock owned by this agent. Fires the grant cascade for waiting agents.

guidance.when: Immediately after the edit is committed. On context loss / restart, call with all_mine=true to release everything.
guidance.notWhen: Mid-edit. The lock should outlive the edit by enough that no other agent races between release and PR merge.
guidance.chaining: locks:acquire → edit → locks:release { lock_id }. Or: session-end → locks:release { all_mine: true }.

tools.name: locks:release_granular
tools.description: Release a granular intention lock-set you hold, by lock_id. Frees the leaf node + all of its ancestor intention locks in one call. Owner-checked.

guidance.when: As soon as the subtree/directory work the lock guarded is done.
guidance.notWhen: While still working under the lock. Release is owner-checked — you can only drop your own lock-set.
guidance.chaining: locks:acquire_granular → work → locks:release_granular { lock_id }.

tools.name: locks:release_resource
tools.description: Release a named-resource lock you hold — pass lock_id (preferred) or the resource name. Releasing the last shared holder completes a pending exclusive's drain; releasing an exclusive frees the resource.

guidance.when: As soon as you are done using a shared resource, or immediately after an exclusive action (e.g. the dev-server restart) completes.
guidance.notWhen: While still using the resource. Do not release another agent's lock — release is owner-checked and only drops your own rows.
guidance.chaining: locks:acquire_resource → use/act → locks:release_resource { lock_id }.

tools.name: loop:arm
tools.description: Arm an engine-managed LOOP on your own session — the tracked replacement for Claude /loop. Each fire re-wakes THIS warm session ~intervalSec after your previous turn SETTLES (a warm coord wake, not a fresh run), so your context carries across iterations. The loop survives restarts, is observable (loop:status / fleet:assignments / fire-history), and inherits guardrails (failure-streak fire-gate + an optional cost-cap). End it with loop:end.

guidance.when: You (an su/interactive agent working directly with a user) agree to "put this on a loop" — keep advancing a plan/goal WARM on a recurring cadence. Arm it as the LAST thing before you end your turn.
guidance.notWhen: Wall-clock recurrence (a fixed time each day) — that is a SCHEDULE (plans:set-schedule). A single future wake — events:await / a one-shot. The autonomous queen/bee/scout loop — that is its OWN system (hive:declare-wake / overwatch:declare-wake); never loop:arm from an autonomous-fleet agent. Do NOT self-pace with Claude's native /loop — declare an engine loop here instead (it is tracked + pauseable).
guidance.chaining: loop:arm { intervalSec, goal, costCapCents? } → end your turn → the engine re-wakes you each iteration with the wakeup prompt (create + self-assign your work_items, work them, set_state) → loop:end to stop. loop:status to inspect.

tools.name: loop:end
tools.description: End the loop on your own session (or another owner's, with `ownerId`) — stops the recurring warm wake. The routine is deactivated (history kept); re-arm anytime with loop:arm.

guidance.when: Stop a loop you armed with loop:arm — the goal is done, you are blocked on something external, or the user says stop. Better to loop:end than burn empty wakes spinning.
guidance.notWhen: Pause the WHOLE autoloop / routines engine — that is autoloop:control. End the autonomous hive loop — that is hive:pause.
guidance.chaining: loop:arm to start; loop:status to check; loop:end to stop.

tools.name: loop:status
tools.description: Inspect the loop on your own session (or another owner's, with `ownerId`): active?, interval, parked (turn in flight), next/last fire, cost-cap. Returns null when no loop exists for the owner.

guidance.when: Check whether your loop is still armed + when it next fires, or inspect another agent's loop.
guidance.notWhen: See the WORK a loop is producing — that is fleet:assignments (the self-assigned work_items). Whole-engine health — autoloop:status.
guidance.chaining: loop:arm to start; loop:end to stop.

tools.name: memory:forget
tools.description: Delete one OR many memory entries by id — pass `id` for one or `ids` for several. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, error? }], counts } — correlate each result by its id, not by position; a not-found / timed-out id comes back as that item's { ok:false } without failing the rest.

guidance.when: When the user explicitly says "forget X" / "don't remember that anymore" / "that's wrong, drop it". Pass every id to drop at once via `ids`. Always inform the user out loud ("Removed that from memory").
guidance.notWhen: To CORRECT a memory (replace its content), use memory:update — preserves history. Only use forget for outright removal.
guidance.chaining: memory:search / memory:list → memory:forget { ids:[…] } to drop several found memories in one call. Bulk: single | ids[] → { ok, results, counts }; correlate by id not position; one failure never fails the rest.

tools.name: memory:list
tools.description: List all memories for the current user. Supports filtering by kind and harness scope.

guidance.when: When the user asks to inspect their memory ("what have you stored about me?") or you need a filter-only query.
guidance.notWhen: For semantic lookup ("what did I say about X?"), use memory:search instead.

tools.name: memory:remember
tools.description: Store a STABLE fact about the user into persistent memory, kept VERBATIM as written. Use one of 4 kinds (user / feedback / project / reference). Write ONE tight, self-contained fact per call. For transient state, use coord — not memory.

guidance.when: When the user says "remember X" / "don't forget Y" / "next time…" / "from now on…", OR when YOU notice an error you made that would recur without persistence. ALWAYS inform the user out loud ("I'll remember that"). For project-specific facts, pass harness_slug — the fact then surfaces for anyone working in that harness. Write ONE self-contained fact per call, tightly phrased: it is stored EXACTLY as written (no server-side rewriting or condensing), so make it stand on its own, lead with the searchable terms/anchors (file paths, F-NNN, backticked symbols), and drop conversational preamble.
guidance.notWhen: Default scope is per-user. Do not pass harness_slug for personal preferences. For IN-FLIGHT / ephemeral state (what you are doing right now), use coord (coord:declare-intent / coord:send) — it is delta-delivered, not a semantic store.
guidance.chaining: After writing, the persona prompt will surface this entry on the next turn's pre-turn injection. No need to call memory:search to verify.

tools.name: memory:search
tools.description: Search the user's persistent memories by semantic similarity. Returns matched facts ranked by relevance.

guidance.when: When the user references specific context from past sessions ("what did I tell you about pricing?"). Pre-turn auto-injection covers most cases; only call this for targeted lookups.
guidance.notWhen: For lookups by exact metadata (kind), use memory:list — it's faster than vector search for filter-only queries.
guidance.chaining: Pair with memory:update / memory:forget when the user corrects something you recall.

tools.name: memory:update
tools.description: Edit one OR many memory entries: replace content and/or patch metadata (kind, workspaceId, scope/recall-pool) — preserving each id. Metadata patches are vec-safe (no re-embed). Single: { id, content?, kind?, … }. Many same patch: { ids:[…], kind?/scope?/… }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ id, content?, kind?, … }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, error? }], counts } — correlate by id, not by position; a not-found / timed-out id never fails the rest.

guidance.when: CONTENT: when the user corrects something you stored ("actually it's Daniel, not Dan") — pass `content`. METADATA HYGIENE: to re-tag a memory's `kind`, fix its `workspaceId`, or move it to the right recall `scope`/pool, pass those fields (no content needed); re-tag MANY at once via { ids:[…], kind } or items:[…]. Find the id via memory:search / memory:list first. For a content edit, tell the user ("Updating my memory: …").
guidance.notWhen: To REMOVE a memory entirely, use memory:forget. To ADD a new memory, use memory:remember. Do not change `scope` casually — it moves which queries can recall the memory.
guidance.chaining: memory:search → memory:update { ids:[…], kind } (bulk metadata hygiene). Bulk: single | items[] (or ids) → { ok, results, counts }; correlate by id not position; one failure never fails the rest.

tools.name: messages:dismiss
tools.description:
When to use: Soft-hide a message you've handled — "ignore that note", "dismiss the comment on X". Reversible (status→archived, not deleted).

When NOT to use: For deleting a message, this isn't it — dismiss is reversible. For archiving a CHAT (multi-turn), use `agent_chats:archive`.

guidance.when: Soft-hide a message you've handled — "ignore that note", "dismiss the comment on X". Reversible (status→archived, not deleted).
guidance.notWhen: For deleting a message, this isn't it — dismiss is reversible. For archiving a CHAT (multi-turn), use `agent_chats:archive`.

tools.name: messages:inbox
tools.description:
When to use: What's pending for me? Harness-level messages (directives, worker replies) — or pass `feature_id` for one feature's thread.

When NOT to use: For sent items use `messages:outbox`. To soft-hide a handled message use `messages:dismiss`.

guidance.when: What's pending for me? Harness-level messages (directives, worker replies) — or pass `feature_id` for one feature's thread.
