tools.description: Fetch one OR many reusable code:run RECIPEs by id — including the full script — so you can inspect what they do before recipes:run-ning them. Pass `id` for one or `ids` for several. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, recipe? | error }], counts } — correlate by id, not by position; a missing id comes back as that item's { ok:false } without failing the rest. Read-only.

guidance.when: When you have one or more recipe ids (from recipes:list / recipes:search / a code:run result's similarRecipes) and want to read their script + metadata before reusing. Pass every id at once via `ids`.
guidance.notWhen: To EXECUTE the recipe — use recipes:run (it runs the script under YOUR role-scoped envelope). To discover recipes by intent — recipes:search.
guidance.chaining: recipes:search / recipes:list → recipes:get { ids:[…] } (inspect) → recipes:run { id } (reuse). Bulk: single | ids[] → { ok, results, counts }; correlate by id not position; one failure never fails the rest.

tools.name: recipes:list
tools.description: List reusable code:run RECIPES for your hive (most-run first). A recipe is a saved code:run script other agents authored; browse them to reuse instead of re-authoring. Read-only.

guidance.when: Before authoring a multi-step code:run, to see what reusable recipes already exist in your hive — the hot ones surface first. If one fits, recipes:run it instead of re-writing the script.
guidance.notWhen: When you already know the recipe id (recipes:get), or to find a recipe by intent (recipes:search ranks by semantic + tool-set similarity). This is the plain most-run-first browse.
guidance.chaining: recipes:list → recipes:get { id } to inspect the script → recipes:run { id } to reuse it.

tools.name: recipes:merge
tools.description: Consolidate near-duplicate code:run RECIPES into one survivor: each duplicate flips to status=merged (pointing at the survivor) and its run_count/success_count are folded onto the survivor so it reflects the cluster's total usage. One transaction; never merges a recipe into itself; ids outside your workspace are skipped. Reversible (a status flip).

guidance.when: After reviewing a near-duplicate MERGE CLUSTER from recipes:candidates and deciding which one survives — pass the keeper as survivorId and the rest as duplicateIds to collapse the cluster into one recipe whose counts reflect all of them.
guidance.notWhen: To retire a stale one-off (recipes:sweep) or to promote a recipe to a tool (file a work-item). Do not merge recipes that are genuinely distinct just because they look similar — the dedup score is a worklist, the merge decision is yours. Inspect each script with recipes:get first.
guidance.chaining: recipes:candidates (mergeClusters) → recipes:get { id } per member to confirm they're truly duplicates → recipes:merge { survivorId, duplicateIds }.

tools.name: recipes:run
tools.description: Run one OR many saved code:run RECIPEs by id — the reuse path. Each recipe's script executes under YOUR role-scoped tool envelope (NOT the author's — no privilege travels with a recipe); returns only each script's summary. Use dryRun:true to preview write-effect mutations. Single: { id, dryRun?, timeoutSec? }. Many same options: { ids:[…], dryRun? }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ id, dryRun?, timeoutSec? }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, result? | error }], counts } — correlate by id, not by position; one recipe failing never fails the rest.

guidance.when: When a recipe already does what you need (found via recipes:search / recipes:list, or a code:run result's similarRecipes) — run it by id instead of re-authoring the same script. Run several at once via ids:[…] or items:[…]. Each runs under YOUR envelope, so you can only reuse recipes whose tools you may call.
guidance.notWhen: When no existing recipe fits — author a fresh code:run (which also auto-captures + dedups). Preview a recipe's mutations with dryRun before a committing run.
guidance.chaining: recipes:search { query } → recipes:get { ids:[…] } (inspect) → recipes:run { id, dryRun:true } → recipes:run { id }. Bulk: single | items[] (or ids) → { ok, results, counts }; correlate by id not position; one failure never fails the rest.

tools.name: recipes:search
tools.description: Search reusable code:run RECIPES by intent (hybrid BM25 + embedding + tool-set overlap). Use BEFORE authoring a multi-step code:run to find a recipe that already does it. Read-only.

guidance.when: BEFORE writing a multi-step code:run — describe what you want to do and this ranks the recipes in your hive that already do something similar (semantic + tool-set match). If a high-similarity recipe fits, recipes:run it instead of re-authoring.
guidance.notWhen: To browse all recipes most-run-first (recipes:list), or when you already hold the id (recipes:get / recipes:run). code:run still auto-surfaces similarRecipes after the fact — this is the BEFORE-you-author check.
guidance.chaining: recipes:search { query } → recipes:get { id } (inspect the top hit) → recipes:run { id } (reuse).

tools.name: recipes:sweep
tools.description: Retire the stale long-tail of never-reused one-off code:run RECIPES (active, last run older than staleDays AND run_count <= maxRunCount). NEVER retires a hot, recently-run, promoted, or merged recipe. dryRun (DEFAULT TRUE) previews the candidates without changing anything — pass dryRun:false to actually retire. Reversible (a status flip).

guidance.when: Periodic hygiene (a Queen idle-turn task) to clear the long tail of one-off recipes that were authored on a single run and never reused. ALWAYS run it once with the default dryRun:true to review the candidates, then dryRun:false to retire them.
guidance.notWhen: To merge near-duplicates (recipes:merge) or to find promote candidates (recipes:candidates). Don't lower staleDays/raise maxRunCount aggressively — that risks retiring recipes still finding their audience; the conservative defaults (30 days, <=1 run) target only true one-offs.
guidance.chaining: recipes:sweep { dryRun: true } (review the would-retire list) → recipes:sweep { dryRun: false } (commit). recipes:get { id } to inspect any candidate before committing.

tools.name: release:checkpoint-config
tools.description: Read or set the green-checkpoint / release thresholds: stallReds + stallAgeMs (held-gate STALLED alert), chronicFlakeCount + flakeNotifyCooldownMs (chronic-flake quarantine nudge), deployBackoffMs (re-deploy backoff after a failed/rolled-back deploy of the same target). set is audited + one-call-revertible.

guidance.when: Tune the release pipeline live — e.g. shorten deployBackoffMs to re-deploy a fixed target sooner during an incident, or raise stallReds/stallAgeMs to quiet a noisy stall alert.
guidance.notWhen: For the placement watchdog use hive:control_policy; for migrations use db:migrate-policy. vitest forks / suite-timeout (green-checkpoint.ts) and the health-probe timing are not covered here (separate consumers — follow-up).
guidance.chaining: /admin/git shows the pipeline; config:list-overrides shows the active override; config:reset-overrides reverts it.

tools.name: release:deploy
tools.description: Manual deploy lever + "why isn't my change live?" diagnosis. op:status (read-only — gate red/green/stalled, release-fixer status, how far :3070 is behind the green pin, + a recommendation; call FIRST when a gate-clean change isn't live). op:trigger (expedite a GREEN-but-stalled deploy; refuses unless green code is ahead; dry-run unless confirm:true; audited). op:force (operator/queen/architect ONLY, loud+audited: deploy an UN-GREEN commit past a red gate — needs acknowledgeRedTests + reason; the rare no-users-window escape). Wraps the deploy-cli chokepoint, fired DETACHED.

guidance.when: A committed, gate-clean change isn't live on :3070 — {op:status} to see why. GREEN-but-stalled → {op:trigger,confirm:true} (safe; only ships the green pin). Gate RED on UNRELATED tests → FIX the reds first (even out of lane).
guidance.notWhen: Never force as a reflex to "get my change out" — force ships KNOWN-BROKEN code (route-around-the-broken-thing); owner/operator-gated, no-users window only. Prefer fix-reds > quarantine-a-confirmed-unrelated-red-by-hand > owner-force; never silently wait. Threshold tuning → release:checkpoint-config; per-path probe → dev:pipeline_position.
guidance.chaining: dev:pipeline_position{path} → release:deploy{op:status} → {op:trigger,confirm:true} (green-but-stalled) OR fix the reds.

tools.name: roles:firing_on
tools.description: Return role manifests whose `firesOn` array includes the given hook event.

guidance.when: You need to know which roles are configured to fire on a given hook event before firing it (avoids no-op fires).
guidance.notWhen: For the hook-event ENUM itself, use `hooks:known`. For role details, use `roles:get`.

tools.name: roles:get
tools.description: Fetch one role manifest by id, scoped to a harness slug (or global when slug omitted).

guidance.when: User names a specific role and wants its full definition (system prompt, allowed tools, quotas).
guidance.notWhen: For the role list, use `roles:list`. For the known-role enum (static), use `roles:known`.

tools.name: roles:known
tools.description: Static well-known role-id allowlist (kernel set; plugin-registered roles extend this).

guidance.when: Static enum of role names the runtime supports — use to validate a role string before passing it elsewhere.
guidance.notWhen: For the workspace's ACTUAL roles (may be a subset), use `roles:list`. known is the universe; list is what's configured.

tools.name: roles:list
tools.description: List role manifests (id, source, fires-on, etc.) for a harness, or globally when no harness given.

guidance.when: You need the set of agent roles configured in the workspace (architect, worker, validator, …) before spawning or dispatching.
guidance.notWhen: For agents currently RUNNING, use `agents:list`. roles:list is the static configuration; agents:list is the live processes.
guidance.chaining: Pair with `roles:get` for one role's definition.

tools.name: routines:list
tools.description: List the scheduled system routines in this workspace (git-sync, green-checkpoint, release-trigger, improvement-watchdog, …): name, install slug, cron, target role, active flag, next/last fire. Read-only.

guidance.when: See the system routines and their cadence/active state before retuning or pausing one (e.g. inspect the git-sync / green-checkpoint / release-trigger schedule).
guidance.notWhen: To CHANGE a routine, use routines:set. For a harness blueprint autoloop, use autoloop:status.
guidance.chaining: routines:set to retune or pause a routine you find here (use its exact name + installSlug).

tools.name: routines:set
tools.description: Retune or pause/resume a scheduled system routine (git-sync, green-checkpoint, release-trigger, …) without raw SQL: change its cron and/or active flag (active:false = PAUSE, active:true = RESUME). Audited + one-call-revertible via the control harness; an invalid cron is rejected. On a cron change, next_fire_at is recomputed.

guidance.when: Pause git-sync during a delicate manual operation (active:false), resume it (active:true), retune a routine's cadence (cron), or patch a routine CONFIG value (triggerConfig — e.g. the bee-transcript-cap caps) on a running system — the safe alternative to the raw UPDATE harness_shared.routines the playbook forbids.
guidance.notWhen: For a harness blueprint autoloop, use autoloop:control. To just SEE routines, routines:list. (These routine rows are their own store; they do not appear in config:list-overrides.)
guidance.chaining: routines:list first to get the exact name + installSlug; routines:list after to confirm the change.

tools.name: rubrics:get
tools.description: Read one OR many rubrics in full — each rubric's criteria (key + model + method + drift markers + optional rating scale), default rating scale, and method_ref runbook. Pass `rubricId` for one or `rubricIds` for several. Grade against these: a structured observation's `ratings` is a Record keyed by criteria[].key here (ratings[criteriaKey] = { rating, evidence }). Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, rubricId, rubric? | error }], counts } — correlate by rubricId, not by position; a missing id never fails the rest.

guidance.when: You have one or more rubric_ids (from rubrics:list/search) and need their full criteria to grade against — e.g. Overwatch emitting the hive-coordination-health scorecard, or filing a structured observation. Pass every id at once via `rubricIds`.
guidance.notWhen: Scanning many — rubrics:list (summary rows).
guidance.chaining: rubrics:list → rubrics:get { rubricIds:[…] } → grade each criterion (observation `ratings` is a Record keyed by criteria[].key) in your observation. Bulk: single | rubricIds[] → { ok, results, counts }; correlate by rubricId not position; one failure never fails the rest.

tools.name: rubrics:list
tools.description: List rubrics (shared standards for a system characteristic) — active first, then proposed. Filter by status / characteristic. A rubric carries the model (how it should work), method, rating scale + drift markers, and per-characteristic criteria that agents grade STRUCTURED OBSERVATIONS against. Returns summary rows; use rubrics:get for full criteria.

guidance.when: Before filing an observation — check whether an ACTIVE rubric fits the characteristic you are assessing, so you can file a structured (rated) observation instead of free-text. Overwatch/Scout: discover the rubric set to grade against.
guidance.notWhen: You already have the rubric_id and want the full criteria — rubrics:get. Free-text keyword lookup — rubrics:search.
guidance.chaining: rubrics:list { status: "active" } → rubrics:get { rubricId } → file a structured observation.

tools.name: rubrics:propose
tools.description: Propose a rubric (the shared standard for a system characteristic) → status "proposed". Any agent may propose — typically on noticing a cluster of free-text observations about one characteristic with no rubric. The Queen/owner ratifies it active (rubrics:ratify). Idempotent on rubric_id (re-propose updates the content).

guidance.when: You see a recurring characteristic worth grading consistently and no rubric covers it. Author the criteria (each: model + how-to-investigate + drift markers); reference an agent-insights runbook via methodRef for the long-form method.
guidance.notWhen: A one-off finding — file a free-text observation instead. Activating an existing proposed rubric — rubrics:ratify. Check rubrics:search first to avoid a duplicate.
guidance.chaining: rubrics:search (dedup) → rubrics:propose → rubrics:ratify (Queen/owner).

tools.name: rubrics:ratify
tools.description: Ratify one OR many proposed rubrics → status "active" (D-001: the Queen/owner gate — an active rubric becomes the shared definition every agent grades against). Single: { rubricId }. Many: { rubricIds:[…] }. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, rubricId, rubric? | error }], counts } — correlate by rubricId, not by position; a not-found id never fails the rest.

guidance.when: You are the Queen/owner reviewing proposed rubric(s) and judge them sound shared standards. Activating one makes every agent grade structured observations against it. Ratify several at once via rubricIds:[…].
guidance.notWhen: Authoring or revising content — rubrics:propose. You are not the ratifying authority — leave it proposed and flag the Queen.
guidance.chaining: rubrics:list { status: "proposed" } → rubrics:get → rubrics:ratify { rubricIds:[…] }. Bulk: single | rubricIds[] → { ok, results, counts }; correlate by rubricId not position; one failure never fails the rest.

tools.name: rubrics:search
tools.description: Full-text search rubrics by id / characteristic / title / description. Use before rubrics:propose to avoid a duplicate, or to locate an existing standard by keywords.

guidance.when: Before proposing a rubric (dedup), or to find a standard covering a characteristic by keyword.
guidance.notWhen: You want a filtered list by status/characteristic — rubrics:list. You have the id — rubrics:get.
guidance.chaining: rubrics:search → rubrics:get (use the existing one) / rubrics:propose (if none fits).

tools.name: rubrics:trend
tools.description: The qualitative health TREND for a rubric — aggregate the every-turn Overwatch scorecard rating time-series per criterion over time, each with a direction (improving | worsening | stable | unknown), a rating distribution, first/latest rating, and the full chronological series. The health-over-time view ("queen-placement-health: degraded, worsening over 5 ratings"). Also returns a `staleness` signal (P-011): criteria the Overwatch persistently CANNOT assess (rated "unknown") — the rubric's model may have drifted from reality and should re-enter the queen↔scout loop for re-ratification. Reads the scorecards (P-013) — no new data.

guidance.when: You want to see how a rubric's criteria have trended OVER TIME — is a characteristic improving or worsening? which criteria are degrading across recent wakes? Or whether the rubric ITSELF is STALE (its model drifted — `staleness.stale`). The qualitative health-over-time view, vs a single point-in-time scorecard.
guidance.notWhen: You want the raw recent scorecards (point-in-time standing + completeness via missingKeys) — scorecards:list. You want the rubric DEFINITION (criteria/model/method) — rubrics:get. You want the cross-corpus ideation rollup — curation:state-of-hive.
guidance.chaining: rubrics:list { status: "active" } → rubrics:trend { rubricRef, since } → drill a worsening criterion via scorecards:list { rubricRef, since } → work_items:get on a scorecard issueId. If `staleness.stale`, re-ratify the rubric via the queen↔scout loop (revise template_data → plans:set-plan-status).

tools.name: saved_prompts:list
tools.description: List cross-client saved prompts for a scope: omit harness_slug for workspace-global prompts, or pass a harness slug for that harness. Returns the canonical PG rows (name, body, description, arg_hint) that materialize to the /name slash-commands in Claude / Codex / OMP.

guidance.when: When you need to inspect which saved `/name` prompts exist for a workspace or harness (e.g. to answer "what prompts are defined?" or before suggesting one).
guidance.notWhen: To create/edit/delete a prompt — that is the dashboard settings UI (POST /api/agent-mcp/saved-prompts). This tool is read-only.

tools.name: scorecards:freshness
tools.description: Has the Overwatch emitted a COMPLETE scorecard for a rubric since a given time (its last wake)? The emission-freshness check (monitor-the-monitor): returns status = fresh (a COMPLETE scorecard landed in-window) | partial-only (scorecards landed but ALL incomplete — a silent truncation) | stale (NOTHING landed — a silent emission gap), plus emitted / complete / count / partialCount, lastEmittedAt, lastCompleteAt, and latestMissingKeys (what is unrated right now). Reads scorecards:list (P-013); a "complete" scorecard rates every rubric criterion.

guidance.when: You want to know whether the Overwatch is actually emitting COMPLETE scorecards, not just whether it emitted anything — monitor-the-monitor. Did a complete hive-coordination-health scorecard land since the last wake (status fresh), or is it silently skipping (stale) / truncating to partials (partial-only)? Pass `since` = the last wake for a precise check.
guidance.notWhen: You want the scorecard ROWS + their ratings — scorecards:list. You want a criterion's rating TREND over time — rubrics:trend. You are FILING a scorecard — improvements:capture { lane: "observation", observation: { rubricRef, ratings } }.
guidance.chaining: scorecards:freshness { rubricRef: "hive-coordination-health", since } → status stale/partial-only ⇒ the Overwatch missed or truncated → scorecards:list { rubricRef, since } to see what (if anything) it emitted, or check latestMissingKeys for which criteria were dropped.

tools.name: scorecards:list
tools.description: Read structured rubric SCORECARDS back — rubric-graded observations (a rubricRef + per-criterion {rating, evidence}) that the Overwatch emits every turn and Scout consumes. Filter by rubricRef + sourceHive + a since time-window; newest-first. Each row carries {issueId, createdAt, createdBy, sourceHive, rubricRef, ratings, nKeys, missingKeys, rubricResolved} — nKeys + missingKeys expose completeness (a partial scorecard rated < all the rubric criteria). The read side of monitoring-the-monitor (was write-only before).

guidance.when: You want to SEE the rubric scorecards that have been emitted — e.g. did the Overwatch emit a COMPLETE hive-coordination-health scorecard recently (missingKeys empty)? what is one criterion's rating over time? is there an emission gap? The data substrate for trend/freshness/self-comparison monitoring.
guidance.notWhen: You want the RUBRIC definition (criteria/model/method) — rubrics:get / rubrics:list. You want the cross-corpus meta-pattern rollup incl. rubric ratings grouped for ideation — curation:state-of-hive. You are FILING a scorecard — improvements:capture { lane: "observation", observation: { rubricRef, ratings } }.
guidance.chaining: scorecards:list { rubricRef: "hive-coordination-health", since } → inspect missingKeys for completeness / ratings for the latest standing → drill into a row via work_items:get { id: issueId }, or rubrics:get { rubricId: rubricRef } for the criterion definitions.

tools.name: scout:grade-idea
tools.description: Grade a routed Scout idea 1–5 with optional feedback (≤2000 chars). Grades steer Scout's learning: fractional win credit in the lens weights + the critique primed into next cycles' ideator prompts. Key by ideaId or routedRef.

guidance.when: You want to score a routed Scout idea 1–5 (optional one-line critique) so Scout learns which lenses to favor. Key by ideaId (Scout view / learning.scout snapshot callers) or by routedRef — the routed artifact's change-feed ref 'plan:<slug>' | 'wi:<id>' | 'gym:<id>' — when you hold the artifact but not the ideaId (the Queen's triage path: grade each ungraded routed draft).
guidance.notWhen: Not an accept/reject of the routed artifact — a grade is a pure learning signal; the draft proceeds through normal triage regardless. Never pass grader attribution: gradedBy is derived from the caller role (Queen vs owner surface).
guidance.chaining: Nothing to chain: weights update on the next refreshScoutOutcomes pass and feedback enters ideator priming automatically. applied:false + reason 'owner-grade-sovereign' (Queen regrading an owner-graded row) is expected, not an error — owner grades are sovereign; the returned summary carries the standing grade.

tools.name: search:fulltext
tools.description: Search workspace prose (escalations, brainstorm notes, older operator turns) by keyword match (BM25-style). Ranked by relevance. Returns excerpts.

guidance.when: User references prose past the chat history budget ("remember when we decided pricing", "the X discussion from last week"), or asks about content in escalations/brainstorm where the right SQL filter is not obvious. Returns ranked snippets.
guidance.notWhen: For STRUCTURED queries on harness state, features, tasks, issues, or messages — use the dedicated tools (harness:status, tasks:list, etc). They are faster and more precise when the schema matches the query. For CODE recall, use `gitnexus:query`. For tasks/goals/projects text, use `search:query`.
guidance.chaining: Pair with `harness:escalation` or `harness:plan_reviews` to fetch the full row of a returned hit. The result `excerpt` is just the first 200 chars for ranking display.

tools.name: search:query
tools.description:
When to use: User asks an open-ended question that could match anything in the workspace ("anything about auth?", "find references to budget guard"). Cross-resource full-text search over tasks, goals, projects, audit, messages.

When NOT to use: For a SPECIFIC resource type, use the dedicated list/get tool — search is broader but ranked less precisely. For code-graph queries, use `gitnexus:query`.

guidance.when: User asks an open-ended question that could match anything in the workspace ("anything about auth?", "find references to budget guard"). Cross-resource full-text search over tasks, goals, projects, audit, messages.
guidance.notWhen: For a SPECIFIC resource type, use the dedicated list/get tool — search is broader but ranked less precisely. For code-graph queries, use `gitnexus:query`.

tools.name: search:semantic
tools.description: Semantic recall over workspace prose using embedding similarity. mode=hybrid combines with BM25 (search:fulltext) via Reciprocal Rank Fusion for best of both keyword and meaning. Falls back to BM25 if embeddings unavailable.

guidance.when: User asks about a concept by paraphrase rather than the exact keyword used in the recorded text. Examples: "when did we talk about authentication strategy" (could match "login flow", "auth approach", "JWT decision"). Prefer mode=hybrid for best recall.
guidance.notWhen: When the user knows the exact keyword they want. `search:fulltext` is faster + cheaper there (no embedding API call). For structured queries (tasks/goals/projects rows by title), use `search:query`.
guidance.chaining: Pair with `harness:escalation` or `harness:plan_reviews` to fetch the full row of a hit.

tools.name: sentinel:converse
tools.description: Sentinel/Herald brain conversation turn. The operator:converse brain loaded with the always-on, voice-first Herald persona (role=sentinel). Same lifecycle (prompt build, budget gate, LLM stream, spend, mem0); only the persona differs.

tools.name: slash:dispatch
tools.description: Fire a slash-exposed tool command AT another running agent: renders the same instruction a typed slash command yields and delivers it as the target's next turn via deliver-and-wake. The target executes the tool over its OWN session with its own gates; a manual-wake-mode target stages the command for owner review instead. For tip [Apply] buttons, wake-board actions, and agent-to-agent command dispatch.

guidance.when: You want ANOTHER agent to run a specific tool command — applying a coord:glance tip to the queen, a UI 'run this on that agent' action, a queen placing a precise command (not prose) onto a bee.
guidance.notWhen: Running the tool YOURSELF — just call it directly (the slash layer adds nothing in-session). Free-form coordination prose — coord:send. Reviewing what a manual-mode target staged — coord:wake-queue.

tools.name: storage:prune
tools.description: Delete a storage category's rows/entries older than N days (or all). Local-only safe categories only; federated categories are refused. Bloat tables also VACUUM FULL to reclaim disk. Pass dryRun to preview count + estimated reclaim.

guidance.when: The owner (or the Storage settings page) deliberately trims a local-only category — telemetry tables, the drained federation outbox, or on-disk session/scratch/flight-recorder stores.
guidance.notWhen: To read sizes use storage:usage. Federated categories (plans/features/issues/coord) are refused — trimming would change what peers see.
guidance.chaining: storage:usage → storage:prune { category, olderThanDays, dryRun: true } → review reclaim → storage:prune { category, olderThanDays }.

tools.name: storage:usage
tools.description: Live storage usage by category (PG tables grouped by federation class + on-disk stores), each with total size, an age distribution, and whether it is safe to trim. Read-only.

guidance.when: Inspecting what is consuming local storage, or before a trim, to see per-category size + the age distribution and which categories are federated (read-only).
guidance.notWhen: To actually delete, use storage:prune (with dryRun first). This never deletes.
guidance.chaining: storage:usage → storage:prune { category, olderThanDays, dryRun: true } → storage:prune { category, olderThanDays }.

tools.name: substrate:revoke_contributor
tools.description: OWNER action: revoke another contributor by adding their device pubkeys to a revocation set. Scope is per-HARNESS (`harnessSlug`) or per-HIVE (`hiveSlug` — revokes from the whole Hive's federation at once, P-006). Every peer honors it on the next admission re-verify and drops them from live federation. Harness scope requires a repo-admin token; Hive scope requires holding the Hive key.

guidance.when: OWNER action: revoke ANOTHER contributor by adding their device pubkeys to a revocation set. Pass `harnessSlug` to drop them from ONE harness's federation (repo-admin token), or `hiveSlug` to drop them from the WHOLE Hive's federation in one action (P-006 — requires this Swarm to hold the Hive key). Use when a contributor is a confirmed bad actor, their account is compromised, or they must be removed from the shared federation entirely.
guidance.notWhen: Revoking your OWN device — use `substrate:revoke_self_device` instead. For harness scope, not when the token lacks GitHub admin on the shared repo. For Hive scope, not when this Swarm does not hold the Hive private key (only the owning Swarm may revoke Hive-wide).
guidance.chaining: Resolve the contributor's githubUserId from the Contributors tab, `dev:dogfood_substrate_status`, `harness:membership`, or `hive:get` first — githubUserId is the stable numeric GitHub user id, not the login.

tools.name: substrate:revoke_self_device
tools.description: Revoke one of your own device pubkeys from a harness (lost or rotated device). Adds the pubkey to revoked_pubkeys in your contributor row, replicates to peers, and drops the device from the booted substrate immediately.

guidance.when: Revoke ONE of your OWN device keys from a harness (a lost or rotated device) so peers stop admitting it.
guidance.notWhen: Revoking ANOTHER contributor's key / kicking out a bad actor — not supported (self-revocation only, v2 for owner-revocation).
guidance.chaining: Resolve the device pubkey from the contributor's own device_attestations first (e.g. via dev:dogfood_substrate_status or the Contributors tab).

tools.name: tasks:create
tools.description:
When to use: User asks to add a task / TODO / item to track. Always confirm the title out loud before calling — task creation isn't silent.

When NOT to use: For asking the harness to DO work (write code, run validation), use `<spawn role="worker" />` instead — tasks track intent, spawns execute it.

Chaining: After creating, mention the task id in your reply so the user can refer back.

guidance.when: User asks to add a task / TODO / item to track. Always confirm the title out loud before calling — task creation isn't silent.
guidance.notWhen: For asking the harness to DO work (write code, run validation), use `<spawn role="worker" />` instead — tasks track intent, spawns execute it.
guidance.chaining: After creating, mention the task id in your reply so the user can refer back.

tools.name: tasks:get
tools.description:
When to use: User names a specific task ("the auth task", "task ABC-123") and you need its full body.

When NOT to use: For a list of tasks, use `tasks:list` first. Don't call `tasks:get` speculatively across many ids — list returns enough for most "what's the gist" questions.

Chaining: Follow `tasks:list` to find the id.

guidance.when: User names a specific task ("the auth task", "task ABC-123") and you need its full body.
guidance.notWhen: For a list of tasks, use `tasks:list` first. Don't call `tasks:get` speculatively across many ids — list returns enough for most "what's the gist" questions.
guidance.chaining: Follow `tasks:list` to find the id.

tools.name: tasks:list
tools.description:
When to use: User asks "what tasks do I have?", "what's on my plate", or you need a task id before calling `tasks:get`/`tasks:update`/`tasks:close`.

When NOT to use: For ONE task by id, use `tasks:get`. For creating a task, use `tasks:create`. For PROJECTS / FEATURES (work the harness is doing), use `harness:*` — tasks are separate from harness features.

Chaining: Pair with `tasks:get` for detail on a specific row.

guidance.when: User asks "what tasks do I have?", "what's on my plate", or you need a task id before calling `tasks:get`/`tasks:update`/`tasks:close`.
guidance.notWhen: For ONE task by id, use `tasks:get`. For creating a task, use `tasks:create`. For PROJECTS / FEATURES (work the harness is doing), use `harness:*` — tasks are separate from harness features.
guidance.chaining: Pair with `tasks:get` for detail on a specific row.

tools.name: telemetry:set_buffer
tools.description: Read/set/reset the dispatch telemetry-buffer sizing (maxPending / debounceMs / maxBatch) at runtime, merged over the baked defaults. Raise maxPending to ride out a PG-stall burst without shedding telemetry, or tune debounce/batch — no deploy. Empty override / kill-switch off (papercusp-telemetry-buffer-config) = byte-identical. set/reset audited + one-call-revertible.

guidance.when: Telemetry rows are being dropped under burst (the "telemetry queue overflow" warning) — raise maxPending; or tune flush debounce/batch for PG load. get to inspect the effective config + override.
guidance.notWhen: Not for quota/rate limits (operator:rate_limit_config), nor for retention (storage settings). This only sizes the in-memory telemetry flush queue.
guidance.chaining: config:list-overrides shows the active telemetry-buffer override; config:reset-overrides reverts it. The kill-switch papercusp-telemetry-buffer-config (default ON) forces the baked defaults when OFF.

tools.name: topics:create
tools.description: Create a coordination topic: a short slug + one-sentence description. Prefer an existing topic (topics:list) over a near-duplicate. Notifies new_topic subscribers; re-creating an existing slug is a no-op.

guidance.when: No existing topic fits a relevance area you (and likely others) will want to follow. Keep the slug to a word or two; the description to one sentence.
guidance.notWhen: A close-enough topic already exists in topics:list — subscribe/tag to that instead. Near-duplicates get merged with topics:merge.

tools.name: topics:feed
tools.description: Read everything tagged with one OR many topics — across issues, conversations, features, and plans — the whole work-stream of an area. Each item carries its title + current state. Single: { topic }. Many: { topics:[…] } or items:[{ topic }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, topic, count, items | error }], counts } — correlate by topic, not position; a topic that fails to read never fails the rest.

guidance.when: To understand all current work in a relevance area before you start in it, or to see what is happening with e.g. `zero-cache` across every object kind. Read several areas at once via topics:[…].
guidance.notWhen: You want messages waiting for you (coord:inbox) or just the list of topics (topics:list).
guidance.chaining: topics:list → topics:feed { topic } → issues:get / conversations:get on an item.

tools.name: topics:list
tools.description: List coordination topics (tag + one-sentence description) and your own active topic subscriptions. A topic = a relevance area you can follow to have its updates injected into your context.

guidance.when: At the start of work, to see the shared topic taxonomy before tagging/subscribing — and to prefer an existing topic over creating a near-duplicate (D-004).
guidance.notWhen: You want the messages already waiting for you — that is coord:inbox, not this.
guidance.chaining: topics:list → topics:subscribe (follow a relevant area) or topics:create (only if nothing fits).

tools.name: topics:merge
tools.description: Merge topic `from` into `into`: aliases the slug (tags resolve to the target) and re-points the merged topic’s subscribers onto the target. The dedup for accidental near-duplicate topics.

guidance.when: topics:list shows two topics that mean the same thing — fold the lesser-used into the better one.
guidance.notWhen: The two topics are genuinely distinct areas — keep both.

tools.name: topics:subscribe
tools.description: Subscribe to one OR many topics so their updates are injected into your inbox — the named sugar for watch(topic,{wake:false}). mode = full | digest | mention (D-006 noise tiering). Subscribe to the built-in `new_topic` to learn of new topics as they appear. Idempotent — re-subscribing updates the mode/TTL. Single: { topic, mode?, ttl_sec? }. Many same mode: { topics:[…], mode?, ttl_sec? }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ topic, mode?, ttl_sec? }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, topic, subscription? | error }], counts } — correlate by topic, not position; one failure never fails the rest.

guidance.when: A topic in topics:list is relevant to your current work and you want its updates pushed to you. Pick digest for high-churn areas, mention to stay quiet. Subscribe to several at once via topics:[…] or items:[…].
guidance.notWhen: You only need a one-time look — just topics:list. To follow a specific object (one thread/issue), that is the object’s own subscribe, not a topic.
guidance.chaining: topics:list → topics:subscribe; topics:unsubscribe to stop.

tools.name: topics:tag
tools.description: Tag one OR many coordination objects (issue / conversation / feature / plan) with a topic so each appears in that topic's feed and its changes reach the topic's subscribers. Pass remove:true to untag. Single: { object_kind, object_ref, topic, remove? }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ object_kind, object_ref, topic, remove? }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, topic, object, topics? | error }], counts } — correlate by topic (not position); one failure never fails the rest.

guidance.when: You want a feature/plan/issue/conversation to be visible to everyone following a relevance area — tag it with the topic. Tag several at once via items:[…].
guidance.notWhen: The topic does not exist yet — topics:create it first (prefer an existing one). For an issue you can also use issues:tag.
guidance.chaining: topics:list → topics:tag { object_kind, object_ref, topic } → topics:feed { topic }.

tools.name: topics:unsubscribe
tools.description: Unsubscribe from one OR many topics. Idempotent — unsubscribing from a topic you do not follow is a no-op. Single: { topic }. Many: { topics:[…] } or items:[{ topic }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, topic, error? }], counts } — correlate by topic, not position; one failure never fails the rest.

guidance.when: A topic you followed is no longer relevant and its updates are noise. Drop several at once via topics:[…].
guidance.notWhen: You want to mute briefly — set the subscription to mention mode via topics:subscribe instead of dropping it.

tools.name: trust:add
tools.description: Add a GitHub user id to the owner's LOCAL trust list — a SECURITY GRANT: a VERIFIED-author remote work item from this user may then auto-run on the owner's install (across every hive the owner is in), bypassing per-item screening. Owner-scoped, local-only, never federated. Audited.

guidance.when: The owner deliberately trusts a GitHub user so their verified remote work auto-runs without screening. Pass the numeric github_user_id (matches hive_members.github_user_id).
guidance.notWhen: To see who is trusted use trust:list; to revoke use trust:remove. This grants auto-run privilege — only the owner grants trust (an unverified or self-claimed author is never auto-admitted regardless).
guidance.chaining: trust:list (who is trusted) → trust:add { githubUserId, note? }.

tools.name: trust:list
tools.description: List the owner's trusted GitHub user ids — the LOCAL, owner-scoped trust list the admission gate consults so a VERIFIED trusted author's remote (federated) work may auto-run without per-item screening.

guidance.when: Show who the owner trusts to auto-run foreign/federated work — the owner-scoped, local-only trust list (shared-hive-trust-admission).
guidance.notWhen: To grant or revoke trust use trust:add / trust:remove. This is read-only.
guidance.chaining: trust:list → trust:add { githubUserId } / trust:remove { githubUserId }.

tools.name: trust:remove
tools.description: Remove a GitHub user id from the owner's LOCAL trust list — revokes the auto-run privilege; their verified remote work returns to per-item screening. Owner-scoped, local-only. Audited.

guidance.when: The owner revokes trust in a GitHub user (their remote work should no longer auto-run).
guidance.notWhen: To grant trust use trust:add; to view the list use trust:list.
guidance.chaining: trust:list → trust:remove { githubUserId }.

tools.name: tui:dispatch
tools.description: Dispatch a control intent to a running pui (terminal workbench) and wait for the result. Built-in intents: get_state ({}) → snapshot of the pui AppState (active tab, selections, counts, chat state, live panes); set_tab ({tab:"Operator"|"Plans"|"Sessions"|"Fleet"|…}); set_harness ({slug}); select ({list:"plans"|"roster"|"inbox"|"features"|"issues"|"docs", index}); open_chat ({}) → focus the operator chat pane; focus_pane ({pane_id}) → focus a worker's zellij pane (ids from get_state.panes). client_id targets the pui instance (its workbench owner key, $USER@$HOSTNAME by default).

guidance.when: You need to drive or read a running pui terminal workbench — switch its tab, change its active harness, move a selection, or read its current state. Side-effect tool: writes a tui_intents row the pui consumes over SSE.
guidance.notWhen: For the browser/desktop UI use `ui:dispatch`. For showing a question + choices use `chat:ask_choice`. For delegating work use `<spawn>` — tui:dispatch is UI control, not work delegation.

tools.name: turn:interrupt
tools.description: End a peer agent's CURRENT turn (the dual of a wake). mode:'cooperative' injects a high-priority `yield` so the peer reaches a safe checkpoint, saves partial state, releases locks, and ends its turn (the polite default; DEFERS if the target holds file locks). mode:'force' ends the turn NOW, mid-thinking — Ctrl+C to a managed-pty session or SIGINT to a headless one (the turn ends; the session stays resumable). reason is REQUIRED + audited; storm-rate-limited so it can't be used to halt the fleet.

guidance.when: A peer is doing the wrong thing / working on something now-obsolete / looping, and you need its current turn to STOP. Prefer cooperative (it wraps up cleanly + saves); use force only when it must stop mid-thinking and cooperative was ignored or there's no time.
guidance.notWhen: To wake an IDLE peer, use coord:send {wake:true} — interrupt is for a RUNNING peer. To hand work over, coord:handoff. Don't force a peer that holds file locks unless necessary (it can orphan a half-written edit) — cooperative defers exactly to avoid that.

tools.name: ui:dispatch
tools.description: Dispatch a UI intent to a browser tab and wait for the result. Defaults client_id to ctx.uiClientId (the tab that spawned the agent). Built-in intents: set_url ({params:{...}}), snapshot ({selector?,mode?}), read_visible_text, focus, scroll_into_view, click. Pages can register additional intents via useUiIntent(name, handler).

guidance.when: You need to make something happen in the user's browser tab — open the panel, navigate, focus a card, etc. Side-effect tool: writes a ui_intents row the tab consumes via SSE.
guidance.notWhen: For showing a question + choices in the chat, use `chat:ask_choice` (renders inline buttons). For asking the operator brain to delegate work, use `<spawn>` — `ui:dispatch` is for UI side effects, not work delegation.

tools.name: ui:get_state
tools.description: Read the URL state of a browser tab (defaults to the tab that spawned the agent via ctx.uiClientId). Returns { url, pathname, params, title, last_seen_at }. Use to answer "what is the user looking at?" — nuqs serializes panel/tab/filter/selection state to the URL, so the params object reflects most UI state.

guidance.when: User asks "what am I looking at?", "what page am I on?", or you need to verify a panel state before acting ("is the panel already open?").
guidance.notWhen: Tool calls ARE idempotent — `panel_open` when already open is fine. Don't pre-check just to skip a call; the persona rule is "always call". Use `ui:get_state` only when you need to BRANCH on what the user is looking at.

tools.name: ui:list_clients
tools.description: List open browser tabs (UI clients) with active presence. Each entry is { client_id, workspace_id, url, title, last_seen_at, opened_at, is_self }. is_self=true when the client matches ctx.uiClientId (i.e., the tab that spawned the agent).

guidance.when: You need to know which browser tab(s) the user has open before calling `ui:dispatch`. Returns client ids the operator can target.
guidance.notWhen: In the operator-converse path, ctx.uiClientId is already populated — you can target the user's current tab directly via `ui:dispatch`. Only list when you need to choose between multiple tabs.
guidance.chaining: Pair with `ui:get_state` to see what each tab is on, then `ui:dispatch` to act.

tools.name: voice:agent
tools.description: Voice agent peer: toggle channel listening (STT) or the converse BRAIN (auto-reply), report status, or speak text (TTS) into the active channel.

guidance.when: Toggle the agent's ears ({op:'enable'|'disable'}), its auto-reply brain ({op:'brain', on}), read {op:'status'}, or speak into the channel ({op:'say', text}).
guidance.notWhen: Joining/leaving the channel itself is `voice:join`/`voice:leave`; this controls only the agent's listen/think/speak behaviors on top.
guidance.chaining: voice:join → voice:agent {op:'brain', on:true} (ears + auto-reply: peer speech → operator-converse → spoken reply). For manual control use {op:'enable'} then {op:'say', text:'…'}.

tools.name: voice:channels
tools.description: List/create/remove P2P voice channels (the durable registry; a channel maps a name to a swarm topic).

guidance.when: Manage the voice-channel registry — list what channels exist, create one before joining it, or remove a stale one.
guidance.notWhen: To enter/exit a channel use `voice:join` / `voice:leave`; for who's in a channel right now use `voice:status`.
guidance.chaining: voice:channels {op:'create'} → voice:join {channel} → voice:status.

tools.name: voice:join
tools.description: Join a P2P voice channel by id or name — starts the voice swarm, announces the topic, connects to peers.

guidance.when: Enter a voice channel (by id or name from `voice:channels`). One active channel at a time; joining another leaves the current one.
guidance.notWhen: Don't poll this — `voice:status` reads the live state; the local voice socket pushes status events to UI clients.
guidance.chaining: voice:channels {op:'list'} → voice:join → speak via the local voice socket (pui/desktop) → voice:leave.

tools.name: voice:leave
tools.description: Leave the active P2P voice channel (drops peer connections, releases the swarm topic).

guidance.when: Exit the current voice channel. Safe no-op when not in one.
guidance.notWhen: Removing a channel from the registry is `voice:channels {op:'remove'}` — leaving only ends THIS node's participation.

tools.name: voice:status
tools.description: Live voice state: active channel, mute, and in-channel peers (id/label/muted/speaking).

guidance.when: Read who's in the active voice channel right now (presence is in-band — liveness IS the peer connection).
guidance.notWhen: The durable channel LIST is `voice:channels {op:'list'}` — status only covers the channel this node is in.

tools.name: voice:transcript
tools.description: Read live speech transcripts from the active voice channel: enable buffering (turns the ears on), then read the most-recent utterances or the delta since a cursor. The OBSERVE seam for an agent to react to spoken input WITHOUT the auto-reply brain.

guidance.when: Let an agent (e.g. a narrator/host) HEAR what peers said and react on its own terms — {op:'enable'} once, then poll {op:'read', since:<cursor>} for new utterances. Unlike voice:agent {op:'brain'}, this never auto-replies — you decide what to do with the speech.
guidance.notWhen: For the agent to AUTO-converse (peer speech → spoken reply) use `voice:agent {op:'brain', on:true}` instead. Buffering needs the ears: {op:'enable'} turns them on; {op:'disable'} stops buffering but leaves the shared ears (toggle those via voice:agent).
guidance.chaining: voice:join → voice:transcript {op:'enable'} → voice:transcript {op:'read'} (note the cursor) → … → voice:transcript {op:'read', since:<cursor>} for only what's new.

tools.name: watch:create
tools.description: The unified subscription primitive — watch(pattern, {wake, once, min_sleep_sec, urgency, timeout_sec, mode}): register an interest, receive a delivery. DELIVERY — wake:false (DEFAULT, cheap) injects updates into your coord inbox (seen on your next natural turn, no token cost); wake:true (opt-in, a turn = tokens) re-invokes you when it fires. CARDINALITY — once:true is one-shot (fires once, auto-consumes — a grant/readiness); once:false is standing (re-fires on every match). Named sugar presets: `events:await {key}` = watch(key,{wake:true,once:true}); `topics:subscribe {topic}` = watch(topic,{wake:false}). Lifecycle: events:cancel / events:status (wake) · topics:unsubscribe (inject).

guidance.when: Register interest in something and receive its updates. Prefer wake:false (inject) for continuous awareness of a churning area — no cost. Use wake:true ONLY for specific readiness ("wake me when THIS grant/lock/deadline is ready"); for a standing wake watch set min_sleep_sec to bound the re-wake rate. once:true for a one-shot grant; once:false to keep following.
guidance.notWhen: A sub-minute wait inside one turn — just do the bounded blocking call. A recurring TIME schedule — the pot/routines own time-based wakes. Ambient interest where a wake would burn turns — use wake:false.
guidance.chaining: wake:true → end your turn; on wake the turn text carries the event + payload. events:cancel (wake) / topics:unsubscribe (inject) to stop; events:status to inspect your active wake watches + recent wakes.

tools.name: wiki:backlinks
tools.description: Find markdown files that reference [[target]] across the workspace, for one OR many pages in ONE call — pass `target` for one or `targets:[…]` for several (1–100), with an optional shared `harness` filter. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, target, harness, hits[] | error }], counts } — correlate each result by its target, not by position; one failed scan never fails the rest.

guidance.when: User asks "what links to X?", "where is `[[name]]` referenced?". Wiki-style backlink lookup across markdown files. Look up several pages at once via `targets:[…]`.
guidance.notWhen: For cross-resource full-text search, use `search:query`. For markdown TOC, use `harness:markdown_index`.
guidance.chaining: single `target` | `targets:[…]` → { ok, results:[{ ok, target, harness, hits[] | error }], counts } — correlate by target not position; one failure never fails the rest.

tools.name: work_items:amend
tools.description: Record a structural decision on a plan-run node (split | drop | reapproach | expand | note) durably, in one call. The Queen/operator disposes; a bee proposes. A disruptive amend on an in-flight node is flagged NEEDS-COMPENSATION (coordinate, never silently yank). The record is the commit-before-dispatch truth — amend BEFORE dispatching the dependent work.

guidance.when: You are making (or, as a bee, PROPOSING) a non-re-derivable structural change to a plan-run node — split it, drop/re-approach the approach, expand a deferred region. Record it here in ONE call before dispatching the dependent work; the durable record is the resumable truth.
guidance.notWhen: A routine progress update / finding → work_items:comment. Re-prioritizing the frontier (re-derivable, costs nothing to lose) → no amend needed. Finishing a node → work_items:complete / set_state.
guidance.chaining: work_items:get → work_items:amend { id, kind, rationale }. A bee PROPOSES (disposition=proposed); the Queen DISPOSES. requiresCompensation=true ⇒ a worker is mid-execution on the node — coordinate (coord:send) before/with the change.

tools.name: work_items:checkpoint
tools.description: Write (or clear) one OR many work-items' checkpoints — a compressed snapshot of your in-flight state. Single: { id, checkpoint? }. Many: items:[{ id, checkpoint?, harness? }]. Your prior transcript does NOT carry across a task boundary / re-spawn; the checkpoint is your continuity, re-injected on the next invocation of that item (yours or a successor's). Replace-on-write; blank/omitted clears. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, harness, cleared, length, by | error }], counts } — correlate by id.

guidance.when: At a task boundary or on graceful eviction, before you finish/yield: persist what a successor (or your next fresh-context wake) needs to continue — what is done, what is left, current approach, gotchas, open threads. Keep it COMPRESSED (a digest, not a transcript).
guidance.notWhen: Mid-task scratch state that the live transcript already holds — checkpoint only the durable, cross-boundary gist. Do not dump file contents or full tool output.
guidance.chaining: work_items:checkpoint { id, checkpoint } before work_items:complete / on yield. Pass blank to clear a stale note.

tools.name: work_items:claim
tools.description: Claim one OR many work-items (assign to yourself, or to `assignee`). Claiming a feature sets taken_by; an issue sets assignee. Single: { id, assignee? }. Many same assignee: { ids:[…], assignee? }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ id, assignee?, harness? }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, workItem? | error, holder? }], counts } — correlate by id; a claim_conflict on one item never fails the rest.

guidance.when: You are starting work on work-item(s) — claim so peers do not duplicate. Claim a swath at once via { ids:[…] }.
guidance.notWhen: A per-item `claim_conflict` means a LIVE peer holds it — coordinate with the `holder` (coord:send) or pick another item; do not blind-retry. (If the holder is dead, the stale-claim reclaim lane frees it.)
guidance.chaining: work_items:list → work_items:claim → work_items:set_state → work_items:release/close.

tools.name: work_items:claim_next
tools.description: Self-select: atomically claim the OLDEST unclaimed work-item in a harness (tuple-space `in` via SKIP LOCKED + work-stealing). Competing agents never double-claim. Returns the claimed item or null.

guidance.when: You are an idle agent picking up work — prefer this self-selection over waiting to be assigned. Returns the oldest claimable feature-family item, now yours.
guidance.notWhen: When a SPECIFIC item must go to a SPECIFIC agent — that is work_items:claim with an explicit assignee (named assignment, the exception).
guidance.chaining: work_items:claim_next → work_items:set_state → work_items:release.

tools.name: work_items:claim_replica
tools.description: Claim one replica slot of a HIGH-STAKES (redundancy>1) work-item — the redundancy analogue of claim_next. Up to N distinct Swarms each get a distinct slot of the SAME item and run it independently. Returns the slot (replica_index + claim_id) or null when not high-stakes / all slots held.

guidance.when: You are a Swarm picking up a high-stakes item that is being run redundantly. Claim a replica slot, run the item independently, then record your result.
guidance.notWhen: A normal exactly-once item — that is work_items:claim_next. Marking an item high-stakes — that is work_items:set_redundancy.
guidance.chaining: work_items:claim_replica → (run the item) → work_items:record_replica_result { replicaIndex } → work_items:judge_redundancy resolves the winner.

tools.name: work_items:co_locate
tools.description: The Queen's co-location lever: stamp a work-item's Swarm affinity so tightly-coupled work runs on the SAME Swarm (instant coordination) and loosely-coupled work spreads. Pin with { swarm }, decide with { coLocateWith, tight? }, or read the current affinity with just { workItem }.

guidance.when: You are the Queen placing work: co-locate a work-item with its tight collaborators on one Swarm (coLocateWith), pin it to a specific Swarm (swarm), or check where it is affined. The affinity is honored by claim_next once the per-Hive claim lease is active.
guidance.notWhen: Ranking a bee's queue (work_items:reorder) or sending a specific item to a specific agent (work_items:claim). Co-location is about WHICH SWARM, not which bee.
guidance.chaining: fleet:assignments (see where collaborators run) → work_items:co_locate { workItem, coLocateWith } → the affined Swarm claims it under the lease.

tools.name: work_items:comment
tools.description: Comment on one OR many work-items (any kind) in one call. Single: { id, body }. Many: items:[{ id, body, harness? }]. Appends to each item's thread (created on first comment) and notifies its subscribers. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, post? | error }], counts } — correlate by id; a not-found item never fails the rest.

guidance.when: You have an update, finding, or question to post on one or more work-items. Comment on several at once via items:[…] instead of one call each.
guidance.notWhen: A contextual aside not tied to a work-item → coord:send. A structured completion → work_items:complete.
guidance.chaining: work_items:get → work_items:comment; work_items:subscribe to follow the thread.

tools.name: work_items:complete
tools.description: Finish one OR many work-items with a STRUCTURED completion record (what landed / migrations / tests / deferred-set) instead of a hand-written coord:send prose dump. The system renders + broadcasts each completion from the fields — you spend no tokens narrating. Optionally also transitions each item to a terminal `state`. Single: { id, completion }. Many: items:[{ id, completion, state?, harness? }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, workItem, completion, reflect, stateError? } | error], counts } — act on each returned `reflect` step once, now.

guidance.when: You finished work-item(s) / plan-item(s) / brief(s). Fill the structured completion fields (summary, whatLanded, migrations, tests, deferred) — do NOT also coord:send a prose summary; this emits it. Finish several at once via items:[…].
guidance.notWhen: For a contextual aside that is not a completion (a question, a design note), use coord:send. To only change state without a completion record, use work_items:set_state.
guidance.chaining: work_items:claim → … → work_items:complete { id, completion }. The completion auto-emits to coord:inbox; no coord:send needed. Then read each returned `reflect` step (self-learning loop): if any friction marker bit you, file it once via improvements:capture — else capture nothing.

tools.name: work_items:create
tools.description: Create ONE or MANY work-items of any kind — feature | research-task | chunk | bug | change. Returns kind-independent WI-NNN ids. bug/change file a tracked issue; feature/research-task/chunk enter the harness work queue. Single: { kind, title, … }. Many: items:[{ kind, title, … }] with batch-level harness / workspace / assign_all_to_self. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, title, workItem } | { ok:false, title, error }], counts } — a mirror-duplicate or one bad item never fails the rest. Dedup with work_items:list/search first.

guidance.when: You want to track unit(s) of work an agent will do. Pick the kind: bug (broken), change (DX ask / one-off), feature (pipeline work-unit), research-task, or chunk (sub-unit, pass `parent`). File several at once via items:[…] instead of a round-trip each.
guidance.notWhen: A passing question with no owner → coord:ask. A validator finding inside a live pipeline run → the validator pipeline, not here.
guidance.chaining: work_items:list (dedup) → work_items:create → work_items:claim/claim_next when you start → work_items:set_state on progress; work_items:promote to give a bug/change a pipeline run.

tools.name: work_items:expand
tools.description: Expand a deferred-expansion node into child work_items in one call. The Queen/operator DISPOSES (children are created); a bee PROPOSES (recorded, the steerer ratifies). Each child carries payload.expanded_from = the parent id. Lets a plan-run start shallow and self-elaborate at the point of best context.

guidance.when: You have reached an "expand-here" node (or any node) that should now fan out into concrete child work_items — the decomposition you deferred until you had the context to make it well.
guidance.notWhen: A flat structural note / re-approach → work_items:amend. A single follow-up → just create/convert one work_item. Re-prioritizing existing nodes → no expansion.
guidance.chaining: work_items:get → work_items:expand { id, children:[{title, files?, brief?}] }. A bee PROPOSES (disposition=proposed, nothing created yet); the Queen DISPOSES (children created with payload.expanded_from = parent).

tools.name: work_items:get
tools.description: Fetch one OR many work-items by id (WI-/F-/EI-…) across every kind in ONE call — pass `id` for one or `ids` for several (1–100). Pass `harness` to disambiguate a feature id that may repeat across harnesses. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, workItem?, error? }], counts } — correlate each result by its id, not by position; a missing id comes back as that item's { ok:false } without failing the rest.

guidance.when: You have one or more work-item ids and need their full state (kind, lifecycle, assignee, parent). Pass every id you need at once via `ids` instead of calling per id.
guidance.notWhen: Browsing or filtering the queue → work_items:list / work_items:search (they already return many rows).
guidance.chaining: work_items:list → work_items:get { ids:[…] } for detail on the ones you care about.

tools.name: work_items:judge_redundancy
tools.description: Judge a high-stakes item's redundant replicas + adopt the winner (reuse gym:judge). Scores each complete replica's result on the gym rubric, picks the highest composite (deterministic tie-break), settles the item to passed, marks winner/losers. Needs ≥2 complete replicas. Returns the winner + every replica's score.

guidance.when: All (or ≥2) replicas of a high-stakes item have recorded their results and you want to pick + adopt the best one. The frozen Opus judge compares them above the per-replica validators.
guidance.notWhen: Fewer than 2 replicas have recorded (wait for them). A normal exactly-once item (it has no replicas to compare). Scoring a gym optimization run — that is gym:judge directly.
guidance.chaining: work_items:set_redundancy → claim_replica (×N) → record_replica_result (×N) → work_items:judge_redundancy (adopt winner).

tools.name: work_items:link
tools.description: Link one OR many work-items to targets (rel: blocks | relates | duplicates | fixes) — single inline { id, rel, target_id } or items:[{ id, rel, target_id | target_kind+target_ref, remove? }] (a source can fan out to many targets in one call). Blocking works across kinds. Pass remove:true to unlink. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, rel, dst? | error }], counts }.

guidance.when: You discovered one or more dependencies/relationships: a work-item blocks/relates-to/duplicates/fixes other work-items or plan items. Create several edges at once via items:[…].
guidance.chaining: work_items:get both sides → work_items:link { rel:"blocks", target_id } (or items:[…]).

tools.name: work_items:list
tools.description: List work-items across kinds (feature/research-task/chunk/bug/change). Default shows top-level items (chunks are hidden — pass parent or includeChildren). Filter by harness, kind, state. Returns the WorkItem array directly — each row's summary is EXCERPTED to keep the list bounded (a row carries summary_truncated + summary_full_chars when cut); use work_items:get { id } for a full body.

guidance.when: You want the current work-items in a harness (or operator-wide). Default hides chunks; pass `parent` to see a parent's chunks. Each row carries `priority` (the shared backlog order, LOWER = claimed sooner) so the Queen can read the whole backlog's order in one call before steering it with work_items:set_priority.
guidance.chaining: work_items:list → work_items:get { id } for detail; work_items:claim to take one; work_items:set_priority to re-order the backlog.

tools.name: work_items:observe
tools.description: Observe one OR many work-items WITHOUT claiming (tuple-space `rd`) — pass `id` for one or `ids` for several (1–100): reports each item's availability + who holds it. Distinct from claim (`in`). Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, …observation | error }], counts } — correlate by id, not position.

guidance.when: Inspect one or more work-items' claimability before deciding to claim — read without taking. Pass every id you are weighing at once.
guidance.chaining: work_items:observe → work_items:claim (if available).

tools.name: work_items:pickup
tools.description: Pick up a specific work-item in ONE call: fetch its full detail, claim it for you, and (when `intent` is given) declare your intent / plan lane. Collapses the get→claim(→declare-intent) round-trips into one and closes the get→claim race.

guidance.when: You have decided to work a SPECIFIC work-item id — pickup fetches its detail, claims it, and optionally declares your intent in one round-trip instead of work_items:get → work_items:claim → coord:declare-intent.
guidance.notWhen: You are still deciding whether to take it (inspect first with work_items:get), or you want the oldest unassigned item regardless of which (work_items:claim_next).
guidance.chaining: work_items:list → work_items:pickup { id, intent } → work → work_items:complete.

tools.name: work_items:promote
tools.description: Promote one OR many bug/change work-items into a feature pipeline run (mints an F-FIX feature in the target harness and links it). Single: { id, harness? }. Many: items:[{ id, harness? }]. An operator-scope item needs an explicit harness. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, … | error }], counts } — correlate by id; one failure never fails the rest.

guidance.when: A filed bug/change is ready to be worked by the pipeline — for one item or several at once.
guidance.notWhen: It is a passing idea (leave it filed) or already a feature.
guidance.chaining: work_items:create { kind:"bug" } → work_items:promote { harness } → the pipeline picks up the feature.

tools.name: work_items:reclaim_config
tools.description: Read or set the stale-claim reclaim policy: reclaimGraceMs (a heartbeat-less claim is presumed orphaned + reclaimed after this; default = the 10-min liveness window) and reclaimRequeueCap (requeues before a mid-flight item is dead-lettered to blocked; default 3). Threaded into the periodic reclaim sweep. set is audited + one-call-revertible.

guidance.when: Tighten reclaim (shorter grace) to free orphaned work faster after a crash wave, or loosen it to avoid reclaiming briefly-quiet live work; raise the requeue cap to retry flaky items more before dead-lettering.
guidance.notWhen: For the presence/liveness window itself (shared STALE_MS source) this only overrides the RECLAIM grace. For handoff TTL use coord:handoff_config; for session reaping use coord:session_reaper_config.
guidance.chaining: fleet:assignments shows orphaned claims; config:list-overrides shows the active override; config:reset-overrides reverts it.

tools.name: work_items:record_replica_result
tools.description: Record your replica's result for a high-stakes item slot you hold + mark it complete (ready to judge). `text` is the distilled output the judge scores (and the winner's is adopted). Owner-checked — no double-record.

guidance.when: You finished running your replica of a high-stakes item — record the distilled result so the judge can compare it against the other Swarms.
guidance.notWhen: A normal item — that is work_items:complete / work_items:set_state. You do not hold the slot (you must claim_replica first).
guidance.chaining: work_items:claim_replica → (run) → work_items:record_replica_result → work_items:judge_redundancy.

tools.name: work_items:redundancy_status
tools.description: Read one OR many work-items' redundancy config + replica ledger (pass `id` for one or `ids` for several, all in the shared `harness`): target N, each slot's status (claimed/complete/winner/loser), owner, lease expiry, and judge verdict. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, redundancy, completeCount, judgeable, replicas, … | error }], counts }.

guidance.when: Checking how one or more high-stakes items are progressing across their Swarms — how many replicas completed, whether judged, which replica won.
guidance.notWhen: A normal item (it has no replicas). The plain item state — that is work_items:get.
guidance.chaining: work_items:redundancy_status → (if ≥2 complete) work_items:judge_redundancy.

tools.name: work_items:release
tools.description: Release one OR many work-items (clear assignee / taken_by) so another agent can pick them up. Single: { id }. Many: { ids:[…] } or items:[{ id, harness? }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, workItem? | error }], counts } — correlate by id; a not-found item never fails the rest.

guidance.when: You claimed work-item(s) but are no longer working them. Release several at once via ids:[…].
guidance.chaining: work_items:claim → … → work_items:release.

tools.name: work_items:reorder
tools.description: Move one OR many work-items to a position (`rank`, 0-based, 0 = head-of-line) within their assignee's ordered work-list — peers shift down. Single: { id, rank }. Many: items:[{ id, rank, writer?, harness? }]. `writer`='bee' (default, a bee resequencing its own list) | 'queen' (Queen overlay). Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, … | error }], counts }.

guidance.when: You are a bee resequencing your own work-list, or the Queen injecting/rebalancing — for one item or several at once. Claim items first; rank is per-assignee.
guidance.notWhen: You only want to START an item (work_items:claim) or change its lifecycle state (work_items:set_state). Reorder changes ORDER, not ownership or state.
guidance.chaining: work_items:claim → work_items:reorder → fleet:assignments { agent } to see the ordered queue. The Queen: fleet:assignments → work_items:reorder { writer:"queen", items:[…] }.

tools.name: work_items:search
tools.description: Full-text search work-items across kinds (feature/research-task/chunk/bug/change). Matches title + body/summary. Filter by harness or kind. Use to dedup before creating.

guidance.when: You want to find existing work-items by free text (e.g. dedup before filing, or locate a known issue/feature).
guidance.chaining: work_items:search (dedup) → work_items:create, or → work_items:get { id } for detail.

tools.name: work_items:set_live_verified
tools.description: Mark a feature-family work-item LIVE-VERIFIED — an additive payload marker { at, by, deployedSha?, evidence? } that separates "done" (code on staging) from "confirmed live" (deployed + exercised). Does NOT change the lifecycle state. Confirm deployment first (release:deploy status / dev:pipeline_position), then record the deployedSha + evidence. clear:true retracts it (rollback). Read via work_items:get (payload.live_verified). Non-feature items return applicable:false.

guidance.when: A pipeline/operator work-item is done = code-on-staging, and you have now confirmed it DEPLOYED + exercised on the live host — record the deployedSha + what you exercised so "shipped" vs "live" is no longer ambiguous.
guidance.notWhen: Not for the lifecycle state (work_items:set_state) — this is an additive live-confirmation marker, not a state. Issue-family items return applicable:false.
guidance.chaining: release:deploy { op:"status" } / dev:pipeline_position (confirm the deployed SHA) → work_items:set_live_verified { id, deployedSha, evidence }. clear:true to retract on rollback. work_items:get shows payload.live_verified.

tools.name: work_items:set_priority
tools.description: The Queen's steer-don't-dispatch lever: set one OR many work-items' BACKLOG priority — the order the decentralized claim layer pulls against (lower = claimed sooner). Single: { workItem, priority?|position? }. Many: items:[{ workItem, priority?, position?, harness?, decision? }]. Each item: set an explicit { priority } integer, bump to { position:'top'|'bottom' }, clear with { priority:null }, or read with just { workItem }. Distinct from work_items:reorder (one bee's already-claimed work-list). Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, workItem, mode, … | error }], counts } — correlate by workItem.

guidance.when: You are the Queen steering the SHARED backlog (read curation:change-feed + work_items:list): promote/demote what the fleet claims next — position:'top'/'bottom' for most/least urgent, or an explicit integer; reprioritize several at once via items:[…]. In a multi-Swarm Hive only the steering-lease holder commits; a non-holder's set returns proposed:true (recorded for the holding Queen to dispose; local placement is unaffected).
guidance.notWhen: Ranking a single bee's already-claimed work-list (work_items:reorder — per-assignee), pinning work to a Swarm (work_items:co_locate), or changing lifecycle state (work_items:set_state). GLOBAL backlog order, feature-family only.
guidance.chaining: curation:change-feed (what shipped / where momentum is) + work_items:list (the backlog) → work_items:set_priority { workItem, position:'top' } → the next claim_next pulls it first.

tools.name: work_items:set_redundancy
tools.description: Mark a high-stakes work-item for BOINC redundancy: run it independently on N Swarms then judge + adopt the best (reuse gym:judge). Pass { id, redundancy: N≥2 } to opt in, or { redundancy: 1 } to clear (back to exactly-once). Opt-in, off by default — inert until PAPERCUSP_WORKITEM_REDUNDANCY=1.

guidance.when: A work-item is high-stakes enough to be worth running redundantly (the cost of a wrong result exceeds the cost of a second independent run + a judge). Set redundancy: 2 to fan it out to two Swarms; a judge picks the winner.
guidance.notWhen: Routine work — redundancy doubles the cost. Issue-family items (bugs/changes) — only feature-family pipeline items carry redundancy. Pinning which Swarm runs it — that is work_items:co_locate.
guidance.chaining: work_items:set_redundancy { id, redundancy: 2 } → work_items:claim_replica (each Swarm) → work_items:record_replica_result → work_items:judge_redundancy (adopt the winner).

tools.name: work_items:set_state
tools.description: Set the lifecycle state of one OR many work-items. feature-family: a feature status (todo|in_progress|passed|failing|deprecated…). issue-family: open|resolved|closed. Single: { id, state }. Many same state: { ids:[…], state }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ id, state, harness?, decision? }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, workItem? | error }], counts } — correlate by id; a not-found item never fails the rest.

guidance.when: You moved one or more work-items along the lifecycle (started, resolved, etc.). Flip a whole wave at once via { ids:[…], state } or items:[…].
guidance.chaining: work_items:claim → … → work_items:set_state { state }.

tools.name: work_items:subscribe
tools.description: Subscribe to one OR many work-items so their updates fan out to your inbox — pass `id` for one or `ids` for several (shared `mode`: full | digest | mention). Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, error? }], counts }.

guidance.when: You want to follow one or more work-items you do not own (e.g. ones that block yours). Subscribe to several at once via `ids`.
guidance.chaining: work_items:get → work_items:subscribe.

tools.name: work_items:tag
tools.description: Tag one OR many work-items with a topic (or untag with remove:true) — routes the item to that topic's subscribers. Single: { id, topic }. Many same topic: { ids:[…], topic }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ id, topic, harness?, remove? }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, topic? | error }], counts } — correlate by id; a not-found item never fails the rest.

guidance.when: You want a work-item visible to agents following an area (topics:list to see topics). Tag several at once via ids:[…]+topic or items:[…].
guidance.chaining: topics:list → work_items:tag { topic } (or { ids, topic }).
